# 73 — Uganda: 5.18.104, the sales follow-up — report, quote chase, daily list, voice notes, offers and the agent's copy (design, 4 Nov 2026)

Status: **design APPROVED by the owner on 5 Nov 2026, with every question's default (§Q); built and tested (§S):
`release/5.18.104` = `994d660`, pushed 7 Nov on the owner's word; `scripts/deploy-5.18.104.sh` rehearsed; DEPLOYED 9 Nov
(copy 03:50:25 UTC; PASSED 231 ok, 0 failed, 57 notes; root `docs/07`), every switch OFF.**
5.18.104 is installed with every switch off; no step has been turned on. The owner's decisions are root `docs/72` §B (D8–D16) and the wording they approved is `docs/72` §H.1; this
document continues `docs/72` §H. Its base is the live release 5.18.103 (`release/5.18.103` = `221c9dc`), switched on
4 Nov (root `docs/07`).

## A. What 5.18.104 does, in plain words

- **P1 — a read-only sales report.** A tool, run by hand, that reads a copy of the book and changes nothing.
- **P2 — every quotation is tracked and chased** on day 1, 3 and 7 with the approved wording (D9). The chase stops when
  the customer writes, a colleague takes over, the customer says STOP, or the quotation is accepted or expires.
- **P3 — a morning list for each salesperson** on WhatsApp: quote numbers and counts only (D13). Customer names are on a
  staff page in the plugin, each salesperson's own leads only.
- **P4 — voice notes heard through OpenAI** (D2, D14), climbed in four rungs, each with its own check: measure only →
  transcribe without acting → staff see the transcript → the AI answers in text.
- **P5 — an instant reply to a voice note**, every day 07:00–21:00 (D15), until the AI hears them.
- **P6 — offers on the Evolution numbers** (D11): a daily batch to customers who chatted in the last 30 days, from the
  number they chatted on, with varied wording, STOP on each and an optional image; 100, 200 or all, "all" spread over
  days; preview, a test to the admin's own phone, then start, pause and stop.
- **P7 — the agent's copy** (D16): the agent who made a quotation gets a visible Cc of the quotation e-mail, in the same
  e-mail, only when the plugin sends it.
- **One daily limit per WhatsApp number**: at most 60 automatic messages a day (D12), counted in one shared ledger;
  chases come first and offers use what is left; replies to customers are not counted.
- **Everything ships OFF.** One tool switches the parts on in one order, each step only after the step before it has
  passed its check (D4); one rollback switches everything off in one sequence. **Uganda only; South Sudan unchanged**,
  and the tests prove it. WhatsApp stays on Evolution until the official number exists (D10).

## B. How to read it

- The design is written in four parts, each meant to be built from:
  - **Part F** (§H.2): P1–P3, and the pieces every part shares — the send ledger, "a person took over", the switch tool
    and its one ladder of steps, the deploy checks and the rollback;
  - **Part V** (§H.3): P4 and P5;
  - **Part O** (§H.4): P6;
  - **Part P** (§H.5): P7.
- §H.2.21, at the end of Part F, is an appendix: the report's first-round text, which §H.2.8 keeps (P1).
- §C is the contract every part was written to, and §R the coordinator's rulings R1–R19, which amend it. **Where a
  part and a ruling disagree, the ruling is right.**
- A bare `path:line` is under `dishnet-hybrid-sudan/` on `release/5.18.103` (`221c9dc`); `dev:` is the development
  branch; `web:` is `dishnet-web-uganda/`; `docs/NN` is a root document.
- Each part's decisions, tests and deploy checks carry its own prefixes (for example QF-, VN-, OF-, AC-). Review ids
  (K2-, S2-, X-, Y-, Z-, and Q15- to Q20- for the focused rounds) record where a choice came from; §H.2.19 records
  each review round.
- Nothing has run. Every "proved" in this document names a test to be written, with a weakened copy that must fail it.
- **Review status.** The four parts were checked against the live release in 14 review sweeps. The coordinator then
  made rulings R18 (a check judges each act only by what its maker could know) and R19 (a sender re-tests every
  switch on a fresh read just before it claims), and seven focused rounds (15–21) fixed what each audit found and
  audited every change. The last check, on round 21's changes, found no blocker or major item. Each part's own
  findings table or list records every round. The build's tests and the rehearsal are the next evidence.

## Q. The questions for the owner, merged from the four parts

Each has a default that ships if it is not answered; only Q1 holds part of the build back, and even it has a fallback.

**Answered 5 Nov 2026:** the owner approved the design and took every default ("go with your recommendation"). So
Q1's fallback applies until the owner confirms the words: on a salesperson's number the day-3 chase and the
voice-note reply are held and day 7 uses B; a later confirmation is one command.

**Before the build**
- **Q1 — the assistant wording on a salesperson's own number** (Part F OQ1, gate B-1). Confirm the exact words of the
  composed messages: chase day 3 (A and B) and day 7 (A), and the two voice-note replies, each opening *"Hello, this is
  {first name}'s assistant at DishNet."*; and that day 1 (A and B) and day 7 (B) are D9's rule applied word for word.
  Unanswered: on a salesperson's number the day-3 chase is held, day 7 uses B, and the voice-note reply is held; a later
  answer is one command.

**When messages go out**
- **Q2 — payment reminders first** (Part F OQ2; Part O asks the same). On a reminder day, chases and offers wait until
  the reminder job has run (normally soon after 09:00, at the latest 17:00), so nobody gets a chase or an offer and a
  payment reminder the same day. The alternative keeps 08:00 starts and accepts that someone may get both.
- **Q3 — day 7** (Part F OQ5). The day-7 message goes at 16:00 on the last open day on or before the 7th day, so it
  arrives while the quotation is valid, and is skipped if that is within 96 hours of a late day-3 message. Confirm.
- **Q4 — the cold chase** (Part F OQ6, step 10). Before it is switched on, say whether support's assistant stays on.

**People and the AI**
- **Q5 — a colleague's media** (Part F OQ3, Part V §H.3.28, Part O §H.4.21). When a colleague answers from the phone
  with a voice note, photo or document without a caption, the chase and the voice-note reply stop, but the AI keeps
  answering, as today. Should the AI stand down too, as its own later switch?
- **Q6 — no STOP line on the voice-note reply** (Part V §H.3.15). The approved text has none, because it answers the
  customer's own message. Confirm.

**Privacy and keys**
- **Q7 — the Privacy Policy paragraph naming OpenAI** (Part V §H.3.23, D14). Approve its words; voice notes go to OpenAI
  only after it is published.
- **Q8 — how long things are kept, and erasing one person** (Part F OQ4, Part V §H.3.21). The send ledger and the marks
  are kept 400 days, the quote tracker indefinitely, and transcripts like typed text under the Policy's periods. Should
  the Policy say so, and is a per-person erase of the conversation history wanted (no tool does it today)?
- **Q9 — keys on the settings page** (Part V §H.3.18, §H.3.22). 5.18.104 stops printing the OpenAI key on Uganda's page.
  Should the Anthropic key be hidden too, and South Sudan's page treated the same? If OpenAI allows a key limited to
  audio, should one be made for this use? (After a rollback, the script tells you to rotate the key if any audio ever
  went to OpenAI, because 5.18.103's page prints it.)

**Voice**
- **Q10 — Whisper's successor** (Part V §H.3.22). D2 says Whisper (`whisper-1`); its removal is reported for 26 Feb
  2027. Choose the successor before then; it is a setting, not a code change.
- **Q11 — the voice limits** (Part V §H.3.5). Defaults: a note up to 2 minutes, 120 minutes a day in all, 10 notes per
  conversation a day; replies at most 25 per number a day, 20 seconds apart, one per conversation per 24 hours,
  07:00–21:00. Confirm or change.

**Offers**
- **Q12 — the pilot limits** (Part O O-D13, §H.4.6). At most 20 offers per number a day (inside the 60), no second offer
  to the same person within 7 days, an automatic pause when STOP reaches 5 % once 40 have gone, and an offer ends 14
  days after Start. Confirm or change.
- **Q13 — voice-note senders** (Part O §H.4.21). A customer who sent a voice note in the last 30 days is left out of
  offers, because offers cannot hear it. Relax that once the AI hears voice notes?
- **Later — the official number** (Part O §H.4.11, D10). When it exists, offers leave from it; decided then.

**The agent's copy (P7)**
- **Q14 — administrators** (Part P PQ1). An administrator who makes a quotation gets the copy; `set agent-cc-admins 0`
  stops that.
- **Q15 — KYC quotations** (PQ2). The copy goes to the salesperson the KYC names when exactly one active account has
  that name, otherwise to the account that submitted it — the daily list's rule. Confirm, or "always the submitter".
- **Q16 — dealer accounts and "Login As"** (PQ3). Retailers and field agents who make quotations get the copy too. And a
  quotation made while an administrator acts as another account: copy that account, or none?
- **Q17 — the address the customer sees** (PQ4). The Cc is visible, so check every selling account's address is one to
  show customers; `on agent-cc` prints the counts. Should an account whose address is the company's own mailbox get no
  copy?
- **Q18 — the double e-mails already live** (PQ5, OB1 and OB2). P7 neither causes nor fixes them. Review them in a later
  release?

## C. The shared contract (set by the coordinator, 4 Nov 2026; binding on every part)

Parts: P1 report · P2 quote tracking and chase (day 1/3/7) · P3 daily list · P4 voice notes through OpenAI ·
P5 interim voice-note acknowledgement · P6 offers on Evolution (D11). Base: release/5.18.103 = 221c9dc.

C1 Switches. Every 5.18.104 switch lives in ONE new tool, `tools/sales_followup.php` (show / on / off / --check),
   Uganda only. `tools/set_config.php` stays byte for byte (pinned by tests I3 and CD_I_KEPT). The tool enforces ONE
   switch-on order across all parts (C6); a switch refuses to turn on while an earlier step is off. Offers also have an
   admin screen (compose, audience, size, preview, test, start/pause/stop) that exists only while the offers switch is on.

C2 Migrations. 089 = quote follow-up AND the shared ledger (C3); 090 = voice media; 091 = offers. Each migration verifies
   itself; trigger bodies avoid CASE…END and any word ending in "end" (MigrationRunner splitter, :118-121).

C3 One ledger, one budget per HANDSET (the Evolution instance — support and account share one handset; never the
   channel id). Table `wa_auto_sends` in 089; primitive `lib/WaSendBudget.php`:
   - `claim(handset, kind, ref)` → ok | defer(reason, retry_at); `settle(claim, sent|failed)`; idempotent per (kind, ref).
   - kind CHECK: quote, enquiry, staff_list, offer, reminder, winback, brief, voice_ack, handover_alert, other.
   - PROACTIVE kinds (quote, enquiry, staff_list, offer, reminder, winback, brief) count against the caps and the
     spacing. REPLY/INTERNAL kinds (voice_ack, handover_alert) are recorded, never deferred by the proactive caps,
     but voice_ack has its own ceiling and resets nothing; a proactive send still keeps its spacing after any send.
   - Existing automated senders that 5.18.104 does not otherwise change (the 09:00 reminders and win-back, staff
     briefs, hand-over alerts) get RECORD-ONLY hooks at their send points: counted, never deferred.
   - Defaults (settings in the tool; the owner may change them): proactive per handset per Kampala day 60; per hour 15;
     random spacing 60–180 s between proactive sends on a handset; 08:00–20:00 Kampala, never Sunday, for proactive
     kinds. Priority when the day's budget is short: quote > staff_list > enquiry > reminder/winback/brief > offer; the
     offer sender uses only what remains after reserving the chases due that day.

C4 Rollback clears every 5.18.104 switch; a redeploy starts dark and each part is switched on again with its check.

C5 cron/master.php: one coordinated change; new jobs quote_chase (600 s), quote_daily_list (window 08–11), ai_media
   (voice), offers_send (300 s); each Uganda-gated with the shared `'uganda' => true` key; the combined worst-case
   cycle is added up and stays inside master's 300 s budget (F2), stating each job's placement.

C6 The one switch-on order (D4), each step with its own check:
   1 P1 report (a tool; no switch) · 2 P5 voice acknowledgement · 3 Q1 quote tracking (records, sends nothing) ·
   4 Q2 the daily list · 5 R1 voice measure (counts voice notes and whether media can be fetched; sends nothing) ·
   6 Q3/Q4 chases from warm numbers · 7 R2 voice dry run (transcribes, says nothing) · 8 R3 transcript to staff ·
   9 R4 the AI answers from the transcript (P5 goes silent for that number) · 10 Q5 cold chase (optional, last of P2) ·
   11 O1 offers: test to the admin's own number only · 12 O2 offers live.

C7 "A person took over" means a fromMe message on that conversation NOT sent by the plugin's own automation (known by
   the ledger and the echo claims), or a hand-over state set AFTER the quote's send (time-bounded); never
   humanRepliedSince's plain reading, which counts the engine's own 'DishNet' rows as a colleague.

C8 Staff-facing WhatsApp texts (the daily list) carry quote numbers and counts only — AlertService writes every body to
   the Message Log; customer names appear only on a staff page in the plugin, under the own-leads-only rule.

C9 Unchanged: South Sudan (proved by tests and deploy checks), Domain B, every existing switch, webhook.php's quote
   send unless a part must change it (then say exactly why), uCRM (GETs only from new code, except what P2 already
   reads). The OpenAI key is never echoed into any page, log or error — the admin page shows only "set"/"not set".

C10 Owner defaults pending the owner's answers (settings, not code): caps as C3; the daily list's WhatsApp text quote
   numbers only; the Privacy Policy line names OpenAI; the voice acknowledgement every day 07:00–21:00 (a reply, not
   proactive); office-registered KYC quotes go to the office account's list (F4 limit, accepted for 5.18.104); partner
   numbers never chase or send offers; the cold chase is its own last switch; forwarded audio is treated as a voice note.

## R. The coordinator's rulings (4 Nov 2026; binding; they amend the contract)

These settle every cross-part item in `r2/find.json` (X-01…X-35 by interface, Y-01…Y-36 by identifier). Where a ruling
names a part, that part's text changes; every other part's text is re-pointed to the same words. A ruling here
overrides the folded parts and the earlier contract wording where they differ.

### R1 cron/master.php (X-01, Y-01, X-29, Y-28, X-02, Y-16) — amendment A-C5-1
- The four new lines, last in `$_m_jobs`, in this order and with this key order, byte for byte:
  `'quote_chase'      => ['interval' => 540, 'uganda' => true, 'flag' => 'quote_tracking_enabled',   'script' => __DIR__ . '/quote_chase.php'],`
  `'quote_daily_list' => ['interval' => 240, 'uganda' => true, 'flag' => 'quote_daily_list_enabled', 'script' => __DIR__ . '/quote_daily_list.php'],`
  `'ai_media'         => ['interval' => 60,  'uganda' => true, 'flag' => 'ai_media_enabled',         'script' => dirname(__DIR__) . '/run_media_worker.php'],`
  `'offers_send'      => ['interval' => 240, 'uganda' => true, 'flag' => 'offers_live_enabled',      'script' => __DIR__ . '/offers_send.php'],`
- Offers go LAST: lowest priority (C3) and the only ban-risk sends; ai_media serves customers already waiting. Every
  new job bounds itself by `$_m_deadline`. Intervals 540/240 are the written values that give C5's 600 s and 300 s
  periods on the ~300 s heartbeat (cron/master.php:298-301) — amendment A-C5-1.
- Cycle sum from each part's final bound: quote_chase 25 s, quote_daily_list 21 s, ai_media ≤ 60 s (starts a note only
  with ≥ 55 s left), offers_send ≤ 55 s (35 s plus one send at O's 15 s client timeout) = 161 s.
- `tools/cron_status.php` on Uganda lists a flagged job whose flag is off as `OFF (switch)`; on South Sudan it never
  lists the four. One guard (F's MS8); V's VN-CA2/V9 become reads of it. O's P-O1-6, OF-CA2, test I and §H.4.17, V's
  §H.3.19 and test_cron_keepalive_order, and F's MS tests all read these exact lines.

### R2 The ledger call contract (F §H.2.5.8 is the one table) (X-03, Y-06, X-04, Y-07, X-17, X-20, Y-24, X-21, Y-29, X-23, X-24, Y-25, X-25, X-26)
- Offer ref is stable per recipient: `offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>` — never per attempt. The ledger's own try count
  counts attempts. O keeps its `attempt` column for its own row CAS only; C-O2-4 and O's test F map by the two-part ref.
- A may-have-been-sent result is `settle($c, 'failed', ['maybe_sent' => true, 'wa_message_id' => <id when returned>])`
  → stored `uncertain`, counted, never retried — for every caller, O's step 9, stale sweep and off-hook included. O's
  OM31 is inverted (settling `sent` is the weakened copy), matching V's A29 and F's LG29.
- `claim()` refuses quote, enquiry and offer without a phone: `no_phone`, final. NO table CHECK on the phone (erase sets
  it NULL; a reminder `record()` with an unreadable number must still be recorded).
- The ledger normalises the phone itself: `PhoneNumber::international` without '+', NULL on failure — every kind,
  claim and record alike — so the one-proactive-per-person-per-day comparison holds across senders.
- `retry_at` is an int unix time, null when final.
- `record()` never throws and returns a fixed code: `recorded | ledger_off | not_uganda | no_table | error`; the
  existing record-only hooks ignore it. The table gains the row `other | Part O's test send | offer_test:<test id> |
  record | no`.
- `WaSendBudget::forInstall` derives the handset itself (`handset(EvolutionApiService::forStore(...)->instanceFor($ch))`);
  a callable is accepted for tests only.
- Callers map by CODE, from one table written from each caller's code:
  - voice_ack: V's mapping table is binding (F replaces its Part V column with it). V's defers write no decision row;
    staleness is measured from `received_at` (600 s rule).
  - offer: `already_sent` → recipient `uncertain('ledger_already_sent')`, never re-sent; `tries_exhausted`,
    `not_claimable`, `no_phone` → recipient `skipped(<code>)`; `in_flight` and every defer carrying `retry_at` → release
    the recipient to `retry_at`; `phone_today` → next Kampala day; `ledger_error` and any unknown code → end the run
    (fail closed).

### R3 Functions Part O relies on — Part F defines them (X-05, Y-02, X-06, Y-03, X-19, X-07, Y-04)
- F adds to `lib/QuoteChase.php` (its file list, its API section and a real F test section — not "D/K"):
  `QuoteChase::offerHolds(\PDO $pdo, string $nowUtc): array` (international digits ⇒ reason) and
  `QuoteChase::offerHold(\PDO $pdo, string $phone, string $nowUtc): string` ('' = none). Read-only SQL: an open tracked
  quotation, an open quote follow-up, or a quote send `sent`/`uncertain` within 48 h, on any conversation of the phone,
  over `quote_tracker`, `followups` (kind quote) and `followup_sends`; the past-moment form for `--check offers-live`
  taken from `status_at`, `closed_at` and `sent_at`.
- F adds to `lib/HumanTakeover.php`: `phoneSince(\PDO $pdo, string $phone, string $sinceUtc, ?string $untilUtc = null):
  ?string` and `phonesSince(\PDO $pdo, string $sinceUtc, ?string $untilUtc = null): array` (phone ⇒ code), built from
  exactly `since()`'s clauses over every conversation of the phone except `category='staff'`, the upper bound applied
  to every clause. Null = none. O's extra `human_active`/`last_human_reply_at` clause is DROPPED (every live writer of
  `human_active` stores a person's row in the same request — evo_webhook.php:197-221, includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:249-257);
  O's test K builds its fixtures through those real writers and proves parity on one fixture.
- `since()`, `phoneSince()` and `phonesSince()` normalise every time argument with
  `UtcClock::stamp(UtcClock::parse($s))` (lib/UtcClock.php:31-45); an unreadable stamp returns a code (sends less).
- `VoiceStopMarks` does not exist and is not built. Drop it as an O precondition and read; remove `partv_missing`.
  Instead O excludes any phone with an inbound `media_type='audio'` row within `offers_warm_days` (the 72 h hold widens
  to the warm window) and keeps the any-source `contact_optouts` read (which includes V's `voice_keyword` rows). Whether
  to relax this once the AI hears voice notes is an owner question.

### R5 One key and settings vocabulary in `SalesFollowupLadder` (X-11, Y-08, X-12, X-13, X-22, Y-05, X-32, Y-15, X-34, Y-32)
- Persona confirmation: `sf_persona_confirmed`, written by `set persona-confirmed <date>`, read by F and V (V's

### R6 Admission (the order of switch-on) (X-14, Y-13, X-15, Y-14, X-35, Y-20)
- The ladder engine owns ORDER (every earlier step on, recorded skipped, or optional; no earlier step left running at
  FAIL). Each row lists only its hard Needs. V drops "steps 2–N on".
- Voice chain: the needs 5 → 7 → 8 → 9 carry a `pass_only` flag: the needed check must read PASS; `--accept-not-yet`
  and a skip do not satisfy them. A voice step may still be recorded skipped (with `--reason`), which satisfies ORDER
  for later non-voice steps only.
- Step 11's Needs: the ledger on (`wa_send_ledger=on`, from step 2 or `skip ack`) with L-ON at PASS; step 3 on with
  Q1-ON at PASS or an accepted `NOT_YET no_traffic`. `skip tracking` cascades to 11 and 12. O's "steps 2 and 3 at PASS"
  and "every other earlier step at PASS" are removed.
- Step 2's row writes `wa_send_ledger=on`, `wa_send_ledger_since` and P5's keys. `off ack` clears P5's keys only and
  never the ledger; only `off sending` or `off all` (last) clear the ledger.
- Check vocabulary everywhere: `PASS`, `FAIL <code>`, `NOT_YET too_soon|no_traffic|no_test`.

### R7 Rollback and off-hooks (X-16, Y-17, Y-19, Y-30, X-31, Y-31)
- One explicit sequence in `SalesFollowupLadder`: O (12, 11) → F (10, 6) → V (9, 8, 7, 5) → 4, 3 → 2 (P5's keys, then
  the ledger last) → the record keys. F's "steps 12 → 2" and O's "reverse ladder order" are reworded to it.
- O's hook runs BEFORE its keys clear (takes the sender lock, pauses every running offer, settles claimed rows
  `uncertain`), in both a plain `off` and a rollback.
- V's work splits by step: step 5's hook runs AFTER V's media keys clear — settle `pending` audio rows
  `skipped/switched_off` (nothing in flight touched) and drain `ai.media` turns (bounded, `ai_enabled` as found); step
  2's hook runs AFTER P5's keys clear and BEFORE the ledger clears — drain acknowledgement events (so they record
  `switched_off`), then count. QF-RB1's V group asserts the end state: 0 pending audio rows and V's keys unset; VN-RB6's
  rotate-the-key instruction prints whenever any `wa_voice_calls` row exists. F's citation of the event count is
  VN-RB4; VN-RB2 is the drain.
- QF-G4 is the ONE stage-A rule, run with the pin's tool and every hook; O's OF-G1 and V's VN-G1 only read its result
  (O's installed-ladder and raw-override branches removed). F replaces "O1-ON"/"O2-ON" with O's real check names.
- `ai.media` events: V's rule is "before switch-on against `ai_media_since`" (re-stamped by `on voice-measure`); there is

### R12 Ruling R7's off-hook, read precisely (recheck Z-08)
- O's hook settles `uncertain` (settle `failed` with `maybe_sent`) every claimed recipient that holds a ledger claim.
  A claimed recipient with no `ledger_claim` never reached the gateway and returns to `queued`. If a ledger row exists
  for its stable ref `offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>` anyway, a re-claim answers `already_sent`, so nothing is sent
  twice. This is ruling R7's reading; F §H.2.16 item 1 and O §H.4.6 cite it as ruling R12.

### R13 The ladder's call surface: two connections and one table of callables (recheck-7 Z-01…Z-05, Z-08)
- Two connections, both opened by `tools/sales_followup.php` and by nothing it calls:
  - `$ro`, the read-only check connection (Part F §H.2.12.1): `PRAGMA query_only=ON`, never `SqliteStore::create`,
    `total_changes()==0` asserted on it at the tool's end. Every check, own-precondition read and after-`on`/after-`off`
    read-back reads the book through `$ro` alone; so do `show`, `doctor` and the baseline preview that
    `on offers-test` prints (`OfferAudience::build()` is given `$ro` there).
  - `$rw`, the one writable connection, opened only by a command that writes (`on`, `off`, `skip`, `set`, `erase`), and
    only when `<data>/plugin.sqlite3` already exists; otherwise the command refuses and saves nothing, as
    `PluginConfig::mirrorToStore` declines to create a store (`lib/PluginConfig.php:373`). It is
    `SqliteStore::create($dataDir)->getPdo()` (`lib/SqliteStore.php:140-265`, `:277`): `busy_timeout` 5000 first
    (`:158`), and its migration run (`:247`) is the one every tool, and `saveOverrides` itself
    (`lib/PluginConfig.php:379`), already makes. `erase` and every off-hook write through `$rw` and nothing else.
    Keys are still written only through `PluginConfig::saveOverrides`.
- Every callable the ladder dispatches to is in this table, with exactly this signature (all `public static`):

| Part | Holder (file) | Precondition | Check | Off-hook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F | `SalesFollowupChecks` (`lib/SalesFollowupChecks.php`, new, Part F's) | `preconditions(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step): array`: rows 1, 2 (Part F's half: the two `_schema_checks` rows and `dn_tz()`), 6, 10 | `check(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $id, int $now): array`, `$id` one of `L-ON`, `Q1-ON`, `Q2-ON`, `Q3-ON`, `Q5-ON` | `QuoteChase::offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array`: row 6, its rollback form only |
| V | `VoiceSteps` (`lib/VoiceSteps.php`, new, Part V's) | `preconditions(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step): array`: rows 2 (Part V's half: `ai_enabled`, `VoiceAckLimits::of()` not null), 5, 7, 9 | `check(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $id, int $now): array`, `$id` one of `VA-ON1`, `VN-ON1`…`VN-ON4` | `offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array`: rows 2 and 5 |
| O | `OfferSwitch` (`lib/OfferSwitch.php`) | `preconditions(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step): array`: rows 11, 12 | `checkTest(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, int $now): array` and `checkLive(` the same `): array` | `offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array`: rows 11 and 12 |
| P | `QuoteAgentCopy` (`lib/QuoteAgentCopy.php`) | `mailSetting(string $dataDir): array` (reads a file, never the book) | `check(\PDO $ro, string $pluginRoot, string $dataDir, int $now): array` (Part P §H.5.7, unchanged) | none (ruling R11) |

- Part P's `state(string $pluginRoot, string $dataDir)` and its pure `accountCounts(array $retailers, array $company)`
  keep their signatures: the tool reads the `retailers.json` row through `$ro` and passes the rows.
- Arguments: `$config` is the configuration the tool reads at the moment of the call, re-read after any key it has just
  cleared; `$dataDir` is `cliDataDir`'s; `$now` is one `time()` taken at the tool's start; `$step` is the row's step
  name; `$why` is `switch` or `rollback`. A hook that takes a lock (Part O's sender lock) finds it under `$dataDir`.
- Returns: a check returns `array{status:string, counts:array<string,int>, notes:list<string>}`, with `status` exactly
  `PASS`, `FAIL <code>` or `NOT_YET too_soon|no_traffic|no_test` (ruling R6): Part P's shape (its §H.5.7). A
  precondition returns `array{ok:bool, code:?string, lines:list<string>}`. A hook returns its counts,
  `array<string,int>`, and throws on failure; what the ladder then does is Part F's (§H.2.12.4, §H.2.16).
- No check, precondition or read-back opens the book itself or through `SqliteStore::create`. No hook opens a
  connection of its own.
- Step 2's one status is the engine's combination of `SalesFollowupChecks::check(…, 'L-ON', …)` and
  `VoiceSteps::check(…, 'VA-ON1', …)`, as Part F §H.2.12.2 defines it.
- `lib/SalesFollowupChecks.php` joins Part F's §H.2.3 list and TL14's Part F slice; `lib/VoiceSteps.php` joins Part V's
  §H.3.2 list, VK1 and TL14's Part V slice (Part F §H.2.12.4, IV-10). Part F's `TL tool` row asserts that every row
  reaches the callable named here, with `$ro` for a check, precondition or read-back and `$rw` for a hook; a weakened
  holder that opens its own connection fails it.

### R16 The `erase` match on `wa_media.remote_jid` (recheck-7 Z-03, Z-04)
- Stated once, in Part V §H.3.3, which owns the table: `erase` blanks `remote_jid` on the union of two sets, the rows

  row with `phone` equal to those digits. An `@lid` JID carries no number (the webhook takes the phone from `senderPn`,
  `evo_webhook.php:233-235`), so the second set is what reaches those rows. Part F §H.2.12.1, its §H.2.4 erasure note,

### R17 Part O's by-hand put-back (recheck-7 Z-06)
- Part O §H.4.19 writes its by-hand statements out, each on open rows only and each valid under 091's CHECKs:
  `running` offers become `paused` (`live_slot` stays 1); `claimed` recipients with a `ledger_claim` become
  `uncertain` with reason `stale_claim` and `sent_at = claimed_at`; `claimed` recipients with none go back to `queued`
  (ruling R12), with the same columns the hook writes (§H.4.6); `sending` tests older than 15 minutes become
  `uncertain`. The by-hand form writes no event row and calls no `settle()`: the ledger rows it leaves in flight are
  read by nothing in 5.18.103, and after a redeploy the next claim on that handset settles each `stale_orphan` (Part F
  §H.2.5.3 step 3a), while a recipient whose ledger row exists answers `already_sent` under its stable ref, so nothing
  is sent twice. Part F §H.2.16 cites "Part O's by-hand statements of §H.4.19 (ruling R17)" and gives no count.

### R18 A check judges each act by what its maker could know (sweep-14 A14-01…A14-04, A14-06…A14-08, B14-01)
- Every `--check` clause and every `*-ON` clause that re-judges a past act (a chase, a list, an acknowledgement, an
  offer, a copy) judges it in three ways, each read from records written when the act was decided:
  1. **At the moment the act was decided**, recorded on the act's own row at that moment: the ledger's `claimed_at`
     for a claimed send; for an offer, a new `judged_at` (UTC) on `wa_offer_recipients`, written by step 4 of the send
     together with its move/release CAS. Never a later stamp such as the gateway's return (`sent_at`).
  2. **From what the maker could have read then.** Every source is bounded by its storage time at or before that
     moment: `wa_messages.created_at`, `followups.opened_at`, `contact_optouts.created_at`, `wa_seen_marks.seen_at`,
     `events.created_at`, `quote_tracker.created_at`. Never by an inbound row's `sent_at`, which is the customer's
     device `messageTimestamp` (live `lib/ConversationService.php:1202-1217`) and can sort before a row stored later.
  3. **Under the limits it applied**, recorded on the row that records the decision, never the settings as they read
     now. `set` may narrow a setting at any time (Part F §H.2.12.7), so a check that reads today's value turns a
     correct past send into a FAIL. Every table below is new in 5.18.104, so no row lacks these values:
     - `wa_auto_sends` gains `win_from`, `win_to` (the Kampala hours `window()` or, for `voice_ack`, `ackPolicy()`
       judged the claim by), `cap_day` (the daily cap; for `voice_ack` the acknowledgement ceiling) and `cap_hour` (the
       hourly cap; NULL for `voice_ack`). All four are written by the claim, are NULL on a `record` row, and are added
       to `was_identity_fixed`. Spacing is judged by each earlier row's own `gap_s`, which already exists.
     - `wa_voice_acks` records the period and the gap its decision applied.
     - `wa_offer_recipients` records `judged_at` and the per-handset maximum the claim applied; an offer's
       `warm_days` and `recent_days` are already recorded at its start and are what C-O2-9 reads.
     Ruling R8's "a check reads the settings" means these recorded values.
- **What the maker could not have known is printed as a count, never a FAIL.** That covers rows stored after the
  moment, content not recorded with the act, and a state a legitimate person may set. In particular, an Inbox reply
  sets `human_active` and stores a row in the staff member's name, never `Team` (live
  `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:244-258`, `:1000-1015`), and its echo is claimed, so no `Team` row follows. No clause
  may treat `human_active` without a `Team` row as a fault.
- **An echo is judged by its identity:** the R-05 trap is "no `wa_messages` row stored as `Team` whose `wa_message_id`
  is the act's own sent id".
- **A clause that compares with what was sent needs it recorded when it was sent.** `quote_list_sends` records, per
  section, the listed `quote_key`s (content-free) and the section's open count. Q2-ON compares those, and its opt-out
  clause reads opt-outs created at or before the row's `created_at` and still in force. Where nothing is recorded,
  the clause is a printed note.
- **A clause that can read FAIL over a correct act is a defect**, because a FAIL can never be accepted (Part F
  §H.2.12.3) and rule 3 then refuses every later `on`. For every clause that re-judges a past act, each part's K tests
  carry a case where the act was correct and the world moved after it: a row stored later, a narrowed setting, a
  colleague's Inbox reply. Each case comes with a weakened copy that judges by the current state and is caught.
- B14-01: Part O carries Part F's fourth hold source, `quote_text_48h`, and the tracker's `created_at` bound (Part F
  §H.2.10.10, IO-5). C-O2-9 re-judges `offerHold` at the recipient's `judged_at`.

### R19 A sender re-tests every switch and mode it depends on, on the fresh read (sweep-14 A14-05)
- A worker built with its start-time `$config` may run for up to its budget plus one event (live `run_worker.php:31`,
  `:43`; `workers/WorkerBase.php:107-112`). So every switch and mode a send decision depends on is re-tested on the
  fresh read taken immediately before the claim, not only the part's own switch.
- For P5 (Part V, the acknowledgement's step 13): beside `VoiceAck::enabled`,
  `MediaPolicy::voiceMode($fresh, $dataDir, $channel) === 'reply'` gives `p4_answers` there. A VK case covers
  `on voice-reply` made while a reply worker is running, with a weakened copy that tests the stale `$config`.
- Every other sender (the chase, the list, the offer) states which fresh read it decides on; where one decides on
  start-time configuration, the same rule applies.

## H. The design, part by part

The numbering continues root `docs/72` §H, whose §H.1 holds the wording the owner approved (D9).

### H.2 Part F — the report (P1), quote tracking and chase (P2), the daily list (P3), and what every part shares: the ledger (C3), the switch tool and its one ladder (C1, C6), cron/master.php (C5) and rollback (C4)

**Status: design only, second round.** The live tree and the development tree were read with `cat`, `sed` and `grep`.
Nothing was built, run or changed, and no PHP, test or git write was run. The second review's findings (S2-xx, K2-xx)
are folded in, and so are **the coordinator's rulings R1–R10 of 4 November** on the cross-part findings X-01…X-35 and
Y-01…Y-36, its later rulings R11 (P7's place in the ladder and in the rollback) and R12 (the offers off-hook, read
precisely), its rulings R13–R17 (the ladder's call surface, step 5's drain, VK4's place, the `erase` match on
`wa_media.remote_jid` and Part O's by-hand put-back), and its rulings R18 (a check judges each act at its moment,
from what could be read then, under the limits recorded with it) and R19 (a sender re-tests every switch it
depends on, on the fresh read it decides on): where this text and a ruling differ, the ruling governs, and each
changed place names its ruling (§H.2.19 maps them). **A ruling is cited as "ruling R1" to "ruling R19"**, as Part V
cites them, so that it is never read as one of C6's voice rungs R1–R4 (steps 5, 7, 8 and 9), which alone keep the bare
labels. Where this text settles a difference between the parts, it says so, and §H.2.18 lists what Parts V and O must
match. **Part P's interface items IP-1…IP-8 (its §H.5.17), as the coordinator's merge review put them to this part
(items Z-01…Z-13), are folded in too** (§H.2.19 maps them). Two of them placed P7 in the ladder and in the rollback.
**Ruling R11 settles both:** an optional row 1b, `agent-cc`, after step 1 and before step 2 with Needs none, and its two
keys cleared with the record keys, last. It declines the proposed amendments A-C6-1 and A-R7-1, so this text states that
one form and no other.

#### H.2.1 Scope, base and conventions

- **Paths.** A bare `path:line` is under `dishnet-hybrid-sudan/` on `release/5.18.103` at `221c9dc` (5.18.103, live). `dev:` is `dishnet-hybrid-sudan/` on the development branch. `docs/NN` is in the repository root. **Line citations into `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php` are at `221c9dc`:** Part V changes that file, and its hunk (`:216-229`) comes before every line cited here, so the build re-makes them against the merged tree. **Line citations into `webhook.php` are at `221c9dc` too:** Part P changes that file (`whQuotationEmail` only, its §H.5.8.2), its hunks sit after `:278` and between `:293` and `:295`, before every line cited here (`:2527-2563`, `:2896-2927`, `:3002`, `:3057-3072`), so the build re-makes them against the merged tree as well (ruling R10). Part P's hunks in `lib/QuotationService.php` come after every line cited here (`:454`, `:503-504`, `:513`, `:516`), which therefore stand.
- **Base.** `release/5.18.104` is cut on `221c9dc`, never on the development tip. That keeps the `ucrm_catalogue` table, the `web-direct` records and `CACHE_SHAPE d103-1`. PHP 7.4 applies: no `match`, no `?->`, no union types, no named arguments.
- **This part owns:**
  - P1 (the report), P2 (quote tracking and the day 1/3/7 chase) and P3 (the daily list and the staff page);
  - migration **089**: the follow-up tables, the shared ledger, the "seen" marks and `_schema_checks`;
  - `lib/WaSendBudget.php`, its call contract (§H.2.5.8) and the record-only hooks at the existing senders (C3);
  - `lib/HumanTakeover.php`, the one "a person took over" rule (C7) with the phone-level forms Part O reads (ruling R3), and the webhook's marks — the **only** hunk in the webhook's `fromMe` branch (K2-09);
  - the offers hold, `QuoteChase::offerHolds()`/`offerHold()`: the one meaning of "a quotation is in play" that Part O reads (ruling R3);
  - `tools/sales_followup.php` and **the one ladder table for every part**, `SalesFollowupLadder::STEPS`, every part's settings included (§H.2.12.2, §H.2.12.7; C1, C6, ruling R5);
  - the one change to `cron/master.php`, all four job lines as ruling R1 writes them (C5);
  - **the one rollback sequence** (§H.2.16; C4, ruling R7).
- **What it gives the other parts, and what they must match:** §H.2.18.
- **Where the contract changes Part F's first-round draft** (not published; its report text is kept in §H.2.21):
  - **Switches.** One tool, one order (C6's 12 steps, and Part P's optional row 1b, `agent-cc`, after step 1 and before step 2; ruling R11), every part's keys, with a recorded `skip` (K2-13).
  - **Gating.** The shared `'uganda' => true` key plus `StaffJobsGate`. The draft's new `NotifyGate::QUOTE_FOLLOWUP` is dropped, and `lib/NotifyGate.php` stays byte for byte.
  - **The ledger.** One table and one primitive for ten kinds. The defaults are 60 a day, 15 an hour and 60–180 s between sends (D12; the draft had 10, 4 and 90–180).
  - **Recording.** The existing senders record their sends.
  - **Two messages to one person.** Guarded per phone per Kampala day, in both directions (R-06, S2-08).
  - **The daily list.** The WhatsApp text carries quote numbers and counts only, with no staff names either. Customer names appear on a new staff page (D13).
  - **Rollback.** It clears every switch, through every part's off-hook, in one sequence.
  - **Job intervals.** Written with the heartbeat margin (R104-12, K2-01).
- **Where this text settles a difference between the parts** (second review; binding on Parts V and O through §H.2.18; the coordinator merges):
