#### H.2.4 Migration `089_quote_followups.sql`

The migration is additive and dark: no `UPDATE`, no `DELETE`, no backfill. It runs on every install, and only Uganda's gated code writes a row.

**The runner's hazards** (`lib/MigrationRunner.php`):
- it marks every file applied, whatever happened (`:243-247`);
- it swallows `already exists`, `duplicate column`, `UNIQUE constraint`, `NOT NULL constraint`, `no such column` only in a statement containing CREATE, and **`no such table` only in one containing INDEX** (`lib/MigrationRunner.php:226-233`). Each test is a case-insensitive `stripos`, on the error and on the statement as split, so CREATE and INDEX count wherever their letters stand (`created_at` contains CREATE). **Measured (ruling R9): `splitStatements()` strips comments first** (`:94`), so the swallow test reads each statement without its comments, and a comment never changes what is swallowed;
- its trigger splitter matches the three letters e-n-d with no left word boundary (`:118-121`).

So:
- every trigger body is exactly `SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '…');`, whose text is a string and is skipped (`:104-112`); no `CASE` and no word ending in those letters appears outside a string;
- the self-check INSERT, as split, contains neither INDEX nor CREATE in any case (it counts indexes with `type NOT IN ('table','trigger','view')`, never `type = 'index'`), so a failure there (a missing `_schema_checks`, an SQLite without `pragma_table_info`, a CHECK) is logged PARTIAL instead of swallowed (S2-18). That is proved per error class on the INSERT as split (MG4 here; Part V's V39 and Part O's OM82 for 090 and 091), not by a word ban (ruling R9);
- each file verifies itself with its last statement (C2), and **every check reads the `_schema_checks` row, never the log line alone** (S2-18).

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _schema_checks (
  migration  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  expected   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  found      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  checked_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  CHECK (found = expected));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quote_tracker (
  quote_key       TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- 'ref:' || the number exactly as the customer's text shows it
  quote_ref       TEXT NOT NULL,
  quote_id        INTEGER,                             -- uCRM quote id when the number maps to one
  crm_client_id   INTEGER,
  phone           TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- digits, international; 'erased' after an erase (A20)
  evidence_msg_id INTEGER NOT NULL,                    -- wa_messages.id of the earliest confirming row
  evidence_event  TEXT NOT NULL,
  made_by         TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- kyc | lead | manual | ucrm | resend | lte
  sent_at         TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- UTC
  sent_conv_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  sent_channel    TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- the Evolution channel it left from: support | account
  valid_until     TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- Kampala date
  owner_staff_id  INTEGER,
  owner_source    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
  spoke_conv_id   INTEGER, spoke_channel TEXT,
  backfilled      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
  status_at       TEXT, status_reason TEXT,            -- a fixed code, e.g. unread_inbound
  chase_hold      TEXT,                                -- why no automatic chase; NULL = none
  followup_id     INTEGER,
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  CHECK (status IN ('open','answered','opted_out','taken','paid','registered','accepted','declined',
                    'superseded','expired','colleague')),
  CHECK (backfilled IN (0,1)));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_qt_quote_id ON quote_tracker(quote_id) WHERE quote_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_qt_open  ON quote_tracker(status, sent_at) WHERE status = 'open';
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_qt_phone ON quote_tracker(phone, sent_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_qt_owner ON quote_tracker(owner_staff_id, status);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS qt_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON quote_tracker
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'quote_tracker: a tracked quotation is history and is never deleted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS qt_status_once BEFORE UPDATE OF status ON quote_tracker WHEN OLD.status <> 'open'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'quote_tracker: a quotation leaves open once'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS qt_identity_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF quote_key, sent_at, evidence_msg_id ON quote_tracker
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'quote_tracker: what was sent and when is fixed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS qt_phone_erase_only BEFORE UPDATE OF phone ON quote_tracker WHEN NEW.phone <> 'erased'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'quote_tracker: a phone is fixed and may only be erased'); END;

ALTER TABLE followups ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'enquiry';
ALTER TABLE followups ADD COLUMN quote_key TEXT;
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_fu_quote ON followups(quote_key) WHERE quote_key IS NOT NULL;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_auto_sends (             -- THE LEDGER (C3): every automated send per handset
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  handset       TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- 'i:' || lower(trim(Evolution instance)); never a channel id
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL,
  ref           TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- the sender's reference: (kind, ref) is one message
  try           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  mode          TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- claim: asked before the send | record: written after it
  proactive     INTEGER NOT NULL,                      -- 1: counts against the daily and hourly caps
  phone         TEXT,                                  -- customer kinds only: international digits, no '+', normalised by the ledger; NULL when unreadable or erased
  local_day     TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- Africa/Kampala date of the claim
  gap_s         INTEGER NOT NULL,                      -- what a proactive send must wait after this row
  claimed_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  outcome       TEXT,                                  -- NULL in flight | sent | uncertain | not_sent
  settled_at    TEXT,
  wa_message_id TEXT,                                  -- our own automation (C7)
  detail        TEXT,                                  -- a fixed code, never message text
  win_from      INTEGER,                               -- claim: the opening hour judged by (ruling R18)
  win_to        INTEGER,                               -- claim: the closing hour judged by
  cap_day       INTEGER,                               -- claim: the daily cap applied (voice_ack: its ceiling)
  cap_hour      INTEGER,                               -- claim: the hourly cap applied (voice_ack: NULL)
  CHECK (handset GLOB 'i:?*'),
  CHECK (kind IN ('quote','enquiry','staff_list','offer','reminder','winback','brief','voice_ack','handover_alert','other')),
  CHECK (proactive = (kind IN ('quote','enquiry','staff_list','offer','reminder','winback','brief'))),
  CHECK (mode IN ('claim','record')),
  CHECK (mode = 'record' OR kind IN ('quote','enquiry','staff_list','offer','voice_ack')),
  CHECK (mode = 'claim' OR outcome IS NOT NULL),
  CHECK (try BETWEEN 1 AND 3),
  CHECK (outcome IS NULL OR outcome IN ('sent','uncertain','not_sent')),
  CHECK (gap_s BETWEEN 0 AND 900),
  CHECK (mode = 'claim' OR (win_from IS NULL AND win_to IS NULL AND cap_day IS NULL AND cap_hour IS NULL)),
  CHECK (mode = 'record' OR (win_from IS NOT NULL AND win_to IS NOT NULL AND cap_day IS NOT NULL
                             AND (cap_hour IS NULL) = (kind = 'voice_ack'))),
  CHECK (win_from IS NULL
         OR (kind = 'voice_ack' AND win_from BETWEEN 7 AND 20 AND win_to BETWEEN win_from + 1 AND 21)
         OR (kind <> 'voice_ack' AND win_from BETWEEN 8 AND 19 AND win_to BETWEEN win_from + 1 AND 20)),
  CHECK (cap_day IS NULL OR cap_day BETWEEN 1 AND 60),
  CHECK (cap_hour IS NULL OR cap_hour BETWEEN 1 AND 30));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_was_ref   ON wa_auto_sends(kind, ref, try);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_was_day   ON wa_auto_sends(handset, local_day);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_was_time  ON wa_auto_sends(handset, claimed_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_was_phone ON wa_auto_sends(phone, local_day) WHERE phone IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_was_waid  ON wa_auto_sends(wa_message_id) WHERE wa_message_id IS NOT NULL;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS was_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_auto_sends
  WHEN OLD.claimed_at > datetime('now', '-400 days')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_auto_sends: the ledger is kept for 400 days'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS was_settled_once BEFORE UPDATE OF outcome ON wa_auto_sends WHEN OLD.outcome IS NOT NULL
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_auto_sends: a claim is settled once'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS was_identity_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF handset, kind, ref, try, mode, proactive, local_day,
  gap_s, claimed_at, win_from, win_to, cap_day, cap_hour ON wa_auto_sends
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_auto_sends: what was claimed is fixed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS was_phone_erase_only BEFORE UPDATE OF phone ON wa_auto_sends WHEN NEW.phone IS NOT NULL
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_auto_sends: a phone may only be erased'); END;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quote_list_sends (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  list_date  TEXT NOT NULL,                            -- Kampala date
  owner_key  TEXT NOT NULL,                            -- 'staff:<retailers id>' | 'central'
  outcome    TEXT NOT NULL,
  item_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  detail     TEXT,                                     -- a missed list's last code, digit_run or no_attempt
  sections   TEXT,                                     -- per section its count and listed quote_keys (JSON), no text
  created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),  -- a built list: the moment its build began to read
  CHECK (outcome IN ('sent','uncertain','not_sent','missed')),
  CHECK ((outcome = 'missed') = (sections IS NULL)));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_qls_day ON quote_list_sends(list_date, owner_key) WHERE outcome <> 'not_sent';
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS qls_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON quote_list_sends
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'quote_list_sends: a list record is never deleted'); END;

-- quote_followup_state holds k/v rows, no phone and no text: tracker_cursor, tracker_ran and
-- ref_conflict:<quote_key> (the tracker); list_swept and list_last:<date>:<owner_key> (the list);
-- wasender:<local_day>:<kind> and noinstance:<local_day>:<kind> (the hooks)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quote_followup_state (k TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')));

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_seen_marks (             -- R-01, R-07: a message the webhook could not store; no text
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  direction     TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- in: a customer's | out: the handset's, with no text
  phone         TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- the customer's digits; '' for an inbound with no number, or once erased
  channel       TEXT NOT NULL,
  instance      TEXT NOT NULL,
  kind          TEXT NOT NULL,                         -- the envelope key, or lid_no_number
  wa_message_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  seen_at       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  CHECK (direction IN ('in','out')));
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wsm_msg   ON wa_seen_marks(wa_message_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wsm_phone ON wa_seen_marks(phone, direction, seen_at);
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wsm_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_seen_marks
  WHEN OLD.seen_at > datetime('now', '-400 days')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_seen_marks: a mark is kept for 400 days'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wsm_never_changed BEFORE UPDATE OF direction, channel, instance, kind, wa_message_id, seen_at ON wa_seen_marks
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_seen_marks: a mark is never changed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wsm_phone_erase_only BEFORE UPDATE OF phone ON wa_seen_marks WHEN NEW.phone <> ''
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_seen_marks: a phone may only be erased'); END;
INSERT INTO _schema_checks (migration, expected, found)
SELECT '089_quote_followups.sql', 38,
   (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name IN
      ('_schema_checks','quote_tracker','wa_auto_sends','quote_list_sends','quote_followup_state','wa_seen_marks'))
 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type NOT IN ('table','trigger','view') AND name IN
      ('idx_qt_quote_id','idx_qt_open','idx_qt_phone','idx_qt_owner','idx_fu_quote','idx_was_ref','idx_was_day',
       'idx_was_time','idx_was_phone','idx_was_waid','idx_qls_day','idx_wsm_msg','idx_wsm_phone'))
 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'trigger' AND sql LIKE '%END' AND name IN
      ('qt_never_deleted','qt_status_once','qt_identity_fixed','qt_phone_erase_only','was_never_deleted',
       'was_settled_once','was_identity_fixed','was_phone_erase_only','qls_never_deleted','wsm_never_deleted',
       'wsm_never_changed','wsm_phone_erase_only'))
 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('followups') WHERE name IN ('kind','quote_key'))
 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('wa_auto_sends') WHERE name IN ('win_from','win_to','cap_day','cap_hour'))
 + (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pragma_table_info('quote_list_sends') WHERE name = 'sections');
```

**How it verifies itself.** If any object is missing or a trigger was cut short, `found ≠ expected`. The INSERT then fails with `CHECK constraint failed`, which the runner does not swallow. A missing `_schema_checks` or an SQLite without `pragma_table_info` fails with `no such table`, which is not swallowed either, because the statement contains no INDEX in any case (`:233`). `migration.log` then records the file as PARTIAL, and `_schema_checks` gets no row.

The object count is 6 tables, 13 indexes, 12 triggers and 7 columns, **38** in all. The columns are `followups`' `kind`
and `quote_key`, the ledger's four limits and `quote_list_sends.sections` (ruling R18), each counted by name through
`pragma_table_info`, so a table that already existed without them fails the check. It is fixed by name, never by a count
alone (R-12). The tool's read-only `doctor` (§H.2.12.1), `quote_followup A`, QF-G2 and QF-CA1 each assert three things,
and **the row is the verdict**:
1. the `_schema_checks` row exists with `found = expected = 38` — its absence is FAIL whatever the log says (MG4);
2. every name is present, from `sqlite_master`;
3. `migration.log` holds `OK: 089_quote_followups.sql` (printed; a mismatch with 1 is reported, never overriding it).

**090 and 091** each repeat 089's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _schema_checks …` statement **byte for byte, immediately
before their own self-check INSERT**, counted by name in the same way; `quote_followup A` compares the three texts
(K2-03, S2-12, ruling R9; §H.2.18). **091 creates no `wa_offer_schema_check`, and holds no DROP statement:** ruling R9's
"drops" is met by removing the table from 091's design: no server holds it (the live migrations end at
`088_bank_statements.sql`), so 091 needs no DROP. The design's earlier table never existed on any server: no migration
of the live release or of `dev:migrations/` names it, and Part O's §H.4.5 says 091 contains no ALTER, no UPDATE and no
DROP. The rows are keyed by the migration filenames — `089_quote_followups.sql`, `090_wa_voice.sql` and
`091_wa_offers.sql` — which step 2's precondition and Part O's `OfferSchema` use exactly. **090 depends on 089:** stated
here and in its test (`on ack` refuses without both rows), not in a comment. One table, one rule, for the doctor, the
deploy and step 2.

**Notes on the schema:**
- **Retention.** The ledger and the marks can be deleted only after 400 days; the tracker never. 5.18.104 ships no prune, so a later prune needs no schema change.
- **Erasure (A20, S2-22).** A phone may be erased — `NULL` in the ledger, `''` in a mark, `'erased'` in the tracker —
  and never otherwise changed. Erased rows drop out of every per-phone rule. The tool's `erase` command (§H.2.12.1) is
  the only writer. It also erases Part O's `wa_offer_recipients.phone` (091's identity trigger relaxed to allow that
  erase-only change, as these triggers do), and sets Part V's `wa_media.remote_jid` to `''` on Part V §H.3.3's union,
  cited and never restated more narrowly: the rows whose `remote_jid` is `<digits>@s.whatsapp.net`, and the rows whose
  `conversation_id` is a conversation with exactly that phone (090 has no trigger; §H.2.12.1, rulings R10, R16).
- **The limits a claim applied (ruling R18).** A `claim` row carries `win_from`, `win_to`, `cap_day` and `cap_hour`,
  written by the claim with its `claimed_at` (§H.2.5.3 step 9); a `record` row carries none, and only a `voice_ack`
  claim has no `cap_hour`. Their CHECKs are A19's narrow-only ranges (§H.2.5.6), so a stored setting outside them
  fails the insert, which is `ledger_error`: nothing is sent. `was_identity_fixed` holds them with the rest of what
  was claimed. `quote_list_sends.sections` records what a built list showed, per section, and its `created_at` the
  moment its build began to read (§H.2.11.3); a `missed` row has no sections. Every check that re-judges a claim
  or a list reads these, never the settings as they read now (§H.2.12.5).
- **No CHECK requires a phone on the customer kinds (ruling R2).** An erase sets it NULL, and a reminder `record()` whose number cannot be read must still be recorded. `claim()` refuses a customer kind without one instead (`no_phone`, §H.2.5.3).
- **`ALTER … ADD COLUMN`** fires no trigger. Closed `followups` rows are untouched, so `fu_closed_is_history` (`migrations/070_followups.sql:54-59`) never fires.
- **Requirement.** `pragma_table_info` needs SQLite 3.16 or later. On anything older, the INSERT fails, is logged PARTIAL and leaves no row. The server's SQLite version is not established; QF-N1 prints it.
- **A partial 089** (for example `database is locked` on the `ALTER` at first boot) is marked applied and never retried (`lib/MigrationRunner.php:243-247`). Every 5.18.104 reader of `followups.kind` therefore goes through `FollowUpService::hasKind()` (S2-19), and `quote_followup L` proves the enquiry jobs on a book where the column is absent.

#### H.2.5 The one ledger: `lib/WaSendBudget.php` (C3)

**H.2.5.1 API**

```php
WaSendBudget::on(array $config, ?string $dataDir): bool        // StaffJobsGate::applies(...) && $config['wa_send_ledger'] === 'on'
WaSendBudget::handset(string $instance): string                 // idempotent: strip a leading 'i:', strtolower(trim()), re-prefix 'i:'; '' when blank
WaSendBudget::forInstall(array $config, ?string $dataDir, StoreInterface $store, ?callable $handsetOf = null,
                         ?callable $now = null, ?callable $rand = null): self   // $handsetOf, $now, $rand: tests only
WaSendBudget::onConnection(\PDO $pdo, array $config, ?string $dataDir): self   // over a held connection (below)
$b->claim(string $handset, string $kind, string $ref, array $o = []): array
    // ['ok'=>true,'claim'=>int] | ['ok'=>false,'defer'=>code,'retry_at'=>?int,'final'=>bool]
    // retry_at: unix time, null when final; $o['phone'] required for quote|enquiry|offer (else no_phone)
    // $o['in_flight_s']: int 0-900, default 0, proactive kinds only; window judged to now + it (§H.2.5.3 step 2)
$b->settle(int $claim, string $result, array $o = []): void    // 'sent' | 'failed'; $o: maybe_sent, wa_message_id, detail
$b->record(string $handset, string $kind, string $ref, string $result, array $o = []): string
    // never throws, never refuses; answers recorded | ledger_off | not_uganda | no_table | error
    // $result 'sent' | 'failed' and $o (maybe_sent, wa_message_id, detail, phone) exactly as settle() (§H.2.5.5)
$b->counts(string $handset): array                              // for the tool, the checks and the report
WaSendBudget::window(array $config): array                     // proactive: [from, to], Mon–Sat (§H.2.5.6)
WaSendBudget::ackPolicy(array $config): ?array                 // voice_ack: VoiceAckLimits::of($config); null = invalid (§H.2.5.6; ruling R4)
```

- **Every method that takes a handset passes it through `handset()` first** (S2-03, K2-05). So a raw instance name (`$evo->instanceFor($channel)`, `lib/EvolutionApiService.php:410-413`, which returns the configured name as written), a lower-cased one and an already-prefixed one land on the same rows. The `CHECK (handset GLOB 'i:?*')` is the floor beneath.
- `claim` is idempotent per `(kind, ref)`. **`forInstall` derives the channel-to-handset map itself** — `WaSendBudget::handset(EvolutionApiService::forStore(...)->instanceFor($ch))` (`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:179`, `:410-413`) — and the reservation (§H.2.5.4) uses it, so the quote reserve that offers depend on never varies with what a caller passes. `$handsetOf` is accepted for tests only (ruling R2).
- **Every phone argument is normalised by the ledger** (ruling R2): `PhoneNumber::international(raw, tenant)` with the leading '+' removed, NULL when that fails — for every kind, in `claim()` and `record()` alike. `sendVia`'s `$to` is the caller's form, which the live sender converts only internally (`lib/NotificationService.php:2062-2082`); without this a reminder row could hold national digits while a chase or an offer holds international ones, and step 8a's equality would miss.
- **`$o['in_flight_s']`, the in-flight bound (A12-01, B12-02).** The longest a caller's claimed send can take from the
  claim's moment to the gateway's return: an int from 0 to 900, default 0, for proactive kinds only. `claim()`
  judges the window at the claim's moment and again at that moment plus the bound (§H.2.5.3 step 2), so a send
  claimed inside the window also ends inside it. Part O passes 50, its measured bound (its O-D9 and §H.4.10); its
  C-O2-2 re-judges the claim from the row's `claimed_at` and the window the row records, never from `sent_at`
  (§H.2.5.3 steps 2 and 9; ruling R18). Part F's own senders pass none: a chase,
  an enquiry follow-up and the daily list are judged at the claim's moment, as before. A value outside 0–900, or
  one given with `voice_ack`, answers `not_claimable`, final (step 0). `record()` takes no bound.
- `settle(…, 'failed', ['maybe_sent' => true])` stores `uncertain`. It counts as sent and is never retried: the live rule, `lib/EvolutionApiService.php:778-783`. That is the form for **every** caller and every path, Part O's step 9, stale sweep and off-hook included (ruling R2).
- `forInstall` takes the store so it can read `master_schedule.json` for `ReminderDay` (step 8b) and the PDO from it.
- **`onConnection()` builds the ledger over a connection the caller already holds**, for a caller that holds no store.
  `SqliteStore`'s constructor is private, and `create()` opens a connection of its own and runs the migrations
  (`lib/SqliteStore.php:130`, `:140-265`), so no store, and no `forInstall()`, can be had over a given `\PDO`.
  `show` and the checks build it on the tool's `$ro`, the report on its one read-only connection (§H.2.8.3), an
  off-hook that settles a ledger claim on the tool's `$rw` (§H.2.12.1; ruling R13), and the Starlink hook's
  `recordDirect()` on the worker's own PDO (§H.2.6.3; A11-05). They call only `counts()` on it, the off-hook only
  `settle()`, and `recordDirect()` only `record()`, an `INSERT OR IGNORE` of a settled row that needs no store
  (§H.2.5.5). `claim()` on it answers `not_claimable`, final, with `retry_at` null, and inserts
  nothing, since it holds no store for `ReminderDay` (step 8b) or the reservation (§H.2.5.4). LG pins it (§H.2.14).

**H.2.5.2 The kinds**

| kind | class | how it enters | counts to day and hour caps | window enforced by `claim` | spacing it waits for | own limit | phone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| quote | proactive | claim | yes | `window()`: default Mon–Sat 08:00–20:00 Kampala (D3) | `max(claimed_at+gap_s)` over every row on the handset | — | yes |
| enquiry | proactive | claim while chase or offers is on, else record | yes | same, when claimed | same | — | yes |
| staff_list | proactive | claim | yes | same (the job itself: 08:00–11:00) | same | — | no |
| offer | proactive | claim (P6) | yes | same, to the claim's moment plus its `in_flight_s` (Part O passes 50; §H.2.5.3 step 2) | same | the reservation | yes |
| reminder, winback | proactive | record | yes | — (never deferred) | — | — | yes |
| brief | proactive | record | yes | — | — | — | no |
| voice_ack | reply | claim (Part V) | **no** | `ackPolicy()`: default every day 07:00–21:00 (D15) | `ackPolicy()` gap (default 20 s) after every row | `ackPolicy()` daily max per handset (default 25) | no |
| handover_alert, other | internal | record | no | — | — | — | no |

- **`gap_s`.** A claimed proactive row draws a random value in [`wa_send_gap_min_s`, `wa_send_gap_max_s`]. Every other row stores `wa_send_gap_min_s`. So a proactive send keeps its spacing after **any** send, while a reply, an alert or a transactional document adds only the minimum gap and restarts nothing (C3).
- **Proactive versus reply.** A proactive claim never waits on a reply's ceiling. A reply is never refused by the proactive caps.

**H.2.5.3 `claim()`, in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`** (`busy_timeout` 5 s, `lib/SqliteStore.php:158`)

**The claim's moment (ruling R18).** `claim()` reads its clock once, `$now` (the injected clock in tests), after
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` holds the lock. Every step below judges at that moment, and step 9 writes it as the row's
`claimed_at`, with the limits the claim applied. So the row records the instant the claim decided, and a check
that re-judges the claim reads that instant and those limits, never a later stamp and never today's settings. No
other writer can write while the lock is held, so a row whose storage stamp is in an earlier second than `$now`
was written, and committed, before the claim took the lock: every read the sender makes after the claim sees it
(§H.2.10.6 item 4).

0. **Refusals before anything else.**
   - The ledger is off → `ledger_off`.
   - The kind cannot be claimed → `not_claimable` (a programming error, final).
   - `$o['in_flight_s']` given and not an int from 0 to 900, or given with `voice_ack` → `not_claimable`, final (a
     programming error; A12-01).
   - The handset, normalised, is `''` → `no_instance`.
   - **`dn_tz() !== 'Africa/Kampala'`** → `zone`, so a stored `timezone` key or the Juba fallback (`lib/timezone.php:43-67`) can never move the window (R-16).
   - A quote, enquiry or offer whose phone is missing, or does not normalise → `no_phone`, final (ruling R2). Part F holds the draft and Part O skips the recipient, so the per-person rule cannot be bypassed by an empty option.
1. **Idempotency on the rows for `(kind, ref)`:**
   - one is `sent` or `uncertain` → `already_sent`, final;
   - one is in flight for less than 900 s → `in_flight`, retry at `claimed_at + 900`;
   - one is in flight for longer → settle it `uncertain` (`stale`) and answer `already_sent`, final, so it is never re-sent (F3);
   - `try = 1 + count(not_sent)`; above 3 → `tries_exhausted`, final.
2. **Window**, computed in a literal `DateTimeZone('Africa/Kampala')`:
   - proactive kinds → `window()`, judged at the claim's moment and again at that moment plus `$o['in_flight_s']`
     (default 0; Part O's offer claims pass 50, §H.2.5.1; A12-01, B12-02): outside at the moment, or the moment
     plus the bound after the window's close → `window`, retry at the next opening (the next open day's
     `wa_send_hour_from` when only the bound passes the close). The bound never reaches the next day, since the
     close is at most 20:00 and the bound at most 900 s. So a send claimed inside the window ends inside it, and
     the row records the window it was judged by (step 9): Part O's C-O2-2, whose `FAIL` can never be accepted
     (§H.2.12.3), re-judges the claim by that window from the row's `claimed_at`, never from `sent_at` and never
     by today's settings (ruling R18);
   - `voice_ack` → `ackPolicy()`; null (an invalid stored value, ruling R4) or outside → `window`, final ("instant" is not tomorrow).
3. **Orphans, then one at a time.**
   - (a) **Any** row on the handset in flight for 900 s or more, whatever its kind and ref, is settled `uncertain` with detail `stale_orphan` (S2-17). An orphan whose ref is never claimed again — a crashed offer attempt, a dropped P5 event — is settled here and counts as sent.
   - (b) Another claim on the handset in flight for less than 900 s → `handset_busy`, retry at now + 60.
4. **Spacing.** Proactive: now is before `max(claimed_at + gap_s)` over the handset's rows whose outcome is not `not_sent` → `spacing`. `voice_ack`: now is before `max(claimed_at) + ackPolicy gap` → `spacing`.
5. **`voice_ack` only:** today's acknowledgements on the handset at or above `ackPolicy` daily max → `ack_ceiling`, final. Steps 6–8 do not apply to it.
6. **Hourly cap.** Proactive rows (any mode) in the last 3,600 s at or above `wa_send_hourly_cap` → `hour_cap`, retry when the oldest leaves the hour.
7. **Daily cap with priority:** `used_today + reserve(kind) + 1 > wa_send_daily_cap` → `reserved` (when reserve > 0) or `day_cap`. Retry at the next day's opening.
8. **One automated customer message per person per Kampala day, both ways** (R-06, S2-08). For quote, enquiry and offer:
   - (a) any other row today with this phone (the ledger's one normalised form, ruling R2), a kind in (quote, enquiry, offer, reminder, winback) and an outcome that is not `not_sent` → `phone_today`, retry at the next day's opening. This holds **across every handset**;
   - (b) **reminders first:** while `ReminderDay::done()` is false → `reminders_first`, retry at the earlier of now + 600 and today's `reminder_until_hour`. So no chase or offer can go before a reminder the same person gets later that day (A17).
9. **Insert the row** (mode `claim`, `try`, `gap_s`, phone, `local_day`), with `claimed_at` the claim's moment and the
   limits it applied (ruling R18): `win_from` and `win_to`, the hours step 2 judged by (`window()`'s, or
   `ackPolicy()`'s for `voice_ack`); `cap_day`, the daily cap of step 7 (for `voice_ack`, the ceiling of step 5);
   and `cap_hour`, the hourly cap of step 6 (NULL for `voice_ack`). The spacing it kept is each earlier row's own
   `gap_s` (step 4), already recorded. A unique conflict → `in_flight`. Commit and return the id.

**Any `PDOException` is `ledger_error`, retry at now + 300, and nothing is sent.** The ledger fails closed.

**`lib/ReminderDay.php`** (pure):

```php
final class ReminderDay {
    /** True when today's payment reminders cannot still come after a send made now. */
    public static function done(array $schedule, array $config, ?string $dataDir, int $now): bool
}
```

It returns true when any of these holds:
- `NotifyGate::REMINDERS` does not apply — the reminders then run in the 02:00 maintenance job (`cron/master.php:290-294`);
- now, in a literal Kampala zone, is at or after `reminder_until_hour` — normalised exactly as `cron/master.php:307-310`, and a test asserts equal results over a table of inputs;
- `$schedule['customer_reminders']` has `last_run` at or after today's `reminder_hour` opening and `duration_ms ≥ 0` — master writes `-1` before the job and the real duration after it (`cron/master.php:371-374`, `:398-402`).

The seeded row (`last_run` 1, `cron/master.php:119`) is not done. A crashed run (`-1`) holds chases and offers until `reminder_until_hour`, never later. The cost is stated in §H.2.20 OQ2: on a reminder day the first chase leaves soon after the reminder job ends (default from 09:00), not at 08:00. **It is the one rule (ruling R8):** Part O calls `ReminderDay::done()` (its `remindersSettled()` is at most a one-line delegate), and the ledger's `reminders_first` binds every offer claim anyway.

**H.2.5.4 The priority (C3)**

Priorities: quote 1 › staff_list 2 › enquiry 3 › reminder/winback/brief 4 › offer 5.

`reserve(kind)` is the sum, on this handset today, of the demand of every kind above it:
- **quote:** open `kind='quote'` follow-ups with `due_at` up to the window's close today whose channel maps to this handset;
- **staff_list:** on the sales handset only, before 11:00 with the list on, the owners still to be sent (`QuoteDailyList::pendingToday()`);
- **enquiry:** approved enquiry drafts on this handset, while enquiry claims;
- **reminder/winback/brief** (reserved for offers only): before `reminder_until_hour` (default 17, `cron/master.php:307-310`), and with none of those kinds recorded today on this handset, the largest daily count of them over the previous 7 Kampala days; otherwise 0.

So offers use only what remains after the chases due today (C3, D12). Record-only kinds are never deferred, but they count. Transactional `other` rows (receipts, invoices, quotation PDFs) are not in D12's sixty and reserve nothing; they keep the minimum spacing and are printed in the true total (§H.2.5.7).

**H.2.5.5 `settle()` and `record()`**

**`settle()`** maps the result:

| Result | Outcome |
|---|---|
| sent | `sent` |
| failed, may have been sent | `uncertain` |
| failed, certainly not sent | `not_sent` (not counted; the next claim for the same ref takes `try + 1`) |

It writes `settled_at`, `wa_message_id` and `detail` (`evo_error`, `policy`, `no_instance`), with `WHERE outcome IS NULL`. A row already settled — by the orphan sweep, step 3a — matches nothing, so `was_settled_once` never fires. `settle()` then writes one `PluginLog::write('wa_send_ledger', 'late_settle')` line and returns. It never throws into the sender, and the earlier `uncertain` stands (S2-17).

**`record()`**:
- **takes `$result` `'sent'|'failed'` and `$o` exactly as `settle()` does** (this round's Z-05): `sent` → stored
  `sent`; `failed` with `maybe_sent` true → stored `uncertain`; otherwise `failed` → `not_sent`. It stores
  `wa_message_id`, `detail` and `phone` from `$o`, the phone normalised by the ledger itself (ruling R2). Every caller
  uses this one form: the three hooks (`recordNotify`, `recordAlert`, `recordDirect`; §H.2.6), the enquiry pass
  (§H.2.10.6 item 12) and Part O's test send, `record($handset, 'other', 'offer_test:<id>', 'sent'|'failed',
  ['maybe_sent' => …, 'wa_message_id' => …])`;
- is an `INSERT OR IGNORE` of a settled row, mode `record`, with `claimed_at` the insert's default and none of the
  four limits (§H.2.5.3 step 9);
- refuses nothing;
- is a no-op when the ledger is off, the tenant is not Uganda, or the table is missing;
- **returns a fixed code (ruling R2):** `recorded`; `ledger_off`, `not_uganda` or `no_table` when it wrote nothing;
  `error` when it swallowed a throwable. The existing record-only hooks ignore it. Part O stores the code on its
  test row. C-O1-1 and `offer_start` count only a `recorded` test. C-O1-3 reads FAIL on `ledger_off`,
  `not_uganda` or `no_table`, on a `recorded` test with no `offer_test:<id>` row on its handset, and on a `sent`
  test with `ledger` NULL. It prints an `error` test, and an `uncertain` test that a sweep settled with `ledger`
  NULL, never FAIL (Part O §H.4.6; Q17-O01; Q18-O02);
- swallows every throwable, answers `error`, and writes one line,
  `PluginLog::write('wa_send_ledger', 'hook_write_lost <kind>')`, for each write it so loses: the fixed code and
  the kind only, never a ref, phone or id (`lib/PluginLog.php:35-45`). The line goes to `data/plugin.log`, a file
  outside the book (`:21-24`), so a wait past `busy_timeout` that loses the row cannot lose the line; L-ON reads
  it (§H.2.6.1, §H.2.12.5; Q19-F02).

**H.2.5.6 Settings**

The tool's `set` command (§H.2.12.7) holds the settings, each refused outside its range. **A setting may narrow an owner-decided window, never widen it** (A19).

| Setting key | Default | Range | Read through |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wa_send_daily_cap` | 60 (D12) | 1–60, narrow only: D12's 60 is the ceiling, and raising it is an owner answer, never a `set` (A19) | `claim()` |
| `wa_send_hourly_cap` | 15 | 1–30 | `claim()` |
| `wa_send_gap_min_s` | 60 | 30–600 | `claim()` |
| `wa_send_gap_max_s` | 180 | min–900 | `claim()` |
| `wa_send_hour_from` | 8 (D3) | 8–19 | `window()` |
| `wa_send_hour_to` | 20 (D3) | from+1–20 | `window()`; Sunday is never open (D3), not a setting |
| `wa_voice_ack_hour_from` | 7 (D15) | 7–20 | `VoiceAckLimits::of()`, through `ackPolicy()` |
| `wa_voice_ack_hour_to` | 21 (D15) | from+1–21 | same |
| `wa_voice_ack_gap_s` | 20 | 5–120 | same |
| `wa_voice_ack_daily_max` (per handset per Kampala day) | 25 | 1–60 | same |

**One holder for each value (K2-18, ruling R4).** The five acknowledgement keys, their defaults and their ranges live once, in Part V's pure `lib/VoiceAckLimits.php` (`KEYS`, `DEFAULTS`, `RANGES`, `of()`, `inWindow()`). The ledger reads four of them through `ackPolicy()`, the four rows above. `WaSendBudget::ackPolicy()` is a thin delegate to `VoiceAckLimits::of($config)`, so the ledger and P5 read the same numbers, and the tool's `set` validates with `VoiceAckLimits::RANGES`. `of()` returns null on any invalid stored value, and `claim('voice_ack')` then answers `window`, final: it fails towards sending nothing. The ceiling key is `wa_voice_ack_daily_max` everywhere. The fifth, `wa_voice_ack_period_hours`, is Part V's per-conversation rule, read only by Part V's P5 (ruling R4). **The hours are narrow-only:** hour_from 7–20, hour_to from+1–21. D15's 07:00–21:00 is the ceiling, because a wider setting would override an owner decision; widening is an owner answer, never a `set`, and `set ack-hours 7 22` is refused with nothing saved.

**A `set` binds the next claim, never an earlier one (ruling R18).** A setting may be narrowed at any time
(§H.2.12.7), and a claim already made keeps the limits it applied: its row records them (§H.2.5.3 step 9), with
each earlier row's `gap_s` for the spacing. Every check that re-judges a claim reads those recorded values, never
the settings as they read now: this part's (§H.2.12.5, QF-ON3), Part V's VA-ON1, and Part O's C-O2-2 and C-O2-6
(IV-1, IO-1, IO-7). Ruling R8's "a check reads the settings" means them.

**H.2.5.7 What `counts()` gives**

Per handset:
- proactive sends today against the cap, and in the last hour against the hourly cap;
- record-only proactive sends today (reminder, winback, brief);
- `voice_ack` today against its ceiling;
- internal and transactional sends today (`handover_alert`, `other`);
- **the true total today**, every kind;
- in-flight claims, and orphans settled today (`stale_orphan`);
- the next allowed time for a proactive send, by the window, the spacing and the two caps.

`counts()` needs no store: the reservation and `reminders_first` depend on the kind and are `claim()`'s alone, so
`onConnection()` serves it (§H.2.5.1).

The tool prints a handset by its role and an index — `handset 1 (support, account)`, `handset 3 (a salesperson's line)` — never the instance name, a staff id or a number.

**H.2.5.8 The call contract — one for every caller (K2-08)**

| Kind | Caller | ref (stable across retries) | claim / record | phone | limits the row records (§H.2.5.3 step 9; ruling R18) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| quote | `cron/followup_send.php` | `fu:<followup_id>:<attempt>` | claim | yes | `win_from`, `win_to` (`window()`'s hours), `cap_day`, `cap_hour` |
| enquiry | `cron/followup_send.php` | `fu:<followup_id>:<attempt>` | claim while chase or offers is on, else record | yes | as quote when claimed; none when recorded |
| staff_list | `cron/quote_daily_list.php` | `list:<Kampala date>:<owner_key>` | claim | no | as quote |
| offer | Part O's sender | `offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>` — stable per recipient, **never a per-attempt token**; the ledger's own `try` counts attempts, and Part O's `attempt` column serves only its own row CAS (ruling R2) | claim, `['phone' => <digits>, 'in_flight_s' => 50]`: the in-flight bound (§H.2.5.1, §H.2.5.3 step 2; A12-01) | yes | as quote; Part O's recipient row records `judged_at` and the per-handset maximum it applied (Part O's half; IO-1) |
| voice_ack | Part V's worker | `ack:<the voice note's wa_message_id>` (Part V's `wa:` form is retired) | claim | no | `win_from`, `win_to` (`ackPolicy()`'s hours), `cap_day` (its ceiling); `cap_hour` NULL; the acknowledgement gap is recorded by Part V's `wa_voice_acks` (IV-1) |
| reminder, winback, brief, other | the hooks (§H.2.6) | `n:<wa id>` or `n:x<sha1(event, to, microtime, random)>`; `a:<…>` for alerts; `s:<…>` for Starlink | record | reminder, winback only, normalised by the ledger (ruling R2) | none |
| handover_alert | `AlertService` hook | `a:<wa id>` or `a:x<sha1>` | record | no | none |
| other | Part O's test send | `offer_test:<test id>` | record | no | none |

Every answer code, and what each caller does with it. **Every caller maps by code, never by the answer's shape** (ruling R2). The Part V column is Part V's own table (§H.3.15 step 13) and is binding: its defers write no decision row, and staleness is measured from the voice note's `received_at` (the 600 s rule). The Part O column is written from Part O's sender:

| Code | Final | Part F's senders | Part V (voice_ack) | Part O (offer) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ledger_off` | yes | the run sends nothing | no send; `skipped:ledger_off` | the recipient released unchanged; the run ends (fail closed) |
| `zone` | yes | held, the code counted | no send; `skipped:ledger_zone` | released unchanged; the run ends |
| `no_instance` | yes | held, the code counted | no send; `skipped:no_instance` | released unchanged; the run ends |
| `not_claimable` | yes | held, the code counted | no send; `skipped:ledger_unknown` | recipient `skipped(not_claimable)` |
| `no_phone` | yes | held, the code counted; never sent | — (it claims no phone) | recipient `skipped(no_phone)` |
| `already_sent` | yes | `recordUncertain` (quote: `armAfterUncertain()`; the daily list writes its owner's row `uncertain`, §H.2.11.3 step 1, Q18-F03) | returns; no decision row (the first decision stands) | recipient `uncertain('ledger_already_sent')`; never re-sent |
| `tries_exhausted` | yes | close `send_failed` | no send; `skipped:ledger_unknown` | recipient `skipped(tries_exhausted)` |
| `in_flight` | no | held, next run | `WorkerDefer(15)` while inside 600 s of `received_at`, no decision row; then `skipped:stale` | released to `retry_at` |
| `handset_busy`, `spacing` | no | held | `WorkerDefer(max(5, min(retry_at − now, 60)))` while inside 600 s of `received_at`, no decision row; then `skipped:stale` | released to `retry_at` |
| `window` | quote, enquiry, list, offer: no; voice_ack: yes | held | no send; `skipped:quiet_hours` | released to `retry_at` (the next opening), also when the claim's moment plus `in_flight_s` passes the close (§H.2.5.3 step 2) |
| `ack_ceiling` | yes | — | no send; `skipped:number_cap` | — |
| `hour_cap`, `day_cap`, `reserved`, `reminders_first` | no | held | — | released to `retry_at` |
| `phone_today` | no | held | — | released to the next Kampala day's opening |
| `ledger_error` | no | held, nothing sent | no send; `skipped:ledger_error` | the run ends (fail closed) |
| any other code | — | held, the code counted | no send; `skipped:ledger_unknown` (the code logged) | the run ends (fail closed) |

`retry_at` is an int unix time, null when final (ruling R2): Part V subtracts it, and Part O stores it with `UtcClock::stamp()`. Part V's own codes `voice_ack_gap` and `voice_ack_ceiling` are retired in favour of these.

**`settle()`'s arguments are the same for every caller:** `settle($claim, 'sent'|'failed', ['maybe_sent' => EvolutionApiService::mayHaveBeenSent($res), 'wa_message_id' => <the id the send returned>, 'detail' => <code>])`. **The id is required whenever the send returned one.** It is how `HumanTakeover` knows the echo is ours (§H.2.7.1). Without it, an acknowledgement or offer echo that beats its claim is stored as `Team` (`evo_webhook.php:197-221`) and stops a quote as `taken`. A may-have-been-sent result is `failed` with `maybe_sent: true` — stored `uncertain`, counted, never retried — and never `sent`, for every caller and every path: Part O's step 9, its stale sweep and its off-hook included (ruling R2). Settling it `sent` is the weakened copy in each part (WB32 here; Part V's A29; Part O's OM31, inverted). Test LG29 drives Part V's and Part O's exact call shapes through fakes.

#### H.2.6 The record-only hooks, and each sender's call into the ledger

**H.2.6.1 `NotificationService::sendVia`, `sendDocument` and `sendImage`**

Each hook goes after the Evolution branch has returned and `$success` is known, between `}   // ← end of the WASender branch` and `// Track result for retry mode`:
- `sendVia`: `lib/NotificationService.php:2380`/`:2382`;
- `sendDocument`: `:1743`/`:1745`;
- `sendImage`: `:1842`, before its own tracking block.

It records in the ledger only when Evolution carried the send (`$evoRes !== null`: `:2346` for text; `:1712` and
`:1811` for the media branch through `sendMediaViaEvolution`, `:1984-2006`), because WASender is not a handset. A
send WASender carried (`$evoRes === null`: `evoFor()` names no Evolution service when the configuration the
service was built with gives the sender's channel no instance, `:1910-1931`) is counted instead, content-free
(`countWasender`, below; Q17-F01), so that L-ON can tell the two transports apart (§H.2.12.5).

```php
// 5.18.104 (root docs/72 §H.2.6, C3): an automated send from a handset goes into the one ledger — never deferred, never
// refused; a record that cannot be written never stops a send. Uganda with the ledger on; nothing at all otherwise.
if ((string)($this->evoConfig['wa_send_ledger'] ?? '') === 'on') {
    try {
        require_once __DIR__ . '/WaSendBudget.php';
        if ($evoRes !== null) {
            WaSendBudget::recordNotify($this->store, $this->evoConfig, $this->evoChannelFor($sender),
                (string)$event, (string)$to, (bool)$success, (string)($evoRes['error'] ?? ''), (string)$response);
        } else {   // Q17-F01: WASender carried it; no handset, so a content-free count for L-ON
            WaSendBudget::countWasender($this->store, $this->evoConfig, (string)$event);
        }
    } catch (\Throwable $e) { /* the send matters more than its record */ }
}
```

What `recordNotify` does:
- **returns at once for a person's event** — `HumanTakeover::personEvents()`: `wa_staff_reply`, `wa_send_document`, `wa_image_send`, `wa_media_send`. The Inbox's sender route reaches `sendVia`, `sendDocument` and `sendImage` with those events (`lib/InboxReplyRoute.php:91-97`; `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:246`, `:276`, `:1002`, `:1036` at `221c9dc`, re-made against the merged tree, ruling R10). A person's send is never filed as automation and adds no spacing (S2-02, K2-12);
- applies `StaffJobsGate` with the store's data directory;
- takes the handset from `evo_instance_<chan>`, the instance `sendViaEvolution` and `sendMediaViaEvolution` used (`:1918-1929`, `:1948-1951`, `:1989`);
- takes `wa_message_id` from the raw answer, as the store does (`:2425-2428`), and passes it in `$o`;
- calls `record()` in its one form (§H.2.5.5): `'sent'` when `$success`, else `'failed'` with
  `['maybe_sent' => EvolutionApiService::mayHaveBeenSent($error)]` (`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:778-783`), so the
  row reads `sent`, `uncertain` or `not_sent`;
- uses the ref `'n:'.wa_message_id`, or else `'n:x'.sha1(event|to|microtime|random)` (never a phone in a ref);
- keeps the phone only for reminder and winback, passed from `$to` as `$o['phone']` and normalised by the ledger itself (ruling R2); it ignores `record()`'s answer code.

What `countWasender($store, array $config, string $event): void` does (Q17-F01): it returns at once for a
person's event and applies `StaffJobsGate`, as `recordNotify` does, and is a no-op where `record()` is one; it
takes the kind from `NOTIFY_KINDS`, below; and it adds one, in one statement so that two processes never lose a
count, to the `quote_followup_state` key `wasender:<local_day>:<kind>`, `local_day` the Kampala date as `record()`
takes it. It keeps no phone, id or text, writes no ledger row and never throws into the send. L-ON reads these
counts (§H.2.12.5).

**A write a hook loses (Q19-F02).** Each of the hooks' writes is one statement on the book, which waits at most
`busy_timeout`, 5 s (live `lib/SqliteStore.php:158`), and the send's Message Log row is a second write, made after
the hook (live `lib/NotificationService.php:2387`, `:1750`, `:1848`, after the hook points above;
`lib/AlertService.php:128`, `:131`, after `:125`). So a writer that holds the book's lock across a hook and
releases it before the log row, as an admin's VACUUM can (live `tabs/admin/maintenance.php:154-157`, "Safe to run
anytime"; `includes/post/post_leads.php:726-736`), loses the hook's write while the log row lands. Every write so
lost, `record()`'s row, `countWasender()`'s increment or the no-instance increment (§H.2.6.2), and every other
throwable they swallow, writes one `PluginLog::write('wa_send_ledger', 'hook_write_lost <kind>')` line, the kind
only (§H.2.5.5). `recordNotify`, `recordAlert` and `recordDirect` also catch every throwable inside themselves,
after taking their kind by a lookup that cannot throw (`NOTIFY_KINDS`, or the alert key's first segment), and
write the same line when one stops them before their write. So a hunk's own `catch` is reached only when
`lib/WaSendBudget.php` cannot be loaded, and then no hook is wired at all. A path that writes nothing by design
(a person's event, `StaffJobsGate`, the ledger off) loses nothing and writes no line. L-ON counts a lost write
and reads the lines (§H.2.12.5).

The kind comes from `WaSendBudget::NOTIFY_KINDS`:

| Kind | Events |
|---|---|
| **reminder** | `ops_pre_due_d7`, `ops_pre_due_d3`, `ops_pre_due_d1`, `ops_overdue_d1`, `ops_overdue_d3`, `ops_overdue_d5`, `ops_low_balance` (the seven tiers, `lib/InvoiceReminders.php:150-163`; `lib/NotificationService.php:804-822,941-1011`) |
| **winback** | `ops_win_back` (`:1130`) |
| **brief** | `staff_jobs_summary` (`cron/staff_jobs_summary.php:253`), `staff_daily_report` (`cron/staff_ssp_report.php:121`), `bidal_morning_summary` (`lib/NotificationService.php:1465`), `cashbook_daily_summary` (`cron/cashbook_summary.php:102,191`), `cash_carry_reminder` (`cron/cash_carry_reminder.php:87`) |
| **other** | every other event: receipts, quotations, invoice, quotation and delivery PDFs, welcomes, admins' alerts, login codes, `wa_media_ack` |

A test asserts that every event in the map occurs as a literal in the tree's `sendVia`, `sendRaw`, `sendDocument`, `sendImage` or method calls, so a renamed event fails the build. The cost is one insert, the same class of write `sendVia` already makes after every success (`storeMessage`, `:2429`).

**H.2.6.2 `AlertService::sendTo`** (`lib/AlertService.php:107-137`)

The hook goes right after `$r = $evo->sendText('sales', …)` (`:125`), before the `ok` test:

```php
// 5.18.104 (root docs/72 §H.2.6, C3): recorded, never deferred. The daily list claims its own place first (quote_list:).
if ((string)($this->config['wa_send_ledger'] ?? '') === 'on' && strpos($key, 'quote_list:') !== 0) {
    try { require_once __DIR__ . '/WaSendBudget.php'; WaSendBudget::recordAlert($this->store, $this->config, $evo, $key, $r); }
    catch (\Throwable $e) { /* the alert matters more than its record */ }
}
```

`recordAlert` takes the handset from `$evo->instanceFor('sales')` (guarded with `method_exists` for injected fakes). The kind is `handover_alert` for an `escalate:` key, which covers the hand-overs, P5's and R3's (R104-04), and `other` for every other key. It keeps no phone.

**An alert with no sales instance (Q18-F01).** AlertService sends only through Evolution on `sales`
(`lib/AlertService.php:120-125`). When `instanceFor('sales')` is blank (`evo_instance_sales` unset, as while the
number is re-paired), `sendText` refuses before any request and answers `http` 0 (live
`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:641-644`, `:765-768`), which AlertService logs with `http_code` 0, not NULL
(`lib/AlertService.php:128`, `:163`). No ledger row can hold that send: `handset('')` is `''`, and the CHECK
`handset GLOB 'i:?*'` keeps the row out (an `INSERT OR IGNORE` skips a CHECK failure without an error). So
`recordAlert` then calls no `record()` and, when the answer carries `http`, adds one, in one statement and
content-free, to the `quote_followup_state` key `noinstance:<local_day>:<kind>`, `local_day` the Kampala date as
`record()` takes it and the kind as above, under `StaffJobsGate` and the never-throw rule, as `countWasender()`
does (§H.2.6.1); a lost increment writes the `hook_write_lost <kind>` line (§H.2.6.1; Q19-F02). An answer with
no `http` is logged with `http_code` NULL, which L-ON skips, and adds nothing.
L-ON subtracts the count (§H.2.12.5).

**One getter, for the daily list (A11-01).** `AlertService` gains `lastResult(): ?array`. `notify()` and
`notifyTo()` set it to null on entry, and `sendTo()` sets it to `$r` right after `sendText` (`:125`), so a cooldown,
a missing number or a throwable before an answer leaves it null. `notify()` and `notifyTo()` return only
`{sent, reason}` (`:51-56`, `:64-69`), and a failure's reason is `'send_failed: '` before the error (`:129`),
which `EvolutionApiService::mayHaveBeenSent()` cannot read, since it tests how the error begins
(`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:778-783`). The daily list settles from `lastResult()` (§H.2.11.3); nothing else
reads it, and every caller's answer is unchanged.

**H.2.6.3 `StarlinkMailWorker`** (`workers/StarlinkMailWorker.php:302`, master job `starlink_mail`, `cron/master.php:163`)

It sends with `$this->evo->sendText(...)` directly, outside the notifier (S2-09). One hook goes right after that line:

```php
// 5.18.104 (root docs/72 §H.2.6, C3): an order message from a handset is recorded — never deferred.
if ((string)($this->config['wa_send_ledger'] ?? '') === 'on') {
    try { require_once dirname(__DIR__) . '/lib/WaSendBudget.php';
          require_once dirname(__DIR__) . '/lib/bootstrap_data.php';
          $dd = $this->config['_data_dir'] ?? ($GLOBALS['dataDir'] ?? null);   // as internationalUg() reads it
          $dd = is_string($dd) && $dd !== '' ? $dd : getDataDir(dirname(__DIR__));
          WaSendBudget::recordDirect($this->pdo, $this->config, $dd, $this->evo, $channel, 'other', 's', $r); }
    catch (\Throwable $e) { /* the order message matters more than its record */ }
}
```

The kind is `other` and no phone is kept: a transactional message, not in D12's sixty.
`recordDirect(\PDO $pdo, array $config, ?string $dataDir, $evo, string $channel, string $kind, string $prefix,
$r): void` builds its ledger with `WaSendBudget::onConnection($pdo, $config, $dataDir)` (§H.2.5.1) and calls only
`record()` on it, in its one form (§H.2.5.5) (A11-05). The hook passes the PDO because nothing else it holds
reaches the book: `$evo` holds no PDO (`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:110-116`; `forStore()` uses one only to build
its routing, `:179-206`), while the worker holds `$this->pdo` (`workers/StarlinkMailWorker.php:39`, `:50-58`),
the store's own connection (`cron/starlink_mail.php:34`, `:39`, `:48`). It passes the data directory as
`internationalUg()` finds it (`workers/StarlinkMailWorker.php:319-320`), else `getDataDir()`
(`lib/bootstrap_data.php:26`), whose answer `cron/starlink_mail.php:33` has already cached: `StaffJobsGate` must
be given it, or it can read Uganda as South Sudan (`lib/StaffJobsGate.php:9-11`). `recordDirect` applies the same
gate and the same never-throw rule. The hunk is PHP 7.4. The file already uses `match`
(`workers/StarlinkMailWorker.php:292`), so whether this worker runs on the server's PHP is not established
(§H.2.20).

**H.2.6.4 `cron/followup_send.php`'s enquiry drafts** (§H.2.10.6)

- They **record** after the send while neither the chase nor offers is on.
- They **claim** (kind `enquiry`, ref `fu:<followup_id>:<attempt>`) while either is on.
- In both cases, only while `followup_enabled` is on (S2-01).

The step that changes them is the chase's own step (6). The tool prints that change at `on chase` (R104-09).

**H.2.6.5 Part V's P5 and Part O's offers** (the interface; §H.2.5.8)

- **P5:** `claim($instance, 'voice_ack', 'ack:'.$waMessageId)` before the send, then `settle()` with the id immediately after the echo claim. V's window, spacing and ceiling come from `VoiceAckLimits::of()`, through `ackPolicy()` (§H.2.5.6; ruling R4). **Migration 090 depends on 089:** stated in §H.2.4 and in its test (`on ack` refuses without both `_schema_checks` rows), not in 090's header (ruling R9).
- **Offers:** `claim($instance, 'offer', 'offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>', ['phone' => $p])`, the same ref for every attempt (ruling R2). The reservation and `reminders_first` apply inside `claim`.
- **The offers audience must exclude:**
  - partner-owned numbers (C10);
  - every phone with an inbound mark (`wa_seen_marks.direction='in'`) inside the audience window, since we could not read what they said (R-01);
  - phones with a live `contact_optouts` row, any channel or scope;
  - phones that `QuoteChase::offerHolds()`/`offerHold()` name (§H.2.10.10): an open tracked quotation, an open quote
    follow-up, a quote chase claimed in the ledger within 48 h and not settled `not_sent` (`sent`, `uncertain` or
    still in flight), or a quotation sent within 48 h, read from its own `wa_messages` row, tracked or not
    (B13-01), on any conversation of the phone (ruling R3);
  - phones that `HumanTakeover::phonesSince()`/`phoneSince()` name (§H.2.7.1; ruling R3);
  - phones with an inbound `media_type='audio'` row within `offers_warm_days`. No voice stop mark exists or is built (`VoiceStopMarks` is dropped), and the any-source `contact_optouts` read above already includes Part V's `voice_keyword` rows (ruling R3).

**H.2.6.6 Not recorded, on purpose**

- AI replies (`AiReplyWorker::handle`, `maybeSendPhoto`, `maybeSendDocument`, `maybeSendFlyer`), and the hand-over holding line (`AiReplyWorker::escalate` at `221c9dc`, carried by Part V into `lib/Handover.php`'s `escalate`): replies are not counted (D12).
- A person's sends: the Inbox's channel route (`NotificationService::sendOnChannel`, `:2200`, `:2269-2270`), its sender route (filtered by event, §H.2.6.1), and the manual pages `tabs/sales/wa_leads.php:72` and `tabs/engage/whatsapp.php:321`.
- **`WaMessageProcessor`'s `DishNet Bot` acknowledgement is recorded**, correcting the first round: it goes through `sendRaw` → `sendVia` with event `wa_media_ack` (`lib/WaMessageProcessor.php:215-220`; `lib/NotificationService.php:1871-1874`), so the hook files it as `other`. Whether it runs on Uganda is not established; Part V's VA-ON1 counts its rows.

**H.2.6.7 The inventory of send sites (HK7)**

A test greps the merged tree for every `->sendText(`, `->sendImage(`, `->sendDocument(` and `->sendMedia(` call on an Evolution service, and fails on any site not in one of these classes. **Sites are classified by file and method (or top level), never by live line number** (ruling R10), so Part V's hunks move no entry:

| Class | Sites (file: method) |
|---|---|
| hooked (record) | `lib/NotificationService.php`: `sendViaEvolution`, `sendMediaViaEvolution` (through `sendVia`, `sendDocument`, `sendImage`); `lib/AlertService.php`: `sendTo`; `workers/StarlinkMailWorker.php`: `notifyCustomer` (through `recordDirect()`, on the worker's PDO; A11-05) |

#### H.2.7 "A person took over" (C7), and what the webhook cannot store

**H.2.7.1 `lib/HumanTakeover.php`**

```php
final class HumanTakeover
{
    const INBOX_EVENTS = ['wa_staff_reply', 'wa_send_document'];   // the Inbox's own row, sent_at UTC (includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:249-253, :279-284)
    const LOCAL_EVENTS = ['wa_image_send', 'wa_media_send'];       // the Inbox's own row, sent_at by date(), Kampala (:1004-1009, :1040-1045)
    const AUTOMATION_LABELS = ['', 'DishNet', 'DishNet Plugin', 'DishNet AI', 'DishNet Bot'];   // plus ConversationService::AGENT_AUTO_REPLY
    public static function personEvents(): array { return array_merge(self::INBOX_EVENTS, self::LOCAL_EVENTS); }
    /** The first sign since $sinceUtc that a person on our side acted for this customer: a code, or null. */
    public static function since(\PDO $pdo, string $phone, array $convIds, string $sinceUtc): ?string
    /** since() over every conversation of $phone except category='staff', each clause also bounded by $untilUtc (ruling R3). */
    public static function phoneSince(\PDO $pdo, string $phone, string $sinceUtc, ?string $untilUtc = null): ?string
    /** The same for every phone at once: international digits ⇒ the first code; a phone with none is absent; an unreadable stamp maps every covered phone to 'unreadable_time' (ruling R3). */
    public static function phonesSince(\PDO $pdo, string $sinceUtc, ?string $untilUtc = null): array
}
```

**Every time argument is normalised first (ruling R3).** `since()`, `phoneSince()` and `phonesSince()` pass `$sinceUtc` and `$untilUtc` through `UtcClock::stamp(UtcClock::parse($s))` (`lib/UtcClock.php:31-45`, the parser the live worker already uses for `received_at`, `workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1432`). The compared columns are `Y-m-d H:i:s` UTC (`lib/ConversationService.php:817`; the `datetime('now')` defaults), and a `gmdate('c')` value's `T` sorts after the space, so without this a person later the same day would compare as older and be missed. An unreadable stamp (parse 0) makes every form answer the code `unreadable_time`, never null and never an empty answer (ruling R3): `since()` and `phoneSince()` return it, and `phonesSince()` returns it **for every phone it covers** — each phone of a conversation outside `category='staff'` — so a caller that leaves out each phone the map names leaves out every customer. A bad argument sends less, never more.

The `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php` lines cited in this section are at `221c9dc` and are re-made against the merged tree (ruling R10).

**"Ours"** is written NULL-safely, never as a bare `NOT IN` (S2-02, K2-12):
- for a `wa_messages` row: `(m.wa_message_id IS NULL OR m.wa_message_id NOT IN (SELECT wa_message_id FROM wa_auto_sends WHERE wa_message_id IS NOT NULL))`. The `wa_message_id` index is unique (`migrations/017_wa_conversation_store.sql:73-74`), so a row's id is never also an automation row's;
- for a mark (its id is never NULL): not in the ledger's ids, **and** not the id of a `wa_messages` row whose `role='assistant'` or whose `agent_name` is an automation label. That covers an AI photo or document sent without a caption whose echo beat its claim: the AI stores its own row under that id (`workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1179-1185`), while W1 has already marked it.

**A table that does not exist reads as empty (A11-02).** `wa_auto_sends` and `wa_seen_marks` are 089's. On a book
without them (the 088-shaped copy that QF-N3's report reads, QF-G1, and C6 step 1's report run before the deploy)
every form first reads `sqlite_master` for the two names and leaves out each clause over one that is absent: the
"not ours" subquery and a mark's ledger test without `wa_auto_sends` (no automation id exists before 089), and
`handset_media` without `wa_seen_marks` (no mark exists before 089). That is exactly what each table, present and
empty, gives, so the answer is never a guess; every other clause reads older tables (`wa_messages`, 017; `events`,
001). HT19 is its weakened copy.

`since()` returns the first of:
- **`team_message`:** a `wa_messages` row in `$convIds` with `direction='out'`, `role='agent'`, `agent_name='Team'`, `sent_at > since`, not ours;
- **`inbox_reply`:** a `wa_messages` row in `$convIds` with `direction='out'`, `role='agent'`, an `event_key` in `INBOX_EVENTS` with `sent_at > since`, or in `LOCAL_EVENTS` with `sent_at` read in a literal Kampala zone and converted to UTC (never "+3"), **and `agent_name` not an automation label**. That is the Inbox's own row, whose name is the staff member's (`api_whatsapp.php:244`, `:251`). In sender mode it has no `wa_message_id` (`lib/InboxReplyRoute.php:91-97`), which the NULL-safe test keeps. The parallel `DishNet Plugin` row that `sendVia` stores for the same reply (`lib/NotificationService.php:2425-2442`) is excluded by its label, so one reply is counted once;
- **`handset_media`:** a `wa_seen_marks` row with `direction='out'`, this phone, a channel among the conversations' channels, `seen_at > since`, not ours;
- **`escalated`:** a conversation in `$convIds` in state `needs_human` with an `events` row (`event_type='wa.escalation'`, `entity_type='conversation'`, `entity_id` = it, `created_at > since`; `migrations/001_event_queue.sql:13-30`).

**Never a person:**
- `DishNet` — enquiry follow-ups, and imports (`lib/ConversationService.php:1218`);
- `DishNet Plugin`, `DishNet AI`, `DishNet Bot`;
- `role='assistant'`;
- the auto-reply (`lib/ConversationService.php:22`).

**The state `human_active` on its own never counts (R104-02).** It never returns to `bot_active` on the release: the only reset is `cron_wa_bot.php`, whose job is disabled (`cron/master.php:229`). Every writer of `human_active` stores a person's row in the same request:
- `evo_webhook.php:197-205` then `:221`;
- `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:249-257`, `:1004-1013` and `:1040-1049`.

So the row and mark rules see exactly the people the state saw, bounded in time, without the false positives.

**Residual, recorded.** An AI **text** reply whose echo beats its claim is stored as `Team` today, and the AI's own row under the same id is then dropped as a duplicate. That is the live race (`evo_webhook.php:197-221`), and such a row reads as a person here, as it does to the live stand-down. It is not measurable from the book, and 5.18.104 does not change it.

**`ConversationService::humanRepliedSince` is not used** (`:962-977`): it counts `DishNet` rows.

Who passes which conversations:
- **P2** passes every conversation whose phone is exactly `p`, excluding `category='staff'`.
- **P5** (Part V) passes the one conversation, with `since` = the voice note's `received_at` **− 30 min** (ruling R4, R104-03, R-10): a colleague's text or W1 mark just before the voice note stands P5 down, which fails towards sending less. HT14 and Part V's A32 pin that one value.
- **P6** (Part O) calls `phonesSince()` for its audience and `phoneSince($pdo, $phone, judged_at − 72 h, judged_at)` for
  its check C-O2-9, at the recipient's `judged_at` (ruling R18; IO-5). **These forms are `since()`'s clauses exactly**,
  over every conversation of the phone except `category='staff'`, with the upper bound applied to every clause on each
  source's storage time: a row's `created_at`, a mark's `seen_at` and an event's `created_at` ≤ until (ruling R18). The
  lower bound stays each clause's own (`sent_at`, `seen_at`, `created_at` > since). Part O's extra
  `human_active`/`last_human_reply_at` clause is dropped: every live writer of `human_active` stores a person's row in
  the same request (above), so the row rules already see it, time-bounded. Part O's `wa_offers K` builds its
  `human_active` and escalation fixtures through those real writers and proves parity with `since()` on one fixture
  (ruling R3).

**H.2.7.2 `lib/WaSeenMarks.php`**

```php
final class WaSeenMarks
{
    const WRAPPERS = ['ephemeralMessage','viewOnceMessage','viewOnceMessageV2','viewOnceMessageV2Extension','documentWithCaptionMessage'];
    const MEDIA    = ['audioMessage','imageMessage','documentMessage','videoMessage','stickerMessage'];
    public static function kindOf(array $msg, string $direction): ?string;   // pure: in → a WRAPPERS key; out → WRAPPERS or MEDIA
    public static function note(\PDO $pdo, array $config, ?string $dataDir, string $direction, string $phone, string $channel,
                                string $instance, string $waMessageId, array $msg): void;   // never throws
    public static function noNumber(\PDO $pdo, array $config, ?string $dataDir, string $channel, string $instance, string $waMessageId): void;
}
```

- `kindOf` looks for the keys, never at `array_keys()[0]`, which can be `messageContextInfo`. Reactions, protocol messages, edits and polls give `null`, so they leave no mark.
- `note` tests `wa_send_ledger === 'on'` first, then `StaffJobsGate`, then `kindOf`, then does `INSERT OR IGNORE`. No text is ever stored.
- A test asserts `WRAPPERS ⊇` the wrapper list at `dev:lib/InboundMedia.php:34`, and `⊇` Part V's ported `InboundMedia::WRAPPERS`.
- The marks are written from step 2 on, when the ledger comes on, so P5 and the tracker see them from the start.

**H.2.7.3 Three hunks in `evo_webhook.php`** (the same commit as Part V's step 8c)

**W1 — R-07**, in the `fromMe` branch, after `$ownText` (`:183`) and before the stored-text branch (`:184`). **It is the only 5.18.104 hunk in that branch (K2-09, S2-15).** Part V's alternative — storing an `[AUDIO]`/`[IMAGE]` `Team` row and calling `markHumanHandling` — is not in 5.18.104. It would make tracking (step 3, "sends nothing") change the AI's behaviour, against D4. It would also stand the AI down for `wa_human_cooldown_minutes` (`workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1374-1386`) on the plugin's own captionless media echoes that beat their claim. Whether the AI should stand down when a colleague answers with media is an owner question (§H.2.20 OQ3), and would be its own later switch.

```php
// 5.18.104 (root docs/72 §H.2.7, R-07): a colleague who answers from the handset with a voice note, a photo or a document
// without a caption leaves no stored message (the store below needs text). On Uganda, with the ledger on, a content-free
// mark says a person wrote to this customer — no text, no file, no state — so a quote chase and the voice-note
// acknowledgement stop. Our own sends are told apart when the mark is read (HumanTakeover), not here.
if ($custPhone !== '' && $ownText === '') {
    require_once __DIR__ . '/lib/WaSeenMarks.php';
    WaSeenMarks::note($pdo, $config, $dataDir, 'out', $custPhone, $channel, $instance, $messageId, $msg);
}
```

**What reaches W1, stated correctly (K2-24).** Every sender claims its echo **immediately after its POST returns**:
- `cron/followup_send.php:170-180`;
- `lib/NotificationService.php:1957-1962`, `:1996-2001` and `:2273-2278`;
- `workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1448-1463`.

An echo that arrives sooner wins the webhook's claim (`evo_webhook.php:163-166`) and reaches this branch. `evoExtractText` reads top-level keys only (`:465-484`), so a captioned PDF that arrives as `documentWithCaptionMessage` has no `$ownText` and is marked. The mark carries the message id. `HumanTakeover` excludes it **when it reads the mark**, by then finding the id in the ledger (every recorded and claimed send stores it, §H.2.5.8) or on the AI's own row (§H.2.7.1). W1 stores nothing in `wa_messages`, sets no state, and leaves what the AI reads unchanged.

**W2 — R-01**, after step 8 (`:271-277`) and before 8a (`:279`):

```php
// 5.18.104 (root docs/72 §H.2.7, R-01): a disappearing or view-once message is not stored (importEvoMessage reads top-level
// keys only, lib/ConversationService.php:1163-1199), so a reply or a STOP inside one is invisible. A content-free mark
// records that this customer wrote; the chase treats it as a reply. Not unwrapped here (§H.2.7.4).
if ($convId === null && $text === '') {
    require_once __DIR__ . '/lib/WaSeenMarks.php';
    WaSeenMarks::note($pdo, $config, $dataDir, 'in', $phone, $channel, $instance, $messageId, $msg);
}
```

A plain media message that `cron_evo_sync` stored first gives `kindOf('in') = null`, so it leaves no mark.

**W3 — counting only.** The `@lid` inbound with no number (`:236`) becomes:

```php
if ($phone === '') {
    require_once __DIR__ . '/lib/WaSeenMarks.php';
    WaSeenMarks::noNumber($pdo, $config, $dataDir, $channel, $instance, $messageId);   // 5.18.104 (§H.2.7): counted only
    $skipped++; continue;
}
```

It writes `phone=''`, `kind='lid_no_number'`. **What reads it (K2-26):** the R-01 measurement that `on chase` prints (§H.2.7.4) and the report's marks-per-day line (§H.2.8.2). It is how often a customer wrote in a way no rule can attribute to a phone, which bounds the chase's "any reply stops it". Nothing else reads it.

On South Sudan the key is never set (the tool refuses there), so every hunk does nothing and requires nothing.

**H.2.7.4 R-01, decided: measured first, a mark rather than an unwrap**

- **The measurement before the chase (step 6).** Stage A counts the existing log line, `no text to answer — <key> message stored` (`evo_webhook.php:383`), for the wrapper keys, where the PHP log is readable (QF-N6). From step 2, the marks count it exactly. `on chase` prints, over the tracking period:
  - the inbound marks per day and per handset;
  - the tracked quotes whose customer has an inbound mark after `sent_at`;
  - the handset marks per day;
  - `lid_no_number` per day.
- **The rule.** An inbound mark after `sent_at` stops a quote as **`answered`**, reason `unread_inbound`, both in the tracker and in `preSendCheck`. The quote goes on its owner's list: "replied — open WhatsApp, the message could not be read here". A STOP inside a wrapper therefore stops the chase too.
- **Not unwrapped behind the chase gate:**
  - an unwrap feeds every wrapped text to the AI at step 9 (`evo_webhook.php:389-407`), which changes the assistant's replies on the day the chase is switched on — two changes in one step, against D4;
  - the chase needs only to know that the customer wrote;
  - offers exclude marked phones (§H.2.6.5);
  - reminders keep today's behaviour, the known F28 limit;
  - the unwrap stays F28, its own Uganda switch in a later release.
- **Precondition of `on chase`:** the W2 hunk is installed (checked on the installed file's text) and `wa_seen_marks` exists. The deploy's after-copy check (QF-CA8) runs a synthetic wrapped payload through the installed webhook code on a copy and finds the mark: the positive control.

#### H.2.8 P1 — the read-only report

**H.2.8.1 What it answers, and the definitions**

Unchanged from the first-round draft's §9.1–9.3, kept word for word in §H.2.21. Per number and per owner, over 30 and 90 days:
- conversations, inbound customers and new ones;
- quotes sent, and those from a registration;
- answered, chased (by the engine and by a person) and **neither** — the headline;
- registered, paid, opted out (before answered, F27).

The windows are UTC. Dates print in Africa/Kampala. Staff-filed conversations, `web:` sessions and DishNet's own numbers are excluded everywhere.

"Chased by a person" uses **`HumanTakeover`'s row and mark rules**, the same code as the tracker, so the two agree by construction.

On a book without 089's tables (the 088-shaped copy of QF-N3, and C6 step 1 run before the deploy) it reads them
through `HumanTakeover`'s absent-table rule (§H.2.7.1), so "chased by a person" and the headline print numbers
there, never `UNKNOWN`; only the lines §H.2.8.2 adds after the deploy print `UNKNOWN` (A11-02).

**H.2.8.2 Output**

Counts only. The masked business numbers show their last two digits (`tools/channels.php:88`). A missing source prints `UNKNOWN`, never 0.

**Owners print as `owner 1…n`.** The mapping `owner n = staff #id` goes to a mode-0600 sheet, `/root/dnb-report/owners-<UTC stamp>.txt`, never to the log. That is 5.18.103's rule: no staff id in the log.

After the deploy it adds:
- the tracker's parity, as Q1-ON states it (§H.2.12.5; Q17-F04);
- the ledger per handset (role and index), with the true total;
- the marks per day, `lid_no_number` included;
- stops by reason.

**H.2.8.3 How it cannot write (F17)**

- It never calls `SqliteStore::create` (`lib/SqliteStore.php:233-248`).
- It opens one connection to a `VACUUM INTO` copy, `SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY`, `immutable=1`, `PRAGMA query_only=ON`. Every statement is a single SELECT or WITH inside BEGIN…ROLLBACK, and the run fails unless `total_changes()` is 0. The precedent is `scripts/bank-recon-p0.php` (repository root). It is **not** `tools/cash_in_hand.php:29-31`, which calls `SqliteStore::create` (R104-20).
- Its includes are pure or read-only: `PhoneNumber`, `TenantProfile`, `PluginConfig::read`, `ContactOptOut::detect`, `QuoteSendEvidence`, `HumanTakeover` (SELECTs only) with the pure `UtcClock` it normalises times with (ruling R3).
  `WaSendBudget` is built by `onConnection()` on that one connection and asked only for `counts()` (§H.2.5.1).

**H.2.8.4 The tenant, from copies (R104-18)**

`scripts/sales-followup-report.sh` places beside the copy, in its mode-700 folder:
- copies of `data/config.json`, the data folder's `config.json` and `kyc_config.json`;
- a vault holding only `tenant_profile`, `currency_code`, `currency_symbol`, `cashbook_base_currency` and `cashbook_currencies`.

It sets `DN_VAULT_FILE` to that vault and runs the tool on a code root in the same folder whose data directory is that folder. That is 5.18.103's "ON COPIES" practice (`scripts/deploy-5.18.103.sh` header). The tool prints which file decided the tenant. Anything but Uganda prints `not this install — nothing read`.

**H.2.8.5 The wrapper and the command**

The rest is the first-round draft's §9.5, kept in §H.2.21:
- the files come from Git at the reviewed commit, sha256-checked;
- the installed `PhoneNumber`, `TenantProfile`, `PluginConfig`, `ConfigVault` and `ContactOptOut` are asserted equal to that commit's bytes;
- it checks free space, makes the copy, runs `integrity_check`, sets `journal_mode=DELETE`, runs PHP with `-d log_errors=0`, and removes everything through a trap.

The operator's single command ends `| ( umask 077; exec tee /root/dnb-report/report-<stamp>.log )`. The operator sends back the **log file**. There is no rollback, because nothing changes.

#### H.2.9 P2a — quote tracking (`lib/QuoteTracker.php`, run by `cron/quote_chase.php`)

**H.2.9.1 Evidence**

`QuoteSendEvidence::EVENTS` is `ops_quote_created`, `ops_quote_wa`, `ops_quote_text`, `quote_kyc`, `quote_lead` and `quote_manual`. A test asserts it equals `NotificationRetry::EVENTS`' quote subset minus `quote_cash` (`lib/NotificationRetry.php:32`).

A row confirms a quote when it is outbound, its event is in the list, and its body carries one of three markers with the number:

| Marker | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `📋 *Ref:* ` | `lib/QuotationService.php:513` |
| `🆔 *Order:* ` | `webhook.php:3002` |
| `📄 *Quote #` | `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:665,674` |

`sendDocument` never writes `wa_messages`, so a PDF is never evidence.

**H.2.9.2 Identity and mapping**

- `quote_key = 'ref:'` + the number, trimmed, with a leading `#` removed.
- `quote_id` is the first of:
  - `wa_sent_quotes.quote_ref` (`lib/QuoteWaLedger.php:21-42`);
  - `quotes_log $.quote_ref` → `$.crm_quote_id`;
  - `kyc_applications $.quote_ref` → `$.quote_id`, ignoring `'PENDING'` (`lib/KycService.php:2781`).
- The earliest confirming row wins (`INSERT OR IGNORE`).
- A clash on `idx_qt_quote_id` (the insert ignored, and no row of that key) is `ref_conflict`: the run records it
  once as the `quote_followup_state` key `ref_conflict:<quote_key>`, its `v` the `quote_id` it clashed on (Q17-F04).
- The cursor is the `quote_followup_state` key `tracker_cursor`, the largest `wa_messages.id` a run has read. A
  run reads up to 500 ids past it, inside the job budget, and writes it in the transaction that inserts the tracker
  rows and `ref_conflict` records for the rows it read, never before them (Q17-F04). `wa_messages.id` is
  AUTOINCREMENT (live `migrations/017_wa_conversation_store.sql:55`), so a row committed after the cursor was
