About 10–13 working days, plus the deploy checks and the rehearsal cases.

### H.4 Part O — offers on the Evolution numbers (P6, D11)

#### H.4.1 What P6 is, and what binds it

**The decision (D11, the owner, 4 Nov):** offers on the Evolution numbers, the careful way. A daily batch goes only to customers who chatted in the last 30 days, from the number they chatted on, with varied wording, STOP on each message, and an image allowed. The admin chooses 100, 200 or all; "all" goes over days within each number's daily limit, never at once. Offers are designed with the chase so that the two share one daily limit and one spacing per number. They ship OFF.

Related decisions:
- **D12:** at most 60 automatic messages per number per day; chases come first and offers use what is left.
- **D10:** Evolution until an official WhatsApp Business Platform number exists.

**Binding:**
- **The shared contract, C1–C10.** Where the first-round material differs, the contract wins:
  - the ledger is `wa_auto_sends` / `lib/WaSendBudget.php` (C3), used through Part F's one call contract (F §H.2.5.8, ruling R2), restated in §H.4.14;
  - the switches are switched by `tools/sales_followup.php` and declared, rows and settings alike, in the one ladder `SalesFollowupLadder`, in `lib/SalesFollowupLadder.php` (Part F's file; C1, ruling R5). The tool reads that table unchanged, and P6 adds nothing to the tool. P6's steps are **`offers-test`** (step 11, O1) and **`offers-live`** (step 12, O2) (C6);
  - the migration is 091 (C2). It repeats 089's `_schema_checks` CREATE byte for byte and verifies itself into that table (ruling R9);
  - the job is `offers_send`, written `'interval' => 240` (amendment A-C5-1: C5's 300 s period on master's ~300 s heartbeat), the last of the four new lines in `$_m_jobs`, with `'uganda' => true` and `'flag' => 'offers_live_enabled'` (C5, ruling R1, §H.4.13);
  - "a person took over" has one meaning, Part F's `HumanTakeover` (C7). P6 has no predicate of its own.
- **The coordinator's rulings R1–R19 (4 Nov)** amend the contract and override this part's earlier text where they
  differ. Each change they made here names its ruling. **A ruling is cited as "ruling R1" to "ruling R19"**, as
  Parts F and V cite them, so that it is never read as one of C6's voice rungs R1–R4 (steps 5, 7, 8 and 9), which
  alone keep the bare labels.
- **The approved wording (§H.1, verbatim):** the STOP line on every offer is **"Reply STOP to stop these messages."** §H.1 approves no offer wording, so the admin writes the wordings and the code adds only this line.

**Base and scope:**
- Base `221c9dc` (5.18.103). Paths are under `dishnet-hybrid-sudan/` on `release/5.18.103` unless marked `dev:`. PHP 7.4 compatible throughout.
- **What P6 does not do:**
  - no e-mail;
  - no uCRM call of any kind (P6 reads only the plugin's own store);
  - no Meta code;
  - no message to a customer who did not write in the window, and none from a number other than the one the customer last wrote on;
  - no new event type, so `cron/event_processor.php` is untouched;
  - **P6 itself changes none of** `evo_webhook.php`, `lib/ContactOptOut.php`, `lib/EvolutionApiService.php`, `lib/NotificationService.php`, `lib/FlyerAsset.php` or `tools/set_config.php`. Parts F and V change some of these under their own declared hunks (§H.4.4).

#### H.4.2 Decisions

| # | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| O-D1 | At most **one live offer** at a time (state `running` or `paused`), enforced by a partial UNIQUE index on `live_slot`. | One queue per handset is easy to pace, prove and pause. A second offer would find most of its audience excluded by the 7-day rule anyway. |
| O-D2 | The audience is **frozen at Start** as a snapshot, warmest first. Every recipient is **judged again just before its own send**. Nothing is added after Start. | "All" runs over days. In that time a customer may opt out, write in, be chased or cool down. |
| O-D3 | The offer goes from the **conversation the customer last wrote on, on an Evolution number**. If that number may not send (a partner's number, a salesperson's own number, or refused by the policy), the customer is **left out, never moved** to another number. The handset is the ledger's key, `WaSendBudget::handset(instance)` (`'i:'` + lower(trim)), and P6 stores it in that form. | D11, "from the number they chatted on". Warm only, never cold. One spelling of the handset across parts (S2-03, K2-05). |
| O-D4 | **One message per recipient**: the image with the wording and the STOP line as its caption, or the text alone. | One send is one ledger claim and one echo. Two messages would double the ban exposure and the echo risk. |
| O-D5 | The STOP line is §H.1's line, **appended by code and stamped on the offer row**. A wording that already says "STOP" is refused. | STOP on each message (D11), with no doubled or altered line. |
| O-D6 | **Two or three wordings**, each 20–900 characters and distinct after case and whitespace are folded. They are used in turn, per handset. | "Varied wording" (D11). 900 characters plus the line stays under WhatsApp's 1,024-character caption. |
| O-D7 | Every customer send claims `WaSendBudget` kind **`offer`** with **the recipient's phone** and a ref **stable per recipient**, `offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>`, never per attempt. The ledger's own try count counts the attempts; P6's `attempt` column serves only its own row CAS (ruling R2). It is settled afterwards with the message id. A **may-have-been-sent** is settled `failed` with `maybe_sent`, stored `uncertain`: counted, never sent again (ruling R2). | C3: the ledger is idempotent per `(kind, ref)`, so it is the floor beneath P6's row CAS, and a crash can lose one recipient but never send twice. Part F's one-message-per-person-per-day rule needs the phone (S2-04, K2-07). `HumanTakeover` recognises our sends by the ledger's id (K2-08). |
| O-D8 | At most **one offer per handset per run**. A run starts sends only while `JobBudget` allows: at most 35 s, **never past master's deadline**. A send starts only with 15 s left, the Evolution timeout. | Never a burst. The cycle stays inside master's budget (S2-16, K2-14). |
| O-D9 | The window is **the ledger's `WaSendBudget::window($config)`**: by default 08:00–20:00, Monday to Saturday, read in a literal `Africa/Kampala`; the owner may narrow it, never widen it. `OfferWindow::open`/`nextOpen` delegate to it (ruling R8). **A send must also end inside it:** every offer claim carries P6's in-flight bound, `in_flight_s` 50, and the ledger answers `window`, retry at the next opening, when the claim's moment plus that bound passes the window's close (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 2; §H.4.10, the in-flight bound). The ledger row records the window the claim was judged by (`win_from`, `win_to`), and C-O2-2 judges each send by its ledger row's `claimed_at`, that recorded window and the 50 s bound (ruling R18). The sender also refuses to run unless `dn_tz()` is `Africa/Kampala`. | One window for every proactive kind: a narrowed setting binds offers' pre-filter, their release times and every later claim, never a claim already made, which keeps the window it recorded (ruling R18). **The claim and C-O2-2 judge the same instant, the same window and the same bound** (B11-01): judged at the claim alone, a send claimed at 19:59:55 could return after 20:00; judged by today's settings, a send correct when made could read FAIL; and C-O2-2's FAIL can never be accepted (Part F §H.2.12.3). R-16: a stored `timezone`, or the `Africa/Juba` fallback, would otherwise move the window. |
| O-D10 | A test goes to **the admin's own phone of record**, never a typed number. It is sent as class `staff` and **recorded after the send** as ledger kind `other`, record-only and never claimed. **Every wording of the current content** must have a sent test, recorded in the ledger, before Start (C-O1-1). | Step `offers-test`. The admin sees exactly what a customer will see, from the real handset. Part F does not let kind `other` be claimed (S2-13, K2-06). |
| O-D11 | Reuse **`EvolutionApiService::sendMedia`/`sendText` and `FlyerAsset::payload`**, the path the AI's flyer takes. **Not** `NotificationService::sendImage`. | §H.4.3 explains why. |
| O-D12 | A sent offer is stored in its conversation as role `agent`, with **`agent_name 'DishNet Plugin'`** and `event_key 'wa_offer'`. | `humanRepliedSince` excludes that name (`lib/ConversationService.php:966-968`), so an offer is never "a colleague replied" to the AI (R-10). |
| O-D13 | **Auto-pause** when STOP reaches `offers_stop_pause_pct` (default 5 %) of an offer's sends, once at least 40 have gone. An offer **ends after `offers_max_days`** (default 14). | Ban and goodwill guards. Each threshold is a setting the owner can change. |
| O-D14 | The sender works through a small **`OfferGateway` interface**. Evolution is the only driver now. | Modelled on ShopBot's `WhatsAppGateway` / `EvolutionGateway` / `CloudApiGateway` (root `docs/12-shopbot-inspection.md:83-88`). D10 adds the official number later, for offers only. |
| O-D15 | **On a Kampala day, no offer goes while Part F's `ReminderDay::done()` is false**: before that day's payment reminders and win-back have run (master's `customer_reminders`), or before their window has closed. One rule, Part F's; P6 has none of its own (ruling R8). | Reminders are record-only and never deferred, so a customer offered something at 08:30 would otherwise be reminded at 09:00. Once they have run, the ledger's per-person rule sees their rows (S2-08). The ledger's `reminders_first` binds every offer claim anyway. |
| O-D16 | Who is left out because a person, or something unreadable, is involved comes from Part F: **`HumanTakeover`** for a person (C7), and **`wa_seen_marks`** for a message that arrived but could not be read. P6 adds two rules of its own: a **hold after an inbound voice note for the whole warm window** (`offers_warm_days`, ruling R3), and a **stop-word scan at any length** over the warm window. | One meaning of C7 (K2-10). A wrapped, voiced or long STOP must not be offered past (S2-06, S2-07). No part records what a voice note said for offers to read, so an unheard note holds the phone for as long as it could matter (ruling R3). |
| O-D17 | **Every phone list is compared in one form**: international digits, from `PhoneNumber::international` with the `+` removed. The ledger stores its phone column in that same form itself, for every kind (ruling R2). | Partner contacts and staff numbers are stored in several forms (S2-05). The one-message-per-person-per-day rule compares the ledger's phones across senders. |
| O-D18 | **The echo's outcome is recorded in the row at the send**: `claimed`, `late` or `none`. | The webhook's echo table is pruned after 72 h, so a later check cannot rely on it (K2-17). |
| O-D19 | An offer sends only if **its latest Start or Resume is later than the moment `offers-live` was last switched on** (`offers_live_since`). | A running offer can never resume by itself after an off and on, even if an off-hook did not run (K2-15). |

#### H.4.3 What the live release already gives P6 (read, not changed by P6)

**The image send path:**
- **`EvolutionApiService::sendImage`** (`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:684-687`) is `sendMedia($channel, $phone, 'image', $media, $caption)` with the default class, proactive. `sendMedia` (`:655-682`):
  - checks the opt-out first (`optOutRefusal`, `:99-108`, which uses `ContactOptOut::blocks`);
  - then checks the automated-send policy (`policyRefusal`, `:286-295`; registry on only; classes `reply`/`proactive`, `:231`);
  - then resolves the instance and POSTs `/message/sendMedia/{instance}`, with `media` as a URL or as base64.
- **`sendText`** (`:633-649`) does the same for text.
- On Uganda every POST goes through `requestUg` (`:813` onwards):
  - a POST that may have left is never repeated;
  - a POST whose attempt never left is tried again, up to three attempts (`:838-846`), so one send's POST can
    take 31.6 s at P6's 15 s client timeout (§H.4.10, the in-flight bound);
  - its error begins "May have been sent — " (`:50`), which `mayHaveBeenSent` (`:778-783`) reads;
  - a policy refusal is marked `policy_refused` (`policyRefused`/`policyReason`, `:274-283`);
  - an opt-out refusal is `suppressed => true`, with no `ok` key (`:105-107`).
- **`lib/FlyerAsset.php`:** `EXTS` jpg/jpeg/png/webp (`:23-28`); `MAX_FILE_BYTES` 4 MB (`:31`); `payload()`, the base64 of a file under the data directory (`:66-75`).
- **The AI's flyer goes exactly this way:** `FlyerAsset::payload` (`workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1282`), then `$this->evo->sendImage(...)` (`:1289`), then `claimOwnEcho` (`:1296`; the method is at `:1448-1463`). The AI's photos do the same (`:1171`). `lib/MediaLibrary.php:37-48` uses the same extensions and the same 4 MB ceiling.
- **`NotificationService::sendImage` is NOT used** (`lib/NotificationService.php:1781-1865`):
  - it takes a public URL that Evolution must fetch;
  - it maps only `support`/`accounts` (`evoChannelFor`, `:1892-1899`);
  - it writes the Message Log with the recipient's number (`:1848-1856`);
  - it queues every failure for the automatic retry (`queueFailed`, `:1858-1864`), which the `notify_retry` job sends later (`cron/master.php:301`), outside the ledger and outside the window.

  Its `sendMediaViaEvolution` (`:1984-2006`) does show the rule P6 keeps: it claims the echo straight after the call returns (`:1995-2002`).

**The echo:**
- Evolution posts every outbound message back as fromMe. The webhook drops an id that was already claimed (`evo_webhook.php:163-166`).
- Any other fromMe **text** is stored as `'Team'` and calls `markHumanHandling` (`:180-224`, text only at `:184`; `lib/ConversationService.php:979-993`). That stands the AI down for `wa_human_cooldown_minutes`, 1,440 by default (`workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1374-1386`).
- An image's caption is read as its text (`evo_webhook.php:465-485`), so an offer, which always carries text, takes the text path.
- The rule is "claim our own echo FIRST — before storing, before bookkeeping" (`cron/followup_send.php:170-180`), through `EvoWebhookGuard::claim` (`lib/EvoWebhookGuard.php:163-185`). The claim returns **false** when the id is already there: the echo came first, and may already have been stored as `'Team'`.
- **`evo_webhook_seen` is pruned to 72 hours**, on about one request in 200 (`evo_webhook.php:455`; `lib/EvoWebhookGuard.php:187-191`).

**Phone forms (S2-05):**
- Conversation phones are digits only (`EvolutionApiService::normalisePhone`/`phoneFromJid`, `lib/EvolutionApiService.php:747-757`).
- A partner contact is stored as typed once it has 7 or more digits. `normPhone` keeps a leading `+` (`lib/DistributorNotifier.php:71-76`, `:88-92`), and there is no international conversion, although migration 080's comment says "normalised international" (`migrations/080_distributor_notifications.sql:30`).
- `StaffDirectory::phoneOf` returns `PhoneNumber::international`, which is the `+` form (`lib/StaffDirectory.php:100-105`). `NotificationService` strips that `+` (`lib/NotificationService.php:2081-2082`).
- `InternalNumbers` converts configured numbers to international digits itself (`lib/InternalNumbers.php:387-396`, `:219-227`).
- `ContactOptOut::normalise` keeps digits only, in whatever form they were typed (`lib/ContactOptOut.php:253-256`).

**What can and cannot be read of a customer's message:**
- `ContactOptOut::detect` matches only a message of 40 characters or fewer (`lib/ContactOptOut.php:238-240`), against `STOP_WORDS` (`:45-51`).
- An inbound voice note is stored with body `[AUDIO]` and `media_type 'audio'` (`lib/ConversationService.php:1174`, `:1186-1190`).
- A wrapped (disappearing or view-once) message leaves no row (R-01).

**DishNet's own side:**
- **Staff and dealers:**
  - `StaffDirectory::activeStaffByPhone` (`lib/StaffDirectory.php:108-118`) knows active staff roles only (`:23`). Dealers (sales, retailer, field agent, collection) are not "staff" there.
  - `ColleagueNumbers::forInstall` / `isColleagueConversation` (`lib/ColleagueNumbers.php:28-54`).
- **DishNet lines and the people beside them:** `InternalNumbers::fromRows` + `useStore` + `senderClass($phone, false)` (`lib/InternalNumbers.php:115-137`, `:202-228`).
- **What needs a store, measured (ruling R13; §H.4.8):**
  - `InternalNumbers::fromRows()` takes `wa_channels` rows by channel id, never `retailers.json`
    (`lib/InternalNumbers.php:110-136`). The line owners (`retailers.json`), the stored settings (`kyc_config.json`)
    and the numbers Evolution reported (`wa_evo_numbers.json`) are read lazily through `useStore()`'s argument
    (`:202-212`, `:315-386`), which is anything with `load(file)`: the store, or a read-only stand-in such as
    `InternalNumbers::reader(\PDO)`, which reads only `wa_evo_numbers.json` straight from the database (`:143`,
    `:153-182`). No form of it takes `retailers.json` rows;
  - `EvolutionApiService::forStore($config, $pdo, $dataDir)` takes a PDO and no store
    (`lib/EvolutionApiService.php:179-206`); `instanceFor()` reads only the routing it built (`:410-413`);
    `useStaffStore()` hands its argument to the automation policy's line owners, and does nothing with the registry
    off (`:252-260`);
  - `new EvoWebhookGuard($pdo, $config)` runs `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in its constructor
    (`lib/EvoWebhookGuard.php:43-51`, `:215-235`), which a `query_only` connection refuses.
- **Partners:**
  - partner contacts are `dist_contacts.phone`;
  - partner-owned numbers are `wa_channels.owner_type = 'partner'` (`migrations/087_wa_channels.sql:25-27`).
- **The automated-send policy:** `AutomationPolicy::refusal` / `channelRefusal` / `transient` (`lib/AutomationPolicy.php:172-219`, `:287-290`), with `forInstall` (`:78-96`).

**The state a person leaves:**
- `humanRepliedSince` counts `DishNet` follow-up rows as a colleague (`lib/ConversationService.php:962-977`), so P6 never uses it (C7).
- `human_active` and `last_human_reply_at` are set by `markHumanHandling`.
- `needs_human` is set by the hand-over, with a `wa.escalation` event (`workers/AiReplyWorker.php:1578-1590`). It is never reset on the release (R104-02).
- An ambiguous identity is `crm_link_method = 'ambiguous'` (`lib/ConversationService.php:687-693`).

**The window:** `FollowUpPolicy::withinSendingWindow` (`lib/FollowUpPolicy.php:182-206`) uses `dn_tz_obj()`, so P6 does not reuse it (O-D9).

**The payment reminders (S2-08):**
- `customer_reminders` (`cron/master.php:295`) runs the reminders and the win-back (`cron/customer_reminders.php:1-10`, `:63`).
- It runs once a day, at the first cycle between `reminder_hour` (default 9) and `reminder_until_hour` (default 17), with master's validation (`cron/master.php:307-310`, `:341`; `lib/JobWindow.php:11-17`).
- The time zone is the one master sets with `dn_tz_apply()` (`cron/master.php:4`).
- Master writes the job's row in the store's `master_schedule.json` with `duration_ms -1` **before** the job runs, and the real duration after it (`:370-376`, `:400-406`).
- Part F's pure `ReminderDay::done()` judges these facts from the schedule it is given (Part F §H.2.5.3); it is the
  one reminders-first rule, and P6 calls it (ruling R8).

**The runner and master:**
- The deadline is set at `cron/master.php:109-110`. Dispatch stops only between jobs (`:318-321`).
- Every job is included in master's own scope (`:385`), so a closure in a job file sees `$_m_deadline` only if it is passed in.
- Each job has a 60 s time limit (`:377-382`), which does not count time spent waiting on curl or the database.
- The `notify_retry` comment records that an interval of exactly 300 can skip a cycle (`:298-301`).
- The `'flag'` rule for a job that exists only while its key is on is on the development tree (`dev:cron/master.php:333-336`), and Part F carries it into 5.18.104.
- **The migration runner:**
  - it always marks a file applied (`lib/MigrationRunner.php:243-247`);
  - its trigger splitter ends a body at any `end\b` with no left word boundary (`:113-121`);
  - it strips comments before the split (`:94`), so its swallow test sees each statement without them;
  - it swallows `already exists`, `duplicate column`, `UNIQUE constraint` and `NOT NULL constraint`; `no such column` only when the statement text contains "CREATE"; and **`no such table` only when the statement text contains "INDEX", in any case** (`:226-233`). An `INSERT` whose text says `type = 'index'` therefore passes silently against a missing table. §H.4.5 tests each error class of its INSERT (ruling R9).

#### H.4.5 Migration `091_wa_offers.sql`

**Shape.** The migration is additive and dark: four tables, seven indexes and fourteen triggers, plus 089's `_schema_checks` CREATE repeated byte for byte and one self-check row in that table (ruling R9). It runs on both installs, and South Sudan never writes a row. It contains no ALTER, no UPDATE and no DROP. It sorts after Part F's 089 and the voice part's 090.

**Rules for the runner:**
- **Triggers:** every trigger body is exactly `SELECT RAISE(ABORT, '<text>');`. The only words in a body are `SELECT` and `RAISE(ABORT, ...)`, and the text sits inside a string, which the splitter skips (`lib/MigrationRunner.php:104-121`). So no `CASE…END`, and no word ending in "end", can occur in a body.
- **The self-check.** 089's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _schema_checks` statement, which carries no inline comment, is repeated byte for byte immediately before 091's INSERT; one test compares the three texts of 089, 090 and 091 (ruling R9). The INSERT counts by name. Measured: the runner strips comments before the split (`:94`), and its swallow test swallows `no such column` only in a statement containing CREATE and `no such table` only in one containing INDEX (`:226-233`). The INSERT contains neither, and `wa_offers` A drives each error class through the runner (OM82) instead of relying on a word rule (ruling R9).

```sql
-- 091_wa_offers.sql — 5.18.104 P6 (root docs/72 §H.4, D11): offers on the Evolution numbers. Additive; read and
-- written only behind OfferSwitch (Uganda, offers_test_enabled / offers_live_enabled). South Sudan: empty tables.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_offers (
    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title          TEXT    NOT NULL,                    -- for staff only, never sent
    wording_1      TEXT    NOT NULL,
    wording_2      TEXT    NOT NULL,
    wording_3      TEXT,
    stop_line      TEXT    NOT NULL,                    -- OfferText::STOP_LINE, stamped at creation
    image_file     TEXT,                                -- basename in <data>/offer_images/, or NULL
    image_mime     TEXT,
    image_bytes    INTEGER,
    image_sha256   TEXT,
    content_hash   TEXT    NOT NULL,                    -- sha256 of the wordings, the stop line and image_sha256
    audience_size  TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '100',
    state          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft',
    live_slot      INTEGER,                             -- 1 while running or paused, else NULL (O-D1)
    warm_days      INTEGER,                             -- the settings in force at the start, recorded
    recent_days    INTEGER,
    queued_n       INTEGER,                             -- recipients in the snapshot
    created_by_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    created_by     TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_at     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    updated_at     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    started_at     TEXT,
    started_by     TEXT,
    closed_at      TEXT,
    closed_by      TEXT,
    close_reason   TEXT,                                -- stopped | done | expired | discarded
    CHECK (audience_size IN ('100', '200', 'all')),
    CHECK (state IN ('draft', 'running', 'paused', 'stopped', 'done')),
    CHECK (live_slot IS NULL OR live_slot = 1),
    CHECK ((state IN ('running', 'paused')) = (live_slot IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK (state IN ('draft', 'stopped') OR started_at IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (length(trim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 80),
    CHECK (length(wording_1) BETWEEN 20 AND 900 AND length(wording_2) BETWEEN 20 AND 900),
    CHECK (wording_3 IS NULL OR length(wording_3) BETWEEN 20 AND 900),
    CHECK (wording_2 <> wording_1 AND (wording_3 IS NULL OR (wording_3 <> wording_1 AND wording_3 <> wording_2))),
    CHECK ((image_file IS NULL AND image_sha256 IS NULL AND image_mime IS NULL AND image_bytes IS NULL)
        OR (image_file IS NOT NULL AND length(image_sha256) = 64
            AND image_mime IN ('image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp') AND image_bytes BETWEEN 1 AND 4194304))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wo_live  ON wa_offers(live_slot) WHERE live_slot IS NOT NULL;
CREATE INDEX        IF NOT EXISTS idx_wo_state ON wa_offers(state, id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_offer_recipients (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    offer_id        INTEGER NOT NULL,
    phone           TEXT,                               -- international digits of the Uganda number; NULL once erased (Part F's A20, ruling R10)
    rank            INTEGER NOT NULL,                   -- 1 = the most recent chat at the start
    conversation_id INTEGER NOT NULL,                   -- the conversation last written on (re-read at the send)
    channel         TEXT    NOT NULL,
    handset         TEXT    NOT NULL,                   -- WaSendBudget::handset(): 'i:' . lower(trim(instance)) (C3)
    last_in_at      TEXT    NOT NULL,                   -- UTC, the customer's last message on an Evolution number, at the start
    state           TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued',
    not_before      TEXT,                               -- UTC: a deferral
    attempt         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,         -- +1 at each claim, for this row's own CAS only; the ledger ref is offer:<offer_id>:<id> (ruling R2)
    claim_token     TEXT,
    claimed_at      TEXT,
    judged_at       TEXT,                               -- UTC, when judge() decided; step 4 writes it (ruling R18)
    day_max         INTEGER,                            -- the per-handset offer ceiling step 5 applied (ruling R18)
    ledger_claim    INTEGER,                            -- WaSendBudget's claim handle, an int (Part F §H.2.5.1); written BEFORE the gateway is called
    variant         INTEGER,                            -- chosen with the ledger claim, before the send
    wa_message_id   TEXT,
    echo            TEXT,                               -- claimed | late | none: the echo claim's outcome at the send (O-D18)
    sent_at         TEXT,                               -- UTC, when the gateway returned (sent or may-have-been)
    settled_at      TEXT,
    reason          TEXT,                               -- a fixed code (§H.4.8, §H.4.10)
    replied_at      TEXT,                               -- first message from this number within 72 h of sent_at
    stop_at         TEXT,                               -- first opt-out or stop word within 72 h of sent_at
    created_at      TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    CHECK (state IN ('queued', 'claimed', 'sent', 'uncertain', 'failed', 'skipped')),
    CHECK (variant IS NULL OR variant BETWEEN 1 AND 3),
    CHECK (echo IS NULL OR echo IN ('claimed', 'late', 'none')),
    CHECK (attempt >= 0),
    CHECK (handset GLOB 'i:?*'),
    CHECK (state <> 'claimed' OR (claim_token IS NOT NULL AND claimed_at IS NOT NULL AND attempt >= 1)),
    CHECK (state NOT IN ('sent', 'uncertain') OR sent_at IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (state NOT IN ('sent', 'uncertain') OR (judged_at IS NOT NULL AND day_max IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK (day_max IS NULL OR day_max BETWEEN 1 AND 60),
    CHECK (state <> 'sent' OR (variant IS NOT NULL AND wa_message_id IS NOT NULL AND echo IS NOT NULL)),
    CHECK (phone IS NULL OR (length(phone) BETWEEN 10 AND 15 AND phone NOT GLOB '*[^0-9]*'))
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wor_once  ON wa_offer_recipients(offer_id, phone);   -- one send per recipient per offer
CREATE INDEX        IF NOT EXISTS idx_wor_next  ON wa_offer_recipients(offer_id, state, handset, rank);
CREATE INDEX        IF NOT EXISTS idx_wor_phone ON wa_offer_recipients(phone, sent_at);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_offer_tests (
    id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    offer_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    content_hash   TEXT    NOT NULL,                    -- what was tested
    variant        INTEGER NOT NULL,
    staff_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,                    -- the admin; the number is that account's own, read at the send, never stored
    channel        TEXT    NOT NULL,
    handset        TEXT    NOT NULL,                    -- WaSendBudget::handset()
    state          TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'sending',
    reason         TEXT,
    wa_message_id  TEXT,
    echo           TEXT,                                -- claimed | late | none
    ledger         TEXT,                                -- 'recorded', or the fixed code WaSendBudget::record() answered
    started_at     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    settled_at     TEXT,
    CHECK (state IN ('sending', 'sent', 'uncertain', 'failed')),
    CHECK (variant BETWEEN 1 AND 3),
    CHECK (handset GLOB 'i:?*'),
    CHECK (echo IS NULL OR echo IN ('claimed', 'late', 'none')),
    CHECK (state <> 'sent' OR (wa_message_id IS NOT NULL AND echo IS NOT NULL))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wot_offer ON wa_offer_tests(offer_id, content_hash, variant, state);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wa_offer_events (
    id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    offer_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    action    TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- created|edited|discarded|tested|started|paused|resumed|stopped|done|expired|
                                  -- paused_by_switch|paused_by_rollback|paused_stop_rate
    by_id     INTEGER,            -- the staff account; NULL = the system
    by_name   TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- the account's name, or 'system'
    detail    TEXT,               -- counts and fixed codes only
    at        TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_woe_offer ON wa_offer_events(offer_id, id);

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wo_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_offers
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offers: an offer is history and is never deleted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wo_content_fixed
BEFORE UPDATE OF title, wording_1, wording_2, wording_3, stop_line, image_file, image_mime, image_bytes, image_sha256,
                 content_hash, audience_size ON wa_offers WHEN OLD.state <> 'draft'
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offers: what an offer says is fixed once it has started'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wo_closed_is_final BEFORE UPDATE ON wa_offers WHEN OLD.state IN ('stopped', 'done')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offers: a stopped or finished offer is final'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wo_state_path BEFORE UPDATE OF state ON wa_offers
WHEN (NEW.state = 'draft' AND OLD.state <> 'draft') OR (OLD.state = 'draft' AND NEW.state IN ('paused', 'done'))
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offers: no such change of state'); END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_offer_recipients
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: a recipient row is history and is never deleted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_final BEFORE UPDATE OF state ON wa_offer_recipients
WHEN OLD.state IN ('sent', 'uncertain', 'failed', 'skipped')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: a settled recipient is final'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_identity_fixed BEFORE UPDATE OF offer_id, rank, last_in_at ON wa_offer_recipients
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: who and in which order is fixed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_phone_erase_only BEFORE UPDATE OF phone ON wa_offer_recipients WHEN NEW.phone IS NOT NULL
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: a phone may only be erased'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_outcome_fixed
BEFORE UPDATE OF conversation_id, channel, handset, attempt, ledger_claim, variant, wa_message_id, echo, sent_at,
                 reason, judged_at, day_max
ON wa_offer_recipients WHEN OLD.state IN ('sent', 'uncertain', 'failed', 'skipped')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: what happened is fixed'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wor_marks_once BEFORE UPDATE OF replied_at, stop_at ON wa_offer_recipients
WHEN (OLD.replied_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.replied_at IS NOT OLD.replied_at)
  OR (OLD.stop_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.stop_at IS NOT OLD.stop_at)
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_recipients: a reply or a STOP is recorded once'); END;

CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wot_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_offer_tests
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_tests: a test is history and is never deleted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS wot_final BEFORE UPDATE OF state ON wa_offer_tests
WHEN OLD.state IN ('sent', 'uncertain', 'failed')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_tests: a settled test is final'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS woe_never_deleted BEFORE DELETE ON wa_offer_events
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_events: the trail is never deleted'); END;
CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS woe_never_changed BEFORE UPDATE ON wa_offer_events
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'wa_offer_events: the trail is never changed'); END;

-- The self-check (C2), into _schema_checks, the one table 089, 090 and 091 share. The CREATE below is 089's statement
-- byte for byte (ruling R9; one test compares the three texts), so 091 verifies itself even where 089's statement failed.
-- Its CHECK (found = expected) refuses a short count, and that refusal is not swallowed, so migration.log says PARTIAL for
-- 091 and the deploy refuses (OF-M2). The runner strips this comment before the split (lib/MigrationRunner.php:94); the
-- INSERT counts by name and holds neither CREATE nor INDEX, so no error of it is swallowed (:226-233; wa_offers A, OM82).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _schema_checks (
  migration  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  expected   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  found      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  checked_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
  CHECK (found = expected));
INSERT INTO _schema_checks (migration, expected, found)
SELECT '091_wa_offers.sql', 25, count(*) FROM sqlite_master
 WHERE name IN ('wa_offers', 'wa_offer_recipients', 'wa_offer_tests', 'wa_offer_events',
                'idx_wo_live', 'idx_wo_state', 'idx_wor_once', 'idx_wor_next', 'idx_wor_phone', 'idx_wot_offer', 'idx_woe_offer',
                'wo_never_deleted', 'wo_content_fixed', 'wo_closed_is_final', 'wo_state_path',
                'wor_never_deleted', 'wor_final', 'wor_identity_fixed', 'wor_phone_erase_only', 'wor_outcome_fixed', 'wor_marks_once',
                'wot_never_deleted', 'wot_final', 'woe_never_deleted', 'woe_never_changed');
```

**Why it is built this way:**
- The runner marks the file applied whatever happens (`lib/MigrationRunner.php:243-247`), and the swallow test is at `:226-233`.
- A `CHECK constraint failed`, a `no such table` and a missing column raised by this INSERT are each **not** swallowed: comments are stripped before the split (`:94`), and the INSERT as split holds neither "INDEX" nor "CREATE" (`:226-233`). Each is therefore logged as `PARTIAL: 091_wa_offers.sql` (`:252-255`). `wa_offers` A proves each class through the runner (ruling R9).
- **The `_schema_checks` CREATE is 089's, byte for byte** (ruling R9): its columns are `migration`, `expected`, `found` and `checked_at`, with `CHECK (found = expected)`. Where 089 made the table it is a no-op; where 089's statement failed, 091 makes it and still verifies itself.
- **A phone may only be erased** (Part F's A20, ruling R10). Part F's `erase` sets `wa_offer_recipients.phone` to
  NULL, which `wor_phone_erase_only` allows and nothing else may do; the identity trigger no longer names the phone,
  as Part F's triggers do. `idx_wor_once` never conflicts on NULLs, and an erased row drops out of every per-phone
  rule (§H.4.8); `--check offers-live` neither groups nor re-judges it, and C-O2-4 compares its phone with `IS`
  (§H.4.6).
- **`judged_at` and `day_max` record what a send was decided by** (ruling R18): the moment `judge()` decided, written
  by step 4 with its outcome under the row's CAS, and the per-handset ceiling step 5 applied (§H.4.10). Every
  `sent`/`uncertain` row holds both, by CHECK, and `wor_outcome_fixed` keeps them once the row is settled, so
  `--check offers-live` re-judges a send at its `judged_at` and under its `day_max` (§H.4.6). Columns are not
  objects, so the self-check still counts 25.
- **`wa_offer_schema_check` is gone.** There is one self-check table for 089, 090 and 091 (K2-03).
- The runner's header claim of "not marked applied … fail-fast" (`:31-37`) is untrue, and 091 does not rely on it.

**`OfferSchema::check(\PDO)`**, used by the tool, the deploy and `wa_offers` A, returns a list of fixed problems; an empty list means sound. It checks:
- each of the 25 objects by type and name;
- that each trigger's stored `sql` ends in `END` after trimming;
- the columns `wa_offer_recipients.attempt`, `.echo`, `.judged_at`, `.day_max` and `wa_offer_tests.echo`, `.ledger`
  (by `PRAGMA table_info`);
- that `_schema_checks` holds the row keyed exactly `091_wa_offers.sql` with `found = expected = 25` (ruling R9);
- that `_migrations` holds `091_wa_offers.sql`.

It never counts "N tables" on its own (R-12).

#### H.4.6 The ladder rows, the settings, and each check

**P6's two rows in `SalesFollowupLadder::STEPS`**, declared in `lib/SalesFollowupLadder.php`, Part F's file (one table,
owned by the coordinator; C1, C6, K2-02). `tools/sales_followup.php` reads the table unchanged. Each row dispatches its
own precondition, its check and its off-hook to `lib/OfferSwitch.php`, to the callables written below and in §H.4.4 with
ruling R13's signatures, each `public static`: the precondition for both steps, `checkTest` for step 11 or `checkLive`
for step 12, and the hook for both. **Two connections, both opened by the tool and by nothing it calls (ruling R13):**
`$ro`, the read-only check connection (`PRAGMA query_only=ON`, never `SqliteStore::create`), given to the precondition
and the checks; and `$rw`, the one writable connection, given to the hook. `$step` is the row's step name (`offers-test`
or `offers-live`), `$config` the configuration as the tool reads it at the call, `$dataDir` is `cliDataDir`'s, and
`$now` the one `time()` the tool takes at its start. A precondition returns
`array{ok:bool, code:?string, lines:list<string>}`, a check
`array{status:string, counts:array<string,int>, notes:list<string>}`, and the hook its counts, `array<string,int>`,
throwing on failure:

| Step | Name | Keys it writes | Precondition | Off-cascade |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **11 (O1)** | `offers-test` | exactly `offers_test_enabled=1`, no since-stamp (ruling R5) | Needs (ruling R6): the ledger on (`wa_send_ledger=on`, from step 2 or `skip ack`) with L-ON at PASS; step 3 on with Q1-ON at PASS or an accepted `NOT_YET no_traffic`. Then P-O1-1 … P-O1-9 below | step 12's off first; then `OfferSwitch::offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array` with `$step` `offers-test`, on the tool's `$rw` (ruling R13), **before** the key clears; then unsets `offers_test_enabled` |
| **12 (O2)** | `offers-live` | `offers_live_enabled=1`, `offers_live_since=<UTC now>` (ruling R5) | step 11 on; `--check offers-test` PASS now; every setting in range | `OfferSwitch::offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array` with `$step` `offers-live`, on the tool's `$rw` (ruling R13), **before** the keys clear; then unsets `offers_live_enabled` and `offers_live_since` |

**Settings, declared once in the ladder's one settings table**, in `lib/SalesFollowupLadder.php` (ruling R5). Each row
holds its key, no short alias, its type, its range and its owning part, `O` in the one table (Part F §H.2.12.7).
`SalesFollowupLadder::settingKeys()` returns them and `allKeys()` does not, so `off all` never clears them and stage A
never reads one as NO-GO; they arm nothing by themselves. They are set with the tool's `set <key> <value>`, which
validates by that row. A value out of range is refused, and nothing is saved:

| Key | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offers_warm_days` | int | 30 | 7–30 | "wrote in the last N days". Never above D11's 30. Also the length of the hold after an inbound voice note (ruling R3). Recorded on an offer at its Start (`warm_days`); every later judgement of that offer applies the recorded value (§H.4.8; ruling R18) |
| `offers_recent_days` | int | 7 | 7–60 | no second offer within N days. Recorded on an offer at its Start (`recent_days`), and applied from there, as above (ruling R18) |
| `offers_daily_max_per_handset` | int | 20 | 1–60, and ≤ Part F's `wa_send_daily_cap` (C3, default 60) | the pilot ceiling for offers on one handset per Kampala day, inside the ledger's own limits. Recorded on each recipient row as `day_max` by the judgement whose step 5 applies it (§H.4.10 step 4; ruling R18) |
| `offers_on_owned_numbers` | int | 0 | 0–1 | whether offers may leave a salesperson's own number |
| `offers_stop_pause_pct` | int | 5 | 1–20 | the auto-pause threshold (O-D13) |
| `offers_max_days` | int | 14 | 1–30 | an offer's lifetime from Start |

**One list of keys (S2-11, rulings R5, R10).** `OfferSwitch::declaredKeys()` returns the two switches, `offers_live_since` and the six settings. `wa_offers` B asserts that:
- its two switches and `offers_live_since` equal P6's part of `SalesFollowupLadder::allKeys()`, and its six settings equal P6's part of `settingKeys()`;
- TL14 scans **P6's slice of the one merged declared list** (Part F §H.2.12.4; ruling R10): a slice of that list, never a list of its own, naming every new or changed P6 PHP file outside `tests/`:
  - **new, scanned whole:** `lib/OfferSwitch.php`, `lib/OfferText.php`, `lib/OfferImage.php`, `lib/OfferAudience.php`, `lib/OfferStore.php`, `lib/OfferGateway.php`, **`lib/EvolutionOfferGateway.php`** (which the pattern `lib/Offer*.php` does not match), `lib/OfferSender.php`, `lib/OfferWindow.php`, `lib/OfferSchema.php`, `cron/offers_send.php`, `tabs/engage/wa_offers.php` and `includes/post/post_offers.php`;
  - **changed, scanned in P6's 5.18.104 hunks only:** `public.php`, `includes/navigation.php` and `includes/post_handlers.php`. P6's line of `cron/master.php` and its rows of `lib/SalesFollowupLadder.php` are scanned in Part F's slice, which holds those shared files with every part's lines.

  TL14 finds no `$config[...]` / `$cfg[...]` key in these files outside `SalesFollowupLadder::allKeys()`, `settingKeys()` and **`SalesFollowupLadder::preexistingKeys()`** (Part F §H.2.12.4), the one declared list of pre-existing keys. That list holds P6's shared reads: `timezone`, `wa_human_cooldown_minutes`, `reminder_hour`, `reminder_until_hour`, and the Evolution and registry keys. The ledger's window and gap keys (`wa_send_hour_from`, `wa_send_hour_to`, `wa_send_gap_min_s`, `wa_send_gap_max_s`) are rows of `settingKeys()`, not pre-existing keys. B reads TL14's result; TL14's control plants a key read in `lib/EvolutionOfferGateway.php`, which fails it;
- after `off all`, no P6 switch or stamp is set, and the six settings keep their values.

**Constants, not settings:**
- 48 h quiet after a follow-up or chase step;
- 72 h for "replied" and "STOP";
- 72 h for "a person is handling";
- 120 min after the customer's last message;
- a 15-minute stale claim;
- the 50 s in-flight bound every offer claim carries (O-D9, §H.4.10);
- the 35 s run budget, the 15 s send timeout, and the 20 s below which a run does only its stale sweep and the
  live-since guard;
- at least 40 sends before the auto-pause can fire.

**Runtime predicates (`lib/OfferSwitch.php`), read on every entry point:**
- `uganda($config, $dataDir)` is `StaffJobsGate::applies($config, $dataDir)` (`lib/StaffJobsGate.php:18-35`), and is false on any doubt.
- `screen()` is `uganda() && offers_test_enabled`.
- `live()` is `screen() && offers_live_enabled && offers_live_since` is a valid UTC stamp.
- `settings($config)` returns the values above. **A stored value out of range makes `live()` false, and the screen says so.** It is never clamped, and never quietly replaced by the default.
- The sender also refuses unless:
  - `dn_tz() === 'Africa/Kampala'` (R-16);
  - Part F's pieces of §H.4.14 are loadable: `WaSendBudget` with its table, `QuoteChase::offerHolds`/`offerHold`, `HumanTakeover::phonesSince`/`phoneSince`, `ReminderDay::done`, `JobBudget`, and the `wa_seen_marks` table. P6 needs nothing from Part V (ruling R3).

**`OfferSwitch::offHook(\PDO $rw, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step, string $why): array`** (ruling R13;
`$step` is `offers-test` or `offers-live`, `$why` is `switch` or `rollback`). It writes only through `$rw`, the tool's
one writable connection, and it opens no connection of its own. Its ledger, `$ledger`, is Part F's ledger over a held
connection, `WaSendBudget::onConnection($rw, $config, $dataDir)` (Part F §H.2.5.1), built once, so each
`$ledger->settle()` below lands on `$rw`, inside the hook's one transaction; the hook calls nothing else on it. It
never uses `forInstall()`, which needs a store, and no store can be had over a given `\PDO`: `SqliteStore`'s
constructor is private and `create()` opens a connection of its own (`lib/SqliteStore.php:130`, `:140`). It takes the
sender's lock `<data>/offers_send.lock`, found under `$dataDir`, waiting up to 70 s, so no send is in flight while it
settles.
Then, in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on `$rw`:
1. every `running` offer becomes `paused` (`live_slot` stays 1, `updated_at` now), with an event `paused_by_switch` or
   `paused_by_rollback`;
2. every `claimed` recipient is settled:
   - with a `ledger_claim`: `$ledger->settle((int)$row['ledger_claim'], 'failed', ['maybe_sent' => true])`, on `$rw`,
     stored `uncertain` (ruling R2), and the row becomes `uncertain('stale_claim')` with `sent_at = claimed_at` and
     `settled_at` now. A row already settled (by Part F's orphan rule, or by step 9 before a death at step 10)
     matches nothing: `settle()` is a no-op that the ledger logs as `late_settle` (Part F §H.2.5.5), and the hook
     goes on; C-O2-4 accepts the outcome that row keeps and prints it (§H.4.6);
   - without one: the row goes back to `queued`, with `not_before` now, the columns the stale sweep writes (§H.4.10),
     because it never reached the gateway (ruling R12's reading of ruling R7). If a ledger row exists under its stable
     ref `offer:<offer_id>:<recipient_id>` anyway (a death between steps 6 and 7 of §H.4.10), the recipient's next claim
     answers `in_flight` while that row is younger than 900 s and `already_sent` after, and the recipient is settled
     `uncertain('ledger_already_sent')`: nothing is sent twice;
3. every `sending` test older than 15 minutes becomes `uncertain`, with `settled_at` now.

It returns its counts, `array<string,int>`, and throws on failure (ruling R13). **The hook runs before P6's keys
clear**, in a plain `off` and in a rollback alike (ruling R7); the ladder unsets the keys only after it returns without
error. **Switching `offers-live` on again resumes nothing**: an admin presses Resume (O-D19).

**The status vocabulary** is the ladder's: `PASS`, `FAIL <code>`, or `NOT_YET too_soon|no_traffic|no_test` (K2-13, ruling R6). P6 prints no other word.

**`on offers-test` — the preconditions, each refusing with its code and saving nothing.** P-O1-1 and P-O1-2 are the
ladder engine's own rules, restated; P-O1-3 … P-O1-9 are step 11's own precondition,
`OfferSwitch::preconditions(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, string $step): array` with `$step` `offers-test`,
in `lib/OfferSwitch.php`, which the row dispatches to (ruling R13). It reads the book only through the tool's `$ro`,
P-O1-4's presence probe and every call of Part F's readers (`offerHolds`/`offerHold`, `phonesSince`/`phoneSince`)
included, and never opens the book itself or through `SqliteStore::create`. Part F's `ReminderDay::done` is not a
reader: it is pure (Part F §H.2.5.3) and is given no connection (P-O1-4). The tool asserts `total_changes()==0` on
`$ro` at its end:
- **P-O1-1:** Uganda.
- **P-O1-2:** step 11's Needs, and the ladder's order (ruling R6):
  - **the ledger on** (`wa_send_ledger=on`, whether from step 2 or from `skip ack`), with L-ON at PASS. The ledger is P6's floor;
  - **step 3 on**, with Q1-ON at PASS or an accepted `NOT_YET no_traffic`. The chase hold reads the tracker, so without it an offer could reach a customer with a pending quotation. `skip tracking` cascades to steps 11 and 12;
  - ORDER is the ladder engine's (ruling R11): every lower-numbered step is on, skipped, or optional (steps 1b and
    10), and none is left running at FAIL. P6 adds no rule of its own: a voice step (5, 7, 8, 9) at `NOT_YET`, and
    the optional row 1b (Part P's `agent-cc`) and step 10 left off, never hold offers back; the daily list (4) and
    the chases (6) are not Needs of step 11, but ORDER still requires each to be on or recorded skipped.
- **P-O1-3:** `OfferSchema::check()` is empty.
- **P-O1-4:** Part F's pieces present. **The probe only reads and writes nothing.**
  Part F defines no side-effect-free form of `claim`, `settle` or `record` that judges anything: `claim()` inserts a
  row whenever it answers ok (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 9), `record()` inserts a settled row (§H.2.5.5), and a ledger over
  the tool's `$ro` can only be `onConnection()`'s, whose `claim()` inserts nothing because it judges nothing: it
  answers `not_claimable`, final (§H.2.5.1). So those three are checked as
  present and never called:
  - the `wa_auto_sends` table exists, and `method_exists` holds for `WaSendBudget`'s `claim`, `settle`, `record` and
    `onConnection` (the off-hook's ledger, §H.4.6);
  - the `wa_seen_marks` table exists.

  Only these are called, with an invented number, an invented instance and an invented time `$t`. The readers,
  `offerHolds`/`offerHold` and `phonesSince`/`phoneSince`, are each given the tool's `$ro` (ruling R13); the pure
  ones, `handset()`, `ReminderDay::done` and `JobBudget`'s two, are given no connection. Each answers without
  throwing, and each read finds nothing (an empty list, `''` or null):
  - `WaSendBudget::handset(' Sales-X ') === WaSendBudget::handset('i:sales-x')`;
  - `QuoteChase::offerHolds`/`offerHold` (ruling R3);
  - `HumanTakeover::phonesSince`/`phoneSince` (ruling R3);
  - `ReminderDay::done([], $config, $dataDir, $t)`, pure (Part F §H.2.5.3), with an empty schedule: the probe reads
    no `master_schedule.json` row, and the bool it answers is not judged (ruling R8);
  - `JobBudget::seconds`/`mayStart`.

  Nothing of Part V is probed: P6 reads no Part V piece (ruling R3).
- **P-O1-5:** `dn_tz()` is `Africa/Kampala`.
- **P-O1-6:** `cron/master.php`, read as text, holds ruling R1's four new lines byte for byte, in ruling R1's order (`quote_chase`, `quote_daily_list`, `ai_media`, `offers_send`), last in `$_m_jobs`. `'offers_send'` occurs exactly once, as the last job, with `'interval' => 240`, `'uganda' => true` and `'flag' => 'offers_live_enabled'` (ruling R1).
- **P-O1-7:** at least one active admin account has a phone that `PhoneNumber::international` accepts (a count only),
  counted in the `retailers.json` rows that `OfferAudience::storedRows($ro)` reads through the tool's `$ro`. The
  preview below is given the same read, with nothing written on `$ro` between, and C-O2-9 builds its staff and
  DishNet lists from the same read through `$ro` (§H.4.8; ruling R13).
- **P-O1-8:** no offer is `running`.
- **P-O1-9:** `OfferSwitch::declaredKeys()` is inside the union of `SalesFollowupLadder::allKeys()` and `settingKeys()`: the switches and the stamp in the first, the six settings in the second (ruling R5).

On success, the tool prints the preview of an audience of size "all" as the baseline (counts only, by handset and by
reason), from `OfferAudience::build()` given the tool's `$ro` and the rows of `OfferAudience::storedRows($ro)`, the
read P-O1-7 counts in, as the tool passes `retailers.json` rows read through `$ro` to Part P's `accountCounts()`
(ruling R13). The audience opens no store and builds none (§H.4.8); the tool then saves.

**`--check offers-test` — the step's own check, which must be PASS before `on offers-live`.** It is
`OfferSwitch::checkTest(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, int $now): array` in `lib/OfferSwitch.php`, dispatched
from step 11's row in the ladder (ruling R13). It reads the book only through the tool's `$ro`, every call of Part F's
readers included, and never opens the book itself or through `SqliteStore::create`; the tool asserts
`total_changes()==0` on `$ro` at its end. Its windows are counted back from `$now`.
- **C-O1-1:** at least one offer has a `sent` test for **each** of its wordings, for its **current**
  `content_hash`, started within the last 7 days, **whose `ledger` is `recorded`** (Q17-O01). If not:
  `NOT_YET no_test`. A test whose `record()` answered `error` does not count (C-O1-3), so its wording needs
  another test, and a later test of that wording, recorded, supersedes it. `offer_start` counts a wording's
  tests the same way (O-D10, §H.4.7).
- **C-O1-2 (K2-17):**
  - every `sent` test has `echo = 'claimed'`; a `late` echo is FAIL `echo_late`;
  - no `wa_messages` row with its id has `agent_name = 'Team'`;
  - for tests sent **within the last 72 h only**, the id is also in `evo_webhook_seen` with event `offer.test`. Older tests are reported as `older than 72 h — not checked`, because the webhook prunes after 72 h.
- **C-O1-3 (K2-06; Q17-O01, ruling R18):** each `sent`/`uncertain` test is judged by what its own request
  recorded. That request writes `record()`'s answer into `ledger` in the one UPDATE that settles the test
  (§H.4.10), so `ledger` is set on every test its request settled, and NULL on one that a sweep settled after
  its request died:
  - a test with `ledger` set reads `recorded` and has a `wa_auto_sends` row with kind `other`, ref
    `offer_test:<id>` and the same handset. Anything else is FAIL, except `error` (below).
    A test is sent only on a read where the ledger is on, and its ledger is built from that read (§H.4.10;
    ruling R19), so its `record()` never answers `ledger_off`: a test recorded so is a fault and reads FAIL,
    never a printed count. Nor can it answer `not_uganda` or `no_table`: `WaSendBudget::on()`, which held on
    that read, holds only on Uganda (Part F §H.2.5.1), and 089's table, which P-O1-4 found, is never dropped;
  - a `sent` test with `ledger` NULL is FAIL: only its request writes `sent`, in the UPDATE that writes `ledger`;
  - an `uncertain` test with `ledger` NULL is counted and printed, never FAIL, split by whether a
    `wa_auto_sends` row with ref `offer_test:<id>` exists (its request died after `record()`) or not (before
    it). A sweep settled it: the next test press of its offer, the sender's step 4 (§H.4.10), the off-hook
    (item 3 above) or the by-hand put-back (§H.4.19). The request that could record it had died, so nothing
    it could do is missing (ruling R18);
  - a test whose `ledger` reads `error` is counted and printed, never FAIL: `record()` swallowed a throwable
    (Part F §H.2.5.5), such as a wait past the book's 5 s `busy_timeout` (live `lib/SqliteStore.php:158`),
    which the request could neither foresee nor prevent. C-O1-1 does not count that test;
  - a test still `sending` is not judged; one older than 15 minutes is counted and printed as not yet swept.

  C-O1-3 is not windowed, and a test is never deleted and is final once settled (`wot_never_deleted`,
  `wot_final`), so a FAIL here would stand for good: none of these clauses reads FAIL over a test whose request
  acted correctly.
- **C-O1-4:** judged only while no offer has ever started, that is while `wa_offer_events` holds no `started`
  event. Step 11 writes no since-stamp to window it by (ruling R5); the trail is never deleted (`woe_never_deleted`),
  and a Start needs `offers-live` on (§H.4.7), so until then it still proves the test step reached no customer:
  - `wa_offer_recipients` is empty;
  - no `wa_auto_sends` row has kind `offer`;
  - no `evo_webhook_seen` row has event `offer.send`.

  After the first Start it prints those three counts as a note line, never FAIL, and leaves customer sends to
  C-O2-1 … C-O2-12. A live run therefore never turns `--check offers-test` to FAIL, and step 12's Need can be met
  again, once C-O1-1 holds, after an `off offers-live` and after a redeploy (Part F §H.2.16; OF-RB2).
- **C-O1-5 (R-01, a note):** the `wa_seen_marks` rows with `direction = 'in'` over the last 30 days, and the phones they cover (counts only).
- **C-O1-6:** P-O1-3, P-O1-4, P-O1-5 and P-O1-9 again, on the same `$ro`. All four only read (P-O1-4 calls no `claim`,
  `settle` or `record`), so `total_changes()==0` on `$ro` still holds at the tool's end (ruling R13).

**`on offers-live`** saves `offers_live_enabled` and `offers_live_since`. **It starts nothing: only an admin's Start does.**

**`--check offers-live` — judges the live run.** It is
`OfferSwitch::checkLive(\PDO $ro, array $config, string $dataDir, int $now): array` in `lib/OfferSwitch.php`, dispatched
from step 12's row in the ladder (ruling R13). It reads the book only through the tool's `$ro`, every call of Part F's
readers included (`offerHold` and `phoneSince` in C-O2-9) and the audience's `lists()` (C-O2-9, §H.4.8), and never
opens the book itself or through `SqliteStore::create`; the tool asserts `total_changes()==0` on `$ro` at its end.
If no offer has ever started:
`NOT_YET no_traffic`.

**How `--check offers-live` judges a past send (ruling R18).** A clause that re-judges a send judges it three ways,
each from records written when the send was decided:
1. **at its moment:** the ledger row's `claimed_at`, the instant the claim judged (Part F §H.2.5.3), for what the
   claim decided (the window, the spacing, the caps), and the recipient's `judged_at`, written by step 4 of the send
   (§H.4.10), for what `judge()` decided; never `sent_at`, the gateway's return, up to 50 s later;
2. **from what could be read then:** every source bounded by its storage time at or before that moment
   (`wa_messages.created_at`, `followups.opened_at`, `contact_optouts.created_at`, `wa_seen_marks.seen_at`,
   `events.created_at`, `quote_tracker.created_at`, `dist_contacts.created_at`, `followup_sends.sent_at`, which its
   insert stamps), never by an inbound row's `sent_at`, the customer's device `messageTimestamp` (live
   `lib/ConversationService.php:1202-1217`), which can sort before a row stored later. Step 4 holds the book's write
   lock until `judged_at`'s second has passed, so every row stored at or before `judged_at` was in `judge()`'s read
   and none stored after it was (§H.4.10). Every stamp a clause bounds as at or before `judged_at` is taken inside
   its writer's own INSERT, once that writer holds the lock: SQLite's `datetime('now')` (live
   `lib/ConversationService.php:784-785`, `lib/DistributorNotifier.php:96-97`; the defaults of
   `migrations/069_contact_optouts.sql:32`, `001_event_queue.sql:26` and `070_followups.sql:29`, `:98`, which the
   live inserts leave in place, `lib/ContactOptOut.php:170-172`, `lib/EventBus.php:97-99`,
   `lib/FollowUpService.php:83-86`, `:364-366`), Part F's defaults on `quote_tracker` and `wa_seen_marks`, and the
   ledger's claim, whose clock is taken once it holds its lock (Part F §H.2.5.3). A stamp bounded the other way
   (`closed_at`, `lifted_at`, `status_at`, a ledger row's `settled_at`) can only make a clause pass. So a row
   stored in `judged_at`'s own second came before `judge()`'s read and is judged as an earlier row is: that is how
   this part meets Part F's IO-5, and why C-O2-9 calls Part F's readers at `judged_at` itself;
3. **under the limits it applied:** the ledger row's `win_from`, `win_to`, `cap_day` and `cap_hour` and each earlier
   row's `gap_s` (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 9), the recipient's `day_max`, and the offer's `warm_days` and `recent_days`,
   recorded at its Start; never the settings as they read now, which `set` may narrow at any time (Part F
   §H.2.12.7). Ruling R8's "a check reads the settings" means these recorded values.

What the maker could not have known is printed as a count, never `FAIL`: a row stored after the moment (between
`judged_at` and `sent_at` included), content no row records, a state a person may set. A clause that could read
`FAIL` over a correct send would be a defect: a `FAIL` can never be accepted (Part F §H.2.12.3).
- **C-O2-1:** per offer, the counts of §H.4.12; per handset, today's offers against the ceiling each row recorded
  (`day_max`), with the setting as it reads now beside it.
- **C-O2-2:** zero sends outside the window their claim applied (O-D9, B11-01; rulings R8, R18). Every
  `sent`/`uncertain` row is judged by its ledger row, the one C-O2-4 maps to it by the two-part ref whose
  outcome is not `not_sent` (`sent`, `uncertain`, or still in flight, as the by-hand put-back leaves it,
  §H.4.19, or a step-9 settle that did not land, §H.4.10): for a row settled `uncertain('ledger_already_sent')`,
  the earlier claim under which its message may have gone, since the later claim answered before judging any
  window (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 1). That
  row's `claimed_at`, read in a literal `Africa/Kampala`, is not on a Sunday, is at or after its `win_from` hour
  and, with P6's in-flight bound of 50 s added, at or before its `win_to` hour: the window that row records, never
  `WaSendBudget::window($config)` as the settings read now. A row settled `uncertain('stale_claim')` whose only
  ledger rows under its ref are `not_sent` was certainly not sent (step 9 settled it before a death at step 10;
  C-O2-4) and is counted and printed, never judged for the window. A row with no ledger row under its ref is
  FAIL under C-O2-4 and counted here. A row whose `sent_at`, the gateway's return, falls after its `win_to` is
  counted and printed, never FAIL: its claim was inside the bound, and the return is what the claim could not
  know.
- **C-O2-3:** zero pairs of offer sends to one phone closer than the later one's `recent_days`, the value its offer
  recorded at its Start, never `offers_recent_days` as it reads now (ruling R18): of two `sent`/`uncertain` rows
  with the same phone, the later is the one with the later `judged_at` (then the higher `id`), and the earlier's
  `sent_at` is more than that many days before the later's `judged_at`, as `recent_offer` held at the later one's
  judgement (§H.4.8), never the later's `sent_at`, the gateway's return. The earlier was settled by then: a
  `claimed` row holds the phone at any age, so no later send was judged while it was claimed. Phones that are
  NULL (erased by Part F's `erase`, ruling R10) are not grouped.
- **C-O2-4 (S2-17, K2-08, ruling R2):**
  - every `sent`/`uncertain` row has a `wa_auto_sends` row with the two-part ref `offer:<offer_id>:<id>`, kind
    `offer`, the row's phone (compared with `IS`, so a pair erased by Part F's `erase` matches) and handset, whose
    outcome is `sent` for a `sent` row and `uncertain` for an `uncertain` row (a may-have-been-sent is settled
    `failed` with `maybe_sent`). Four designed outcomes are judged otherwise (ruling R18; Q16-O03, Q16-O04, Q18-O01):
    - a row settled `uncertain('ledger_already_sent')` is matched by ref, kind and phone only, with outcome
      `sent` or `uncertain`. The ledger's idempotency is by `(kind, ref)`, never by handset (Part F §H.2.5.3
      step 1), so after a death between steps 6 and 7, step 4 may move the recipient to another handset, whose
      claim then answers `in_flight` and `already_sent` over the first handset's row (§H.4.10). A handset that
      differs is counted and printed, never FAIL;
    - a row settled `uncertain('stale_claim')` whose ledger row step 9 had already settled, `sent` or `not_sent`:
      a death between steps 9 and 10 leaves the recipient `claimed` with its ledger row settled, and the stale
      sweep, the off-hook and the by-hand put-back each make it `uncertain` while their `settle()`, where they
      call one, changes nothing (Part F §H.2.5.5). The ledger's outcome is counted and printed, never FAIL;
    - a row settled `uncertain('stale_claim')` whose ledger row is still in flight, as the by-hand put-back
      leaves it (§H.4.19), is judged as the last bullet below judges a ledger row in flight;
    - any other `sent`/`uncertain` row, settled by step 10, whose ledger row under its ref, matched by ref, kind
      and phone, is still in flight, or was settled `uncertain` by the ledger's own sweep before its settle
      landed (detail `stale_orphan` or `stale`, Part F §H.2.5.3 steps 1 and 3a): step 9's `settle()` did not
      land. It never throws into the sender (Part F §H.2.5.5), so a wait past the book's 5 s `busy_timeout`
      (live `lib/SqliteStore.php:158`) leaves the ledger row in flight, and step 10 settles the recipient by
      the gateway's answer all the same (§H.4.10). Such a row is counted and printed as `settle_not_landed`,
      never FAIL, before the sweep and after it, as Part F's Q3-ON counts a chase (Part F §H.2.12.5): the send
      was claimed, and the ledger counts it. FAIL stays for a row with no ledger row under its ref, for one
      whose ledger rows there are all `not_sent`, and for every other outcome that differs; the last bullet
      below still judges the ledger row itself while it is in flight;
  - every `wa_auto_sends` row of kind `offer` maps by its two-part ref to a recipient; the ledger's own `try` numbers that recipient's attempts;
  - every try but the latest is settled, whatever its outcome;
  - **one still in flight more than 900 s after a later claim on its handset is FAIL `ledger_orphan`**: a later claim on the handset settles every row there in flight for 900 s or more (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 3), so one left in flight is a fault. One not yet swept, older than 900 s with no later claim on its handset, is counted and printed, never FAIL. This is Part F's L-ON condition (§H.2.12.5).
- **C-O2-5:** per handset and Kampala day, each `sent`/`uncertain` row was within the per-handset maximum its own
  row recorded, `day_max`, the value step 5 applied (§H.4.10), never `offers_daily_max_per_handset` as it reads now
  (ruling R18): fewer than `day_max` of the handset's other `sent`/`uncertain` rows that day have an earlier
  `judged_at` (then a lower `id`). The day is each row's `COALESCE(sent_at, claimed_at)` in Kampala, as step 5
  counts it. Part F's total of proactive kinds is printed beside it, against the `cap_day` each ledger row recorded.
- **C-O2-6:** every offer claim kept the spacing the ledger applied (C3; rulings R8, R18): its ledger row's
  `claimed_at` is at or after `claimed_at + gap_s` of every earlier row on its handset (a lower `id`), whatever its
  kind, whose outcome is not `not_sent`, each by its own `gap_s` (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 4), never by
  `wa_send_gap_min_s` as it reads now.
- **C-O2-7 (Q17-O02; ruling R18):** a `claimed` row older than 15 minutes is FAIL `claim_unswept` only once a
  later run's stale sweep should have reached it: some recipient row, of any offer, has a `claimed_at` more
  than 15 minutes and 35 s after this row's. Every claim of a run follows that run's completed sweep by at
  most 35 s (§H.4.10 steps 1 and 4), and that sweep settles every `claimed` row older than 15 minutes, so
  such a claim shows that a sweep ran after this row was stale. Otherwise the row is counted and printed as
  `claimed, not yet swept`, never FAIL: a run returns before its sweep on `busy`, on a failed precondition and
  with `offers_off` or `ledger_off` (§H.4.10 steps 2 and 3), and `off sending` leaves `offers_live_enabled`
  set and runs no P6 hook (Part F §H.2.12.4), so while the ledger is off no run sweeps at all. This is
  C-O2-4's form for a ledger row still in flight.
- **C-O2-8 (the echo trap, R-05, K2-17):**
  - every `sent` row has `echo = 'claimed'`; any `late` is FAIL `echo_late`, with its count;
  - no `wa_messages` row stored as `'Team'` has a send's own `wa_message_id`: the R-05 trap, judged by the act's
    identity (ruling R18);
  - for rows sent within the last 72 h only, the id is in `evo_webhook_seen` with event `offer.send`;
  - printed, never FAIL (ruling R18): the recipients whose conversation's `last_human_reply_at` falls within
    5 minutes after the send, split by the person row stored in that span: a `'Team'` row, a row in a staff
    member's name from the Inbox (`event_key` `wa_staff_reply` or `wa_image_send`; live
    `includes/api/api_whatsapp.php:244-258`, `:1000-1015`), or none. An Inbox reply sets `human_active`, stores no
    `'Team'` row and has its echo claimed, so a colleague's reply after an offer is never a fault.
- **C-O2-9:** the exclusions re-judged at the recipient's `judged_at`, the moment `judge()` decided (§H.4.10
  step 4), from the rows stored at or before it and under the offer's recorded `warm_days` and `recent_days`
  (ruling R18), for every row with a phone (an erased row, NULL, is counted and printed, never re-judged and never
  FAIL):
  - no opt-out for the phone was live then: none with `created_at` at or before `judged_at` and `lifted_at` NULL or
    after it (live `migrations/069_contact_optouts.sql:32-34`; `lib/ContactOptOut.php:201`), any channel, scope or
    source, in the one form;
  - none to a partner contact stored then (`dist_contacts.created_at` at or before `judged_at`; live
    `migrations/080_distributor_notifications.sql:35`), in the one form. The staff and DishNet lists, kept in the
    store's `retailers.json`, `kyc_config.json` and `wa_evo_numbers.json` and in a conversation's `category`,
    record no time at which a number joined them, so a send to a number on them today is counted and printed,
    never FAIL. All are read through `OfferAudience::lists()` given `$ro`, the rows of
    `OfferAudience::storedRows($ro)`, the read P-O1-7 counts in, never a store (ruling R13), and the
    recipient's `judged_at` as `$atUtc`, which bounds the partner list by `created_at`; a second call with
    `$atUtc` null gives the count printed for contacts stored after it (§H.4.8; Q16-O06);
  - none within 48 h after a follow-up send for the phone, by `followup_recent`'s two reads (§H.4.8) at `judged_at`:
    a `followup_sends` row by its `sent_at`, the stamp its insert stores (live `migrations/070_followups.sql:98`), or
    a `wa_auto_sends` row of kind `quote` or `enquiry` whose outcome is `sent`, `uncertain` or NULL (in flight), by
    its `claimed_at`, each in the 48 h before `judged_at`, compared in the one form (ruling R2, O-D17);
  - none while a `followups` row of any kind for the phone was open at `judged_at` (`followup_open` at that moment,
    §H.4.8): a row counts only when `opened_at <= judged_at AND (closed_at IS NULL OR closed_at > judged_at)`, the
    bound on both sides that Part F's hold takes (Part F §H.2.10.10, IO-5; A12-05). Both columns are compared in
    SQLite's `datetime('now')` form, `Y-m-d H:i:s` UTC: `opened_at` takes its default (live
    `migrations/070_followups.sql:29`) and the only live writer of `closed_at` writes `datetime('now')` (live
    `lib/FollowUpService.php:201`); `judged_at` is written in that form (`UtcClock::stamp()`), and the phone is
    compared in the one form (O-D17). Without the `opened_at`
    bound, the normal path after an offer (the customer replies, then stays quiet 24 h, and `followup_scan` opens an
    enquiry follow-up: `cron/followup_scan.php:67-77`, `:142`; `lib/FollowUpPolicy.php:57`, `:404`) would re-judge
    every such offer as sent while a follow-up was open, and C-O2-9 would read `FAIL`, which can never be accepted
    (Part F §H.2.12.3);
  - none while Part F's hold applied: `QuoteChase::offerHold($ro, $phone, judged_at)`, the past-moment form over its
    four sources, each bounded by its storage time (ruling R3, §H.4.14 item 2);
  - none within the offer's `recent_days` after another offer (C-O2-3's pair rule);
  - none after an inbound voice note stored (`created_at`) at or before `judged_at` whose `sent_at` is within the
    offer's `warm_days` before it (ruling R3);
  - none with a `wa_seen_marks` `'in'` row whose `seen_at` is at or before `judged_at` and within the offer's
    `warm_days` before it;
  - none while `HumanTakeover::phoneSince($ro, $phone, judged_at − 72 h, judged_at)` returned a code, not null
    (rulings R3, R13); its upper bound reads each source's storage time (Part F §H.2.7.1).

  What landed after `judged_at`, between it and `sent_at` included, is counted and printed per clause, never FAIL:
  `judge()` could not read it (ruling R18).
- **C-O2-10:** every send went from a warm conversation of the phone, re-judged at `judged_at` (ruling R18). FAIL
  when the conversation its row records (`conversation_id`, as step 4 last re-pointed it), still present, holds no
  inbound from the phone stored (`created_at`) at or before `judged_at` whose `sent_at` is within the offer's
  `warm_days` before it. Counted and printed, never FAIL: a send where another conversation of the phone, on a
  channel that maps today to another handset, holds a later inbound so stored (by `sent_at`, ties as §H.4.8
  breaks them), because which channels mapped to a handset when the send was judged is not recorded with it; an
  inbound stored after `judged_at`; a conversation since deleted whole (live `tools/wa_prune_history.php:89-90`);
  and an erased row (NULL phone).
- **C-O2-11:** the STOP rate per offer, and whether the auto-pause fired. Above the threshold it prints `STOP RATE ABOVE <n>%` in capitals.
- **C-O2-12 (S2-08, R-06):** one customer-proactive message per phone per Kampala day, judged on claims only, as
  Part F's Q3-ON judges it (Part F §H.2.12.5; ruling R18). An offer row is paired with the other
  customer-proactive rows (`quote`, `enquiry`, `reminder`, `winback`) in `wa_auto_sends` with the same phone and
  Kampala day, by each row's `claimed_at`. Only rows whose outcome is not `not_sent` are paired, in `id` order,
  exactly as the ledger's step 8a pairs them (Part F §H.2.5.3 step 8), each judged by what its claim could read.
  FAIL is only what a claim could have refused, and Part F's claim refuses both ways: an offer claim with such a
  row of a lower `id`, and a `quote` or `enquiry` claim (mode `claim`) with an offer row of a lower `id`. Every
  row recorded (mode `record`) with a higher `id` than the offer's claim, a `reminder`, a `winback` or an
  `enquiry`, is counted and printed, never FAIL: a record is never deferred (C3), and Part F's enquiry pass
  records rather than claims whenever neither the chase nor offers is on (Part F §H.2.6.4), so once the offers
  steps are off it may legitimately send to a phone offered that morning. A failed send, stored
  `not_sent` (Part F §H.2.5.5), pairs with nothing: a reminder that failed at 09:00 leaves the phone to a 10:30
  offer, and an offer settled `not_sent` after a transient refusal leaves it to a later chase. A lower-`id` row
  now `not_sent` whose `settled_at` is after the higher row's `claimed_at`, so in flight when that claim was
  judged, is counted and printed, never FAIL. Both reads go through the ledger's phone column, which the ledger
  itself stores in the one form (ruling R2). NULL phones (erased, or recorded when the number could not be read,
  ruling R2) are never paired.

**`off offers-live`** and **`off offers-test`** refuse nothing beyond the tool's own uid and tenant refusals once
`<data>/plugin.sqlite3` exists; without it, the tool refuses and saves nothing (ruling R13). Each runs the ladder's
off-cascade with P6's hook, on the tool's `$rw`; if the hook throws, its keys stay set, and the tool prints
`FAIL off_hook <step>`, clears nothing further and exits non-zero (Part F §H.2.12.4).
**`show`** prints the two switches, `offers_live_since`, the settings, the live offer's id and its counts,
reading the book through the tool's `$ro` (ruling R13).

#### H.4.7 The admin screen and its actions

**The tab, `tabs/engage/wa_offers.php`:**
- It is routed as `?page=dashboard&tab=wa_offers`, `'*admin'` (`public.php:2817` onwards), and it guards itself too.
- With `OfferSwitch::screen()` false it prints one card, *"Offers are not switched on here."*, reads nothing and draws no form.
- `includes/navigation.php` draws its entry inside the admin block (`:471`), after "Customer Follow-ups", only when `OfferSwitch::screen()`:

```php
<?php /* 5.18.104 P6 (root docs/72 §H.4): offers, Uganda only, while offers_test_enabled is on */
require_once dirname(__DIR__) . '/lib/OfferSwitch.php';
if (OfferSwitch::screen(is_array($config ?? null) ? $config : [], isset($dataDir) ? (string)$dataDir : null)): ?>
<a href="?page=dashboard&tab=wa_offers" class="kyc-tab <?= $tab==='wa_offers'?'active':'' ?>">
    <span class="nav-icon"><i class="bi bi-megaphone" style="color:#7C3AED;"></i></span> WhatsApp offers
</a>
<?php endif; ?>
```

**What the screen shows.** Every string goes through `h()`, and no phone number, customer name or customer's message body appears anywhere.

1. **Status:**
   - test mode (`offers-test`) or live (`offers-live`);
   - the live offer and its state;
   - settings out of range;
   - any precondition the sender is refusing on, as a fixed code: `reminders_pending` reads *"waiting for today's payment reminders to go first"*, and `partf_missing` reads *"a part this needs is missing"*.
2. **Compose** (a draft only):
   - a title;
   - wording 1, wording 2 and an optional wording 3, each with a character counter (20–900);
   - the fixed line shown read-only beneath: *"Reply STOP to stop these messages. (added automatically)"*;
   - an optional image (jpg, png or webp, at most 4 MB);
   - the audience size: 100, 200 or all.

   Save keeps the draft. **Saving changes `content_hash`, so tests of the old content no longer count.**
3. **Preview** (`&offer=<id>&preview=1`, read-only, `OfferAudience::build()` given the screen's PDO and its own
   store's `retailers.json` rows and `kyc_config.json`, §H.4.8):
   - each wording exactly as it will go (`OfferText::render()`), under the image thumbnail (`OfferImage::thumbnailDataUri()`);
   - the eligible audience by handset, labelled by the number's name as staff see it (`ChannelContext::displayName()`, or the department). Support and accounts are shown as one handset where they share an instance;
   - those left out, by reason (counts only);
   - the count that would be queued, min(size, eligible);
   - an estimate: "at least ⌈n ÷ ceiling⌉ sending days per number. Quote reminders come first and offers start each day after the payment reminders, so it can take longer. Sundays do not count."
4. **Test** (a draft only): per wording, a *Send to my phone* button with a number select. The select lists the handsets the audience uses, sales first. It shows each test's state, its echo, and its reason if it failed. It says *"to your account's phone"*, and never prints the number.
   It also shows whether the ledger recorded each test: one sent but not recorded (`error`) does not count for
   Start, and the screen asks for that wording to be tested again (§H.4.6 C-O1-1; Q17-O01).
5. **Start** (`offers-live` on, and every wording tested on the current content): a confirmation with the counts as they stand. **Pause**, **Resume** (`offers-live` on), **Stop** (with a confirmation) and **Discard** (a draft).
   A wording counts as tested by a test sent and recorded in the ledger, as C-O1-1 counts it (§H.4.6; Q17-O01).
