**H.5.8.2 `webhook.php` — `whQuotationEmail` only, and why C9 allows it**

**Why this file must change.** Path 3 is the plugin's only quotation e-mail for every KYC quote and for every quote typed in uCRM. It also composes app quotes whenever the webhook wins the `QEMAIL` claim, or whenever path 1 is off. The agent can be resolved only where the store, the configuration, the quote id, the client id and the quote entity are all in hand together, and that is `whQuotationEmail` (`:242-245`).
- **The dispatcher holds a PDO, not a store.** A store can be had only from `SqliteStore::create`: the constructor is private (`lib/SqliteStore.php:130`), and `create` runs the migration runner and the seeder (`:231-265`), on every e-mail.
- **Reading `retailers.json`, `kyc_applications.json` and P7's two collections straight through that PDO would duplicate `SqliteStore`'s table logic:** blob or column tables (`isProperTable`, `:1138-1156`) and `findAll`'s two query forms (`:579-615`). Two implementations of one store can drift.

That is the reason (IP-5), not impossibility. Without these two hunks D16 could not be met for KYC quotes, the main way agents quote on Uganda, and the copy on app quotes would depend on which side won the claim.

**The quote send itself is not altered:** the call `$r = $d->send('quotation', … ], (string)$quoteId, $atts);` (`:285-293`) and every line around it keep their bytes. #### H.5.9 Records: what is written, and what is not

| Record | What P7 does |
|---|---|
| `quote_agent_copies` (store collection `quote_agent_copies.json`) | **One row per quotation e-mail a path composes while P7 is on**, or that the webhook path set out to compose (`not_composed`), added or skipped, with its eleven fields (§H.5.7): ids, the quote's number, fixed codes and `decided_at`, the moment P7 decided. `rcpt` is `accepted`, `refused`, `none` or `excluded` (the dispatcher's floor dropped the copy). **No address, no name, no phone.** It is the evidence AC-ON counts, and the earliest row of a quote fixes its resolution (P-D16) |
| `quote_agent_makers` (store collection `quote_agent_makers.json`) | The hand-off rows: client id, maker's account id, quote id, state, epoch times |
| `customer_email_log` (created in code, `lib/CustomerEmailDispatcher.php:478-508`) | **Unchanged.** Same row, schema and recipient as 5.18.103 (the customer's address, as today). No column is added: the table is shared with South Sudan, and its additive `ALTER` (`:501`) would reach both countries. AC-ON pairs P7's decisions with its rows by the key `quotation:<id>` (§H.5.10.4) |
| `quote_mail.log` (`lib/QuotationService.php:1426-1427`) | **Unchanged**, byte for byte. Its line already carries the customer's address (pre-existing, OB3); P7 adds nothing to it, so no agent address ever enters it |
| `whLog` (the webhook log) | **Unchanged.** P7 adds no line |
| The PHP error log | **Unchanged.** P7 calls `error_log` nowhere, and on South Sudan its code is not loaded (§H.5.16 compares the log) |
| `PluginLog` | Only a failed P7 write: `quote_agent_copy: <what> not written (<exception class>)`. `PluginLog::mask` would also mask any address (`lib/PluginLog.php:47-48`), but none is ever passed to it |
| MailService's returned log | Holds `cc <address>` (`lib/MailService.php:481-483`). P7 compares it in memory (`rcptOutcome`) and keeps only `accepted`, `refused` or `none` |
| The dispatcher's result | Gains `agent_rcpt` and, when the floor dropped the copy, `agent_code` — fixed values only, read by the webhook hunk and never logged |
| The deploy log | Counts and fixed codes only (§H.5.14) |

**Retention and erasure.** The rows hold no phone, so Part F's `erase` has nothing to reach there. They are not pruned. They are a few bytes per quotation e-mail.

#### H.5.10 The switch: an optional row 1b of the one ladder, and its check AC-ON

**H.5.10.1 The row** (in `SalesFollowupLadder::STEPS`, in Part F's columns)

| # | Step | Part | Writes: switch keys; record keys | Needs | Own precondition | Check | `off` also clears | Off-hook (placement) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1b (optional) | `agent-cc` | P (P7) | `quote_agent_cc_enabled=1`, `quote_agent_cc_since=<UTC now>` | **none** — the order asks only that step 1 has run (§H.5.10.2) | plugin mail configured, **judged from `email_settings.json` alone** (`QuoteAgentCopy::preconditions()`, in ruling R13's precondition shape, the one mapping of `QuoteAgentCopy::mailSetting()`; §H.5.7; A11-07): `smtp_host` set, or `use_ucrm_email` on (printed "uCRM's mailer, not asked"). Never `MailService::getConfig()`, which would ask uCRM | **AC-ON** | — | **none**; its keys are cleared in ruling R7's last phase, with the record keys (ruling R11; IP-3) |

**The setting** (in the ladder's one settings table, ruling R5):

| Key | Alias | Type | Default and range | Part |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `quote_agent_cc_admins` | `agent-cc-admins` | int | **1** (0–1); absent reads as 1. Whether an administrator who makes a quote is copied: D16's reading is yes, and `0` is the owner's narrowing (PQ1). Any stored value other than `1` reads as `0`, the narrower reading | P |

- `allKeys()` gains `quote_agent_cc_enabled` and `quote_agent_cc_since`. `settingKeys()` gains `quote_agent_cc_admins`, which is never cleared by `off` and never NO-GO.
- `preexistingKeys()` gains the keys P7 reads and never writes. Each is shown with where it is read:
  - `quote_email_via_plugin`, `use_ucrm_email`, `smtp_host`, `smtp_from`, `smtp_user`: the `email_settings.json` keys `mailSetting`, AC-ON and AC-N1 read;
  - `sent_copy_enabled`: AC-CA2's refusal reads it;
  - `kyc_quote_send_via_crm`: printed by `on`, AC-ON and AC-N1;
  - `kyc_auto_quote_enabled`: read by `state()` and `forWebhook`.

  P7 reads the other existing switches — `email_cc_contacts`, `customer_emails_enabled`, `customer_email_quotation` — only through `CustomerEmailDispatcher::ccEnabled()` and `::enabled()`, never as literals.
- TL14 therefore finds every key in P7's files declared (IP-4).

**H.5.10.2 Its place in the order — what the ladder engine does with row 1b** (ruling R11; IP-2)

1. `on agent-cc` applies the tool's rules 1–5 (Part F §H.2.12.3) as for every row: Uganda, and the uid that owns the data folder; **order** — step 1, the report, has run (`sf_report_ran_at` set; it is the only lower row, and it cannot be skipped); no earlier FAIL left running; Needs — none; and the row's own precondition.
2. **For every later step it is optional:** rule 2 passes it whether it is on or off, as it passes step 10. No row's Needs names it, so it is never a Need, and no step waits for it.
3. **Rule 3 applies to it unchanged.** While `agent-cc` is on and AC-ON reads `FAIL <code>`, `on` of any later step is refused until `off agent-cc`; a step already on is not affected. AC-ON's window starts at `quote_agent_cc_since` (§H.5.10.4), so its FAIL does not clear by itself; a later `on agent-cc` writes a new since-stamp and is judged from it. This is the row's one cost.
   **Ruling R18 bounds it:** no AC-ON FAIL rests on what P7 could not have known. A send that failed while carrying
   a copy, and plugin mail switched off since, are printed (§H.5.10.4 rules 2 and 7), so a FAIL left here is about
   P7's own records: a missing decision, a malformed one, or an unreadable since-stamp.
4. `skip agent-cc` is refused: "optional: the order passes it while it is off". Nothing waits for it.
5. `off` of any other step, and its cascades, never reach P7: no row's "`off` also clears" names it. `off sending` does not clear it, because it is not a WhatsApp send. `off agent-cc` clears its two keys and nothing else.
6. `--check` with no step judges the highest step that is on, as for every row, so it judges AC-ON only while steps 1
   and 1b are the only steps on. `--check agent-cc` judges AC-ON; while it is off it prints `OFF — not judged` and
   judges nothing, the one form Parts V and O print for a step that is off (V §H.3.25 `--after-only`; O §H.4.18). The
   no-argument output stays one line (ruling R11), so TL17's unknown-status guard reads it unchanged.
7. `show` prints it in its place in the ladder, as "1b agent-cc (optional, P7)".

**H.5.10.3 What `on`, `off` and `show` print** (counts only)

- **`on agent-cc`:**
  - "From now on, when the plugin e-mails a quotation, the account that made it is copied, visibly, in the same e-mail. uCRM's own quotation e-mails are not changed."
  - the states of `quote_email_via_plugin`, of the master switch with `customer_email_quotation`, of `email_cc_contacts`, and of `kyc_quote_send_via_crm`. With `kyc_quote_send_via_crm` at `0` it adds: "for KYC quotes the plugin's e-mail is the only quotation e-mail; one that fails is lost, and AC-ON says so";
  - how plugin mail is configured: the one line of the row's own precondition, `preconditions()` (§H.5.7),
    "plugin mail: plugin SMTP" or "plugin mail: uCRM's mailer, not asked";
  - the pure `accountCounts(array $retailers, array $company)`: the tool reads the `retailers.json` row through `$ro`,
    its read-only connection (`PRAGMA query_only=ON`), never `SqliteStore::create`, which runs the migrations
    (`lib/SqliteStore.php:231-265`), and passes the rows (ruling R13). It gives: active accounts with a usable
    address; active accounts without one; administrators, copied unless `set agent-cc-admins 0`; and active accounts
    whose address is the company's Reply-To or the sender read from `email_settings.json`, which the customer will see
    in `Cc` (PQ4).
  - **When both quotation paths are off:** "no plugin quotation e-mail is on — the copy will have nothing to ride on". This is printed, not refused; AC-ON then reads `NOT_YET no_traffic`.
  - Refused, saving nothing, when `preconditions()` answers `ok` false with code `mail_not_configured`: it prints
    that answer's one line, "plugin mail is not configured (Settings → System → Email)", or, for a file that
    cannot be read, "plugin mail is not configured (email_settings.json cannot be read)".
  - **It reads itself back.** After writing, it reads `QuoteAgentCopy::state()` through `PluginConfig::read`. If the gate still reads off, it prints `FAIL gate_reads_off`, unsets the two keys it wrote and saves nothing else.
- **`off agent-cc`** — alone, in `off all`, and in the rollback:
  - It unsets both keys, removing them from the overrides file and the store row; it never writes `0` (ruling R5).
  - **It reads the gate back the same way.** If `state()['on']` is still true, a key outside the overrides file is holding P7 on (`data/config.json` or `<data>/config.json`, `lib/PluginConfig.php:82-90`, `:322`). It prints `FAIL key_outside_overrides`, naming the file and never the value, and the rollback's final assertion fails with it.
  - Otherwise it prints "quotation e-mails are as 5.18.103 from the next one".
- **`show`:** `1b agent-cc (optional, P7): on since <date> | off; administrators: included | excluded`, the two quotation paths' states, and `kyc_quote_send_via_crm`.

**H.5.10.4 AC-ON** (`QuoteAgentCopy::check`; read-only; vocabulary `PASS`, `FAIL <code>`, `NOT_YET too_soon|no_traffic`, ruling R6)

How it reads:
- `QuoteAgentCopy::check(\PDO $ro, string $pluginRoot, string $dataDir, int $now)` is unchanged (§H.5.7), and its
  first parameter is the tool's `$ro`, the read-only connection (Part F §H.2.12.1; ruling R13). It reads the book
  through `$ro` alone and opens no connection of its own. The row's own precondition,
  `preconditions(string $dataDir)`, reads `email_settings.json` through `mailSetting()`, never the book (§H.5.7;
  A11-07), and P7 has no hook (ruling R11).
- Before reading any table it checks that the table exists in `sqlite_master`, never through `SqliteStore::load`, which would create a missing table (`lib/SqliteStore.php:1106-1132`).
- It reads `quote_mail.log` line by line, keeps of a sent line only its stamp and the quote's number (rule 4), and
  prints none of it.
- It writes nothing: the tool asserts `total_changes()==0` on `$ro` at its end (ruling R13; Part F §H.2.12.1), and the
  check does not repeat it. Test G1's "`total_changes()` unchanged after the check" is the test's own observation.

**How it judges a past copy (ruling R18).** A decision is P7's act. Its row is written once the send returns
(§H.5.8), and records `decided_at`, the moment P7 decided, taken by `forActor` or `forWebhook` before the send
(§H.5.7): AC-ON places each decision by it, never by when its row was written (ruling R18, its first point).
AC-ON judges each decision only by what that row recorded: its `decided_at`, `number`, `path`, `outcome`, `code`,
`source`, `rule`, `agent_id`, `send_ok` and `rcpt` (§H.5.7 `record`). It never re-reads `retailers.json`,
`quote_agent_cc_admins` or `email_settings.json` to judge one, and never runs `decide()` again: a decision's code is
its verdict under the limits it applied. So `set agent-cc-admins 0`, or an account deactivated, re-addressed or made
an administrator, after its copy was `added`, changes no past verdict. The row records neither the setting nor the
account's state, and no clause needs either; a clause that did would need it recorded on the row first. What P7
could not have known is printed, never a FAIL: a count of the sends that failed while carrying a copy (rule 7),
and plugin mail as it reads now, a note (rule 2). Each such clause has its case in `quote_agent_copy G` (G7–G10), with a
weakened copy that judges by the current state and is caught (PW60, PW61, PW71–PW73; §H.5.12). One copy's own two
stamps can also lie on either side of the window's edge: its decision before, its log line or `customer_email_log`
row after. Rule 6 takes decisions from `since` on and pairs path 1 by quote number, so that copy reads PASS
(`quote_agent_copy G11`), and its weakened copies, which pair by count or window the decisions, are caught
(PW74–PW79).

1. `quote_agent_cc_since` does not parse as a UTC stamp → **FAIL `since_unreadable`**.
2. **Plugin mail as it reads now is a printed note, never a status** (ruling R18). An administrator may switch
   plugin mail off at any time on Settings → System → Email, which writes `use_ucrm_email` and `smtp_host` (live
   `tabs/admin/settings.php:308,311`, saved through `lib/EmailSettingsWriter.php:35-36`), and the copies already
   decided stay correct. AC-ON prints the one line of the row's own precondition, `preconditions()` (§H.5.7), such
   as "plugin mail is not configured (Settings → System → Email)", and the status comes from the other rules: with
   no e-mail and no decision it reads `NOT_YET no_traffic`, as with both quotation paths off (§H.5.10.3). uCRM is
   never asked; a `use_ucrm_email` install prints "plugin mail: uCRM's mailer, not asked". `mail_not_configured`
   is only `on agent-cc`'s refusal.
3. **The window** is `[since + 300 s, now − 300 s]`. If it is empty → **NOT_YET too_soon**. An e-mail is placed in
   it by its own stamp (a log line's, a row's `created_at`), a decision by its `decided_at`, never by when its row
   was written (ruling R18).
4. In the window:
   - *e-mails sent by path 1:* the `quote_mail.log` lines `[<UTC>] <number> -> <address> sent`, whose stamp is
     `gmdate` (`:1426-1427`). They carry the quote's number, not its id. AC-ON keeps of each only its stamp and the
     number, the text between `] ` and the first ` -> `;
   - *e-mails sent by path 3:* the `customer_email_log` rows with `template='quotation'` and `status='sent'`, keyed `quotation:<id>` (`created_at` in UTC);
   - *decisions:* `quote_agent_copies` rows by path, placed by their `decided_at`, with their `number`, `send_ok`,
     `outcome` and `rcpt`.
5. No e-mail and no decision → **NOT_YET no_traffic**.
6. **The positive control on the hooks, paired:**
   - *path 3, by quote id:* every `quotation:<id>` sent row in the window must have a decision of path `webhook`,
     `send_ok=1`, for that `<id>`, with `decided_at` at or after `since`. One without → **FAIL `decision_missing`**;
   - *path 1, by quote number,* because the log line names the quote's number, not its id, and the decision row
     records the same `$number` (§H.5.7 `record`): for each number, the sent lines in the window must be no more
     than that number's path-1 decisions at `send_ok=1` with `decided_at` at or after `since`. More →
     **FAIL `decision_missing`**;
   - **On both paths only the e-mails are windowed** (ruling R18). One copy's line is stamped after the whole SMTP
     session and after `record()`'s write, which may wait up to `busy_timeout`, 5000 ms (`lib/SqliteStore.php:158`,
     `:716`), and its path-3 row is claimed after the decision, so a correct copy decided before `since + 300 s` can
     have its line or row inside the window. Taking decisions from `since` on pairs it. Pairing by count, with both
     windowed, would read it as a missed hook, and for good: the window's lower edge never moves, and rule 3 then
     refuses every later `on` until `off agent-cc` (`quote_agent_copy G11`).
7. **A copy that rode on a failed send is a printed count, never a status** (ruling R18; §H.5.4.6). Each `added`
   decision with `send_ok=0` in the window counts as "failed carrying a copy", per path and split by `rcpt`:
   - `none`: the send failed before the agent's `RCPT` was sent — before the session (`lib/MailService.php:343-352`),
     at the connection (`:397-401`), from the greeting through `MAIL FROM` (`:424-456`) or at the customer's own
     `RCPT TO` (`:459`), all before the `Cc` `RCPT`s (`:461-485`) — so the copy had no part in it;
   - `accepted` or `refused`: the row records no failing step, so nothing says whether the copy caused it
     (`quote_agent_copy E5`, `quote_agent_copy E6`).

   The count carries its path's line: on path 1 "handed to uCRM's `/send`", which still delivered the e-mail
   (`lib/QuotationService.php:1421-1424`, `:794-797`); on path 3 "a lost e-mail: resend with
   `tools/quote_email_send.php`" (`webhook.php:296-303`; the dispatcher answers sent=false,
   `lib/CustomerEmailDispatcher.php:285-287`). A FAIL here would not clear by itself: the window starts at `since`
   (§H.5.10.2 item 3), and the resend writes no decision. A FAIL that blames the copy would first need the decision
   row to record the failing step, content-free; P7 records none, so this clause is a note.
8. An `added` row with no `agent_id` above 0, or with a source that names no agent (`in_flight`, `none`) or lies
   outside `SOURCES` → **FAIL `added_without_agent`**. It reads the row alone, never the agent's `retailers.json`
   row or `quote_agent_cc_admins` as they read now (ruling R18).
9. A code, path, source, rule or `rcpt` outside its fixed list, or a `decided_at` that does not parse as a UTC
   stamp → **FAIL `unknown_code`**. A `decided_at` before the window is a stamp like any other
   (`quote_agent_copy G11`).
10. Otherwise **PASS**.

**Printed as counts, never a FAIL**, each with its legitimate source:
- **"forgotten (resend tool)":** a webhook decision at `send_ok=1` whose `quotation:<id>` row is gone. `tools/quote_email_send.php --clear-claim` deletes it on purpose (`:90-96`; `lib/CustomerEmailDispatcher.php:559-565`), and its own send writes no row;
- **"sent again":** a quote id with more than one decision at `send_ok=1`. `--clear-claim`, then the webhook, sends a quote again on purpose. P7 itself makes no send call (tests `quote_agent_copy B3` and `quote_agent_copy C7`);
- **"row not settled":** a webhook decision at `send_ok=1` whose row is not `sent`;
- **"no log line":** per number, path-1 decisions at `send_ok=1` in the window beyond that number's sent lines
  stamped at or after `since`. `quote_mail.log`'s write is silenced with `@` (`:1426`);
- **"failed carrying a copy"** (rule 7), and beside the counts **plugin mail as it reads now**, a note line
  (rule 2): what P7 could not have known when it decided (ruling R18).

A check that fails falsely teaches the operator to ignore it, and P7 relies on this one to show a missed hook.

**It prints, per path:**
- decisions, added, and skipped by code;
- `rcpt` accepted/refused/none/excluded among the composed copies;
- "sent carrying a copy", "failed carrying a copy" split by `rcpt` (rule 7), and "failed without one", each failed
  count with its path's line from rule 7;
- the sources (`first_decision` among them);
- `kyc_quote_send_via_crm`.

**How the copy is proved made:** an `added` row with `send_ok=1` and `rcpt=accepted` means the relay took the agent's `RCPT` in the same session whose `DATA` it accepted — the strongest evidence short of reading a mailbox. The first live copy is also confirmed by the agent seeing it (an owner action, not a check). AC-CA2 (§H.5.14) is the positive control on a copy.

#### H.5.11 No migration

P7 adds no SQL file, and 089–091 are unchanged.

- **Its records are the plugin's ordinary store collections:** created by `SqliteStore` as `id` + `data` tables on the first write, or on the first read through the store (`findAll` runs `ensureTable`, `lib/SqliteStore.php:579-582`, `:1106-1132`), which is how `quotes_log.json`, `kyc_applications.json` and `retailers.json` are kept.
- **No guarantee rests on a constraint:**
  - *one e-mail per claim* rests on the existing `QEMAIL` claim and on P7 making no send call;
  - *no wrong copy*, beyond §H.5.5's recorded limits, rests on the resolution taking positive evidence only and on each quote's first decision;
  - *no address* rests on the eleven declared fields.
- **They are read and written only on Uganda with P7 on**, so South Sudan never gains a table (§H.5.16, proof step 3).
- **If a later release wants them under triggers like Part F's,** they would belong in 089 beside the ledger (C2: 089 holds the shared follow-up records). Nothing in 5.18.104 needs that.

#### H.5.12 Tests, and a weakened copy for every guard

**The file is `tests/test_quote_agent_copy.php`**, with its sections in `tests/quote_agent_copy/` and cited by file and letter (`quote_agent_copy A`), as ruling R10 asks.
- It uses the fakes of `tests/test_mail_quote.php` (`FakeCrm`, the recording mailer, the `TestQuoteSvc` seam over `newMailService()`), a real `SqliteStore` per case, and two relays:
  - `tests/fixtures/fake_smtp_server.php` (unchanged), which accepts everything and writes a transcript of `MAIL FROM`, every `RCPT TO` and the message;
  - the new `tests/fixtures/fake_smtp_refuse.php`.
- No fixture address belongs to a real person: every address is under a reserved test domain.
- **The fault-injection stubs** (`quote_agent_copy B7`, `quote_agent_copy C12` and `quote_agent_copy D7`) are `QuoteAgentCopy` classes loaded in place of the real file, with the key set on and the profile Uganda: one whose every public method throws, and, for each public method in turn, one in which only that method throws and the others behave as the real class. A call site is reached only when the calls before it succeed (`markResult` only after `markMaking` returned an id), so only the per-method stubs reach every call site.
- Each weakened copy is built from an anchor that occurs exactly once, in the `sj_weakened_copy` style. A control run on the real tree trips none of them, and **the build runs every copy**.

The log holds counts and fixed codes only, never an address or an id. P7's keys are covered at stage A by

- **AC-N2 — what the copy would have covered, over 30 days (UTC).** Plugin quotation e-mails by path: `quote_mail.log` "sent" lines, and `customer_email_log` quotation rows by status. For path 3's sent rows (key `quotation:<id>`), the quote id as today's records know it:
  - held by a KYC application;
  - held by a `quotes_log` row as `crm_quote_id`, or by a lead;
  - held by none (typed in uCRM, or never recorded).

  This is an upper bound: at send time the race of §H.5.5 narrows it.

**After the copy:**

- **AC-CA1:**
  - the installed `QuoteAgentCopy::on()` is false on the live configuration; true on a copy with the key set; false on that copy with the profile forced to South Sudan;
  - on a first deploy the live book holds no `quote_agent_makers` or `quote_agent_copies` table; on a redeploy their row counts are printed, and nothing is read from them.
- **AC-CA2 — positive and negative controls on a copy,** through the installed code, with uCRM the pin's recording fake (`tests/test_mail_quote.php`'s). **Before anything runs, the harness makes the copy unable to reach a live system** (P7S-02):
  1. it writes a **fresh** `email_settings.json` in the copy's data folder holding only `use_ucrm_email` false, `sent_copy_enabled` false, `smtp_host` `127.0.0.1` and the port of the pin's `tests/fixtures/fake_smtp_server.php`. Nothing of the copied file survives: with `use_ucrm_email` on, `getConfig()` would GET the live uCRM's `/settings` and send through the live relay (`lib/MailService.php:155,179-200`), and with `sent_copy_enabled` on every send would file the raw message into the live mailbox over IMAP (`:506`, `:515-533`). Precedents: `tests/fixtures/notify_harness.php:111-113`, `tests/fixtures/staff_jobs_sandbox.php:293-294`;

It asserts that no connection left the host except to loopback;

  6. the key set and the profile forced to South Sudan → equal to 5.18.103's, and no table.

#### H.5.15 Rollback (C4)

- **No off-hook.** P7 keeps no work in flight: each quotation e-mail reads the switch when it is composed. One composed while `off` runs carries the copy or not, and is still one e-mail.
- **P7's place in the one sequence (ruling R11; IP-3):** ruling R7's sequence, extended at its end only, with P7's two
  keys cleared in its last phase, **together with the record keys**: O (12, 11) → F (10, 6) → V (9, 8, 7, 5) → 4, 3 → 2
  (P5's keys, then the ledger last) → the record keys and Part P's two keys (`quote_agent_cc_enabled`,
  `quote_agent_cc_since`), last. The only cost is that copies keep riding on quotation e-mails for the seconds the
  rollback takes, which is harmless: each is still one e-mail. Ruling R11 declines A-R7-1, which would have cleared P7
  first.
- **QF-RB1's last assertion** — no key in `allKeys()` set, in the files or the store row — covers P7's two keys. It is joined by the read-back of §H.5.10.3: `QuoteAgentCopy::state()['on'] === false` through `PluginConfig::read`, so a key left in either `config.json` fails the rollback with `FAIL key_outside_overrides` instead of passing it. The by-hand put-back list in the rollback output names both keys.
- **After the put-back,** 5.18.103's code has no P7: no copy, no hand-off. The two collections stay, and nothing reads them.
- **A redeploy starts dark** (QF-G4), and P7 is switched on again with `on agent-cc` and judged by AC-ON.

#### H.5.16 South Sudan unchanged, and how that is proved

**Mechanism:**

- **The tool** refuses there, so P7's keys are never set by it.
- **P7's code is never loaded on South Sudan.** Every hunk asks `StaffJobsGate::applies()` before any `require` of `QuoteAgentCopy` (§H.5.8): both `QuotationService` hunks and the webhook's. `StaffJobsGate` is false on South Sudan and on any doubt (`lib/StaffJobsGate.php:18-35`). So:
  - a fault in `lib/QuoteAgentCopy.php` — a construct newer than the server's PHP, or a file missing from a partial copy — cannot reach South Sudan's quoting, and AC-L1 lints it before the copy;
  - `QuoteAgentCopy::state()`, and with it `PluginConfig::read` and `ConfigVault::fill`, whose failure is an `error_log` line (`lib/ConfigVault.php:186`), never runs there;
  - `createCrmQuote` writes no hand-off, `emailQuotePdf`'s header is 5.18.103's, and `record()` is never called.
- **`QuoteAgentCopy::state()`** is false there in any case, whatever is stored: the second lock.
- **The dispatcher hunks** act only after `agentCopy()` was called, which only the webhook hunk does. `send()`'s signature, `sendReminderDue()` and `sendInstallAuth()` are unchanged.
- **No migration;** P7's collections are created only by P7's own reads and writes, which happen only on Uganda with P7 on.
- **Byte for byte:** `MailService`, `EmailRecipients`, `CustomerEmails`, `EmailTemplate` and `QuotePdfSource`.

**Proof (`quote_agent_copy H`):**

1. On a South Sudan fixture book, from `221c9dc` (Git archive) and from the 5.18.104 tree, run each of these:
   - `createCrmQuote` with `quote_email_via_plugin` on;
   - `whQuotationEmail` with the quotation switch on;
   - the dispatcher's `send()` for every catalogue key;
   - `sendReminderDue`;
   - `sendInstallAuth`.

   Each run goes to `fake_smtp_server.php` and the fake uCRM. The following must be identical between the two trees:
   - the relay transcripts: `MAIL FROM`, every `RCPT TO`, and the message, with `Date`, `Message-ID` and MIME boundaries masked;
   - the uCRM requests;
   - `quote_mail.log` and `customer_email_log`;
   - the webhook log;
   - **the PHP error log** (`error_log` pointed at a file per run);
   - the return values.
2. The same with P7's three keys written **ON** directly into South Sudan's configuration — the tool refuses, so they are written by hand — proving that the gate stops it, not the switch.
3. After 1 and 2:
   - `sqlite_master` holds no `quote_agent_makers` or `quote_agent_copies`;
   - `class_exists('QuoteAgentCopy', false)` is false in each run's process.
4. A Uganda book with P7 off is identical to `221c9dc` in the same way, error log included (P7 off = 5.18.103).
5. PW1, PW30 and PW57 fail 1–3.

**At the deploy:** AC-L1 lints before the copy. AC-CA1 and AC-CA2 (case 6) force the profile to South Sudan on a copy. The deploy runs on the Uganda server only.

#### H.5.17 What the other parts must match (the interface, IP-n)

- **IP-1 — one KYC agent rule.** Part F's pure `lib/QuoteSendEvidence.php` exposes its owner rule 1 as `QuoteSendEvidence::kycAgent(array $application, array $retailerRows): array` returning `['id' => ?int, 'source' => 'kyc_sales_person'|'kyc_submitter'|'none']`:
  - `sales_person` naming exactly one active account (exact, case-insensitive, trimmed), else an active `retailer_id`;
  - F's rules 1 and 6 call it, and so does P7;
  - `quote_followup C` and `quote_agent_copy A7` share its fixtures, and `quote_agent_copy C2` reads its expected results from them.

  Part F §H.2.9.4 states the two-match case: two or more active accounts named by `sales_person` give no owner from the
  name, and `kycAgent()` then takes an active `retailer_id` (`kyc_submitter`). `quote_followup C` declares that fixture,
  and `quote_agent_copy A7` and `C2` read it.
- **IP-2 — P7's row in the one table: the optional row 1b (ruling R11).**
  - **Part F's `SalesFollowupLadder::STEPS` (§H.2.12.2) carries the row of §H.5.10.1**, marked optional, in the table's
    order after step 1 and before step 2, with Needs none and `skip` refused. C6's twelve steps keep their numbers,
    order and Needs, and the `lib/SalesFollowupLadder.php` row of F's file list (§H.2.3) names the extra row: "C6's
    twelve and Part P's optional row 1b".
  - **§H.2.12.3 rule 2 names it beside step 10:** "every lower-numbered step is on, skipped, or optional (steps 1b and 10)". Rules 1, 3, 4 and 5 apply to it unchanged, so a P7 FAIL holds back every later `on` until `off agent-cc` (§H.5.10.2). No row's Needs or "`off` also clears" names it.
  - **Shared output is unchanged:** `--check` with no step prints one line, the highest step that is on, and TL17's
    unknown-status guard reads it as it reads any row. `--check agent-cc` while off prints `OFF — not judged`, the form
    Parts V and O print. `show` lists it in its place.
  - TL1, TL2, TL15 and TL16 are Part F's weakened copies of the shared rules; P7's own proof that those rules reach row 1b is `quote_agent_copy F1`, `quote_agent_copy F2` and `quote_agent_copy F3`.
  - **C1 and ruling R6 bind it as written, and ruling R11 places it; C6's list as written does not name it.** So the row
    is written once in Part F's §H.2.12.2 and §H.2.12.3, and Parts V and O, wherever they restate the order, state the
    same words: ruling R11 binds every part to this one form.
  - **Ruling R11 declines amendment A-C6-1**, the independent row proposed in round 2, and makes row 1b the design.
    Round 1's claim that the independent row was the coordinator's instruction stays withdrawn.
- **IP-3 — P7's place in the rollback sequence: ruling R7's last phase (ruling R11).**
  - **The sequence:** O (12, 11) → F (10, 6) → V (9, 8, 7, 5) → 4, 3 → 2 (P5's keys, then the ledger last) → the
    record keys and Part P's two keys (`quote_agent_cc_enabled`, `quote_agent_cc_since`), last. P7 has no hook, and

#### H.5.18 Observed in passing: recorded, not changed by this part

Labelled OB1–OB5, so that none collides with C6's step ids (ruling R10).

- **OB1** With `quote_email_via_plugin` on, when the webhook wins the `QEMAIL` claim for an app quote, `emailQuotePdf` returns "already sent" (`lib/QuotationService.php:1374-1376`). `createCrmQuote` then calls uCRM's `/send` (`:794-797`), and the customer gets the plugin's e-mail and uCRM's.
- **OB2** With `quote_email_via_plugin` off and the quotation switch on, an app quote is sent by uCRM's `/send` (`:794-797`) and by the webhook (`webhook.php:2884-2886`): two e-mails. This is the `docs/45` D2a pattern.
- **OB3** `quote_mail.log` writes the customer's address in clear (`lib/QuotationService.php:1426-1427`).
- **OB4** `tools/quote_email_send.php` sends without the client's other contacts, whatever `email_cc_contacts` says (`:184-185`), and writes no `customer_email_log` row for its own send.
- **OB5** The webhook writes `quote_id` into the client's first application (`webhook.php:2896`, `:2915-2918`). For a returning customer, a new quote is recorded on an old application, which also skews Part F's owner rule 1 for that quote. P7 no longer reads it on a later send (§H.5.4.3 step 1); what remains is §H.5.5's recorded limit.
- **OB6** `emailQuotePdf`'s outer `catch` returns without releasing `QEMAIL` (`lib/QuotationService.php:1432-1434`). After any throw there, uCRM's `/send` still delivers, but the webhook can never send that quote. P7's calls cannot reach it (§H.5.8.1).

P7 neither causes nor fixes any of these, and each carries at most one copy per plugin e-mail.

#### H.5.19 Owner questions, coordinator rulings, what is not established, and size

**Owner questions.** Each default below is D16's literal reading (P-D17); every answer is a setting or a small change the build can take before switch-on.

**PQ1 — administrators.** When an administrator's account makes a quote, it gets the copy: D16 names "the agent creating the quote", and an administrator who makes one is that agent. If you would rather administrators were not copied, that is one command: `set agent-cc-admins 0`.

**PQ2 — KYC quotes.** The copy goes to the salesperson the KYC names, when exactly one active account has that name, and otherwise to the account that submitted the KYC — the same rule as the daily list. Confirm, or say "always the submitting account".

**PQ3 — dealer accounts, and "Login As".**
- Accounts of retailers and field agents that make quotes are agents too, and get the copy. Confirm, or limit the copy to DishNet staff.
- When an administrator uses "Login As" to act as another account, a quote made that way is copied to that account, which did not make it in person. Should it get the copy, or should no copy go while an administrator is acting as someone else?
  - "No copy" can be built for quotes made in the app.
  - A KYC submitted that way leaves no record of it, so it would still be copied to that account.

**PQ4 — the address the customer sees.**
- The copy is a visible Cc (D16), so the customer sees the agent's address on the e-mail. Before switching P7 on, check that every selling account's address is one you are content to show customers. `on agent-cc` prints how many accounts have a usable address.
- An account whose address is the company's own mailbox (the Reply-To or the sending address) gets its copy in that mailbox, and the customer sees the company's address in Cc. `on agent-cc` prints how many such accounts there are. Should such accounts get no copy instead?

**PQ5 — the double e-mails OB1 and OB2.** These are already live, and P7 neither causes nor fixes them. Should they be reviewed as their own item in a later release?

**Settled by the coordinator: ruling R11.** It declines the amendments proposed in round 2, A-C6-1 (P7 as an independent
row) and A-R7-1 (P7 cleared first in the rollback), and makes this part's form the design: P7 is the optional row 1b of
the one order, after step 1 and before step 2, with Needs none (IP-2), and its keys are cleared at the end of
ruling R7's sequence, with the record keys, last, with no hook (IP-3). Ruling R11 binds every part to state this one
form: Part F writes it once, in its §H.2.12.2, §H.2.12.3 and §H.2.16, and Parts V and O restate it in the places IP-3
lists. Nothing of ruling R11 is left for the coordinator.

**Left for the coordinator: ruling R13's row P (A11-07).** Its precondition cell is to name
`preconditions(string $dataDir): array`, which answers in ruling R13's precondition shape, in place of
`mailSetting(string $dataDir): array`, which does not (§H.5.7; IP-6).

**Not established** (read-only, no server):

- whether `quote_email_via_plugin` is on on Uganda, and whether the quotation switch is still on — `docs/45` recorded it switched on on 15 Sep (AC-N1 prints both);
- `kyc_quote_send_via_crm` on Uganda, and so whether the webhook's e-mail is the only quotation e-mail for KYC quotes (AC-N1 prints it);
- whether uCRM sends its own e-mail for a quote typed in its screen;
- how often `quote.add` arrives before the plugin's own records, so how many copies come from the in-flight rule (AC-ON prints the sources);
- how DishNet's relay answers an extra `RCPT`, whether it judges recipients at the end of `DATA`, and what header
  length it refuses. `quote_agent_copy E` uses a fake relay; the first live copies show `rcpt`, and AC-ON counts a
  lost webhook e-mail, never as a FAIL (ruling R18);
- how many accounts have a usable address, and how many use the company's mailbox (AC-N1);
- whether uCRM 4.5.33's `quote.add` entity or its GET of a quote returns `adminNotes`. If it does, the in-flight limit of §H.5.5 closes by the plugin's mark; if not, it stands;
- whether the server's `FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL` accepts quoted local parts. PW32 measures it at the build;
- the PHP default zone of `date()` stamps (`submitted_at`, `crm_synced_at`). They are written and read on the same server, so the in-flight comparison is consistent; a stamp that does not parse is "not in flight".

**Size, as an estimate:**
- `lib/QuoteAgentCopy.php`: about 460 lines;
- the three files' hunks: about 75 lines;
- tests: about 1,500 lines, plus the relay fixture's 190;
- the deploy's `AC` checks: about 170 lines.

## S. Status, 9 Nov 2026 — built and tested; NOT deployed

### S.1 The release

- **Built:** `release/5.18.104` = **`994d660`**, one commit on 5.18.103 (`221c9dc`): 260 files, 215 added, 45 changed;
  43,561 insertions, 151 deletions; three migrations, **089, 090 and 091**, each verifying itself. **Pushed 7 Nov on the
  owner's word** (*"push it."*): `origin/release/5.18.104` = `994d660`, after a scan of every added line for keys,
  tokens, phone numbers and e-mail addresses (none real). Any later change to the release is a new commit on top of it.
- **How it was built:** in ten stages (B1–B10), each built, then reviewed by someone who had not built it, then fixed,
  then rechecked: 23 working commits (`abfccb7` … `1845009`, kept locally under `refs/keep/wip/5.18.104`), squashed
  into the release. The release's tree is identical to `1845009`'s, the one the stage runs tested. The development
  branch keeps the release as a patch (`wip/release-5.18.104.patch`, `git diff 221c9dc..994d660`), so a container
  restart cannot lose it.
- **The stages:** B1 the ledger (089) and what every part shares · B2 quote tracking and the chase · B3 the daily list,
  *My quotations* and the report · B4 Part P (the agent's Cc) · B5 Part V's media chain (090) · B6 Part V's replies ·
  B7 Part O's engine (091) · B8 Part O's screen and switch · B9 the switch tool and its one ladder · B10 `cron/master.php`,
  `cron_status`, the boundary, South Sudan, logging and the re-pointed tests. Every stage's review found something and
  every finding was verified against this design and the code before it was fixed; nothing is open.
- **Everything is OFF.** After the deploy no switch is on, no new job runs and no message is sent that 5.18.103 would
  not send. `tools/sales_followup.php` turns each part on in the one order (C6), each step only after the step before it
  has passed its check.
- **Q1 is still unanswered**, so its fallback ships (§Q): while `sf_persona_confirmed` is unset, on a salesperson's own
  number the day-3 chase and the voice-note reply are held and day 7 uses form B. A later answer is one command,
  `set persona-confirmed <date>`.
- **The Privacy Policy paragraph Q7 approved (§H.3.23)** is in the website's source, committed on the development
  branch (`29797c8`), and **not published**. Step 7, `voice-dry-run` (P4's second rung, the first that sends a recording
  to OpenAI), refuses until the publish date is recorded with `set ai_media_voice_privacy_line <date>`, and so does
  `MediaPolicy::voiceEnabled` at run time.

### S.4 The deploy script and its rehearsal

- **`scripts/deploy-5.18.104.sh`** (14,499 lines, sha256 `1aafc15bd1cdb1d7…`), pinned to `994d660`: derived
  from 5.18.103's by asserted edits in eleven parts, 394 edits, every pin, count and sha256 read off Git, each fix
  round derived twice byte for byte. It keeps every 5.18.103 check and places all 78 of this design's deploy codes,
  each in its stage: QF 28 (§H.2.15–§H.2.16), VN and VA 26 (§H.3.25), OF 16 (§H.4.18–§H.4.19), AC 8
  (§H.5.14–§H.5.15). It adds `--clear-switches` (§H.2.15.1) and runs the one rollback sequence, QF-RB1, before any
  put-back, in `--rollback` and in V1's automatic rollback alike. Beside it are two wrappers:
  `scripts/sales-followup.sh` runs the switch tool as the book's owner, and `scripts/sales-followup-report.sh` runs P1
  on a copy.
- **Where the script reads this design its own way.** Each was decided in its stage and reviewed:
  1. `--clear-switches` is refused on a book 5.18.104 never ran on: the pin's tool would migrate the live book before
     the copy. A key held by `data/config.json` or `<data>/config.json` is NO-GO even with the flag, because the tool
     never writes those files.
  2. The clear and the redeploy baseline run after DEPLOY is typed and before the checkout, so a stop leaves the
     checkout where it was.
  3. On a first deploy, any of 090's tables or a voice event is NO-GO, where §H.3.25 exempts only the redeploy; so is
     any `wa_offer*` table, where §H.4.18 says only that none is expected. An unreadable redeploy baseline is NO-GO too.
  4. QF-RB1 also runs before V1's automatic put-back, and its failure stops there as well. After a verified V1,
     QF-RB3 reads the put-back.
  5. AC-CA2 keeps only the copy's book: its configuration is replaced by the check's own and read back before every
     drive. That is stronger than §H.5.14's "blank `evo_api_url` and `evo_api_key`".
  6. 5.18.103's QC-N1 is a note either way, and QC-ON1–QC-ON3 judge the catalogue switch as found: production's has
     been on since 4 Nov, an admin's choice. V3g names, in a note, a key the switch tool removes where this run runs it.
- **Reviews.** DS1–DS4 found 11, 3, 2 and 1 findings, all fixed and rechecked. One of DS1's was a blocker: QF-G2
  would have stopped every redeploy. DS5 audited every text carried from 5.18.103. It confirmed 189 carried lines
  that, one release on, said false things — most naming the wrong release, some mechanism defects of the same kind
